rows.title: Idealized IPC under an N-wide machine
rows.how_to_grade: Learner computes IPC = total_ops / max(critical_path, ops/width) under issue-width + port constraints; rel_err vs reference model. Mac today.

rows.title: Identify reuses in a tiny trace
rows.how_to_grade: Small .npy trace; learner counts accesses that are re-references (address seen before); exact_match vs reference. Mac today.

rows.title: ILP of an attention inner loop: pick unroll+accumulate
rows.how_to_grade: Learner restructures a score inner loop; harness computes modeled critical path which must meet a reference (exact_match on below-reference check + value). Mac today (modeled).

rows.title: Inclusive vs exclusive hierarchy miss counts
rows.how_to_grade: Same trace, two policies (inclusive back-invalidation vs exclusive victim fill). Learner returns the (inclusive_miss, exclusive_miss) pair; exact_match vs reference. Mac today.

rows.title: Insert software prefetch distance to hide latency
rows.how_to_grade: Learner annotates a loop with a prefetch distance; harness models demand misses hidden and remaining modeled misses must be below gate. Mac today.

rows.title: int8 GEMV with SIMD widening equivalence
rows.concept: SIMD / vectorization (NEON on Apple, AVX on x86)
rows.how_to_grade: Learner implements int8*int8->int32 widening GEMV; max_abs_err vs an int reference == 0 (byte-exact accumulation). Mac today (numpy int); native variant later.

rows.title: Interleaved vs first-touch remote accesses
rows.how_to_grade: Learner returns remote-access counts for interleaved vs first-touch placement on the same trace; exact_match on pair. Mac today (modeled).

rows.title: Kahan/pairwise summation accuracy
rows.how_to_grade: Learner implements compensated summation; max_abs_err vs high-precision reference below a tight tol on adversarial fixtures. Mac today.

rows.title: Knee detection in a working-set sweep
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture: modeled staircase array of latency vs working-set-size. Learner runs knee/derivative detection and returns knee indices; exact_match vs reference indices (grades the algorithm, never wall-clock). Mac today.

rows.title: KV record layout optimal for both read paths
rows.how_to_grade: Learner lays out a multi-head KV record so per-head streaming read AND whole-token write are traffic-optimal; harness checks modeled traffic for both paths matches reference (exact_match on chosen layout id + rel_err on bytes). Mac today.

rows.title: Label 5 traces line-efficient vs wasteful
rows.how_to_grade: For each .npy trace, learner computes bytes-used/bytes-fetched and thresholds; exact_match on 5 labels. Mac today.

rows.title: Label stride-1 innermost or not
rows.how_to_grade: Given a loop nest + C-contiguous shape, learner labels whether innermost access is stride-1; exact_match vs reference. Mac today.

rows.title: Large activation write-out: NT vs temporal traffic
rows.how_to_grade: Learner chooses store type for a large activation write; modeled total DRAM traffic (incl. avoided RFO and avoided pollution refetch) must meet reference. Mac today (modeled).

rows.title: Linked list to index-array (byte-exact + MLP up)
rows.how_to_grade: Learner converts pointer traversal to indexable batch; byte_exact result AND modeled MLP above gate. Mac today.

rows.title: Local vs remote access counts
rows.how_to_grade: Given placement + access trace, learner returns (local,remote) counts; exact_match. Mac today (modeled).

rows.title: LogSumExp stability across scales
rows.how_to_grade: Learner implements stable LSE; max_abs_err vs reference below tol over extreme-scale fixtures. Mac today.

rows.title: Loop interchange to a traffic gate
rows.how_to_grade: Learner reorders loops so innermost is stride-1; harness traces and modeled line fetches must be below gate. Mac today.

rows.title: Loop-overhead ops eliminated by unrolling
rows.how_to_grade: Learner computes modeled branch/increment ops saved = (N - N/U) type formula; exact_match on the overhead-op count. Mac today.

rows.title: LRU stack monotonicity over 50 traces
rows.how_to_grade: Learner verifies inclusion property (LRU misses non-increasing in size) via the stack model on 50 random traces and returns count where monotonicity holds; exact_match = 50. Mac today.

rows.title: Max outstanding misses (MLP degree)
rows.how_to_grade: Given a dependency graph over loads, learner returns the max independent in-flight misses (MLP); exact_match vs reference. Mac today.

rows.title: Min accumulators to hide FMA latency
rows.how_to_grade: Given FMA latency L and throughput 1/cycle, learner returns min accumulators = ceil(L*throughput) to saturate the pipe; exact_match. Mac today.

rows.title: Miss-rate curve from a reuse histogram
rows.how_to_grade: From a reuse-distance histogram, learner produces miss-rate vs cache-size curve (MRC = tail-sum) and reads off a queried size; rel_err vs reference < 1e-9. Mac today.

rows.title: Model coherence invalidations for interleaved writes
rows.how_to_grade: Learner implements a simple MSI invalidation counter over an interleaved multi-thread write trace; exact_match on invalidation count vs reference. Mac today.

rows.title: Model runtime = misses/MLP * latency
rows.how_to_grade: Learner computes modeled cycles = (num_misses/MLP)*miss_latency; rel_err vs reference. Mac today.

rows.title: Modeled op-count speedup of vectorized dot
rows.concept: SIMD / vectorization (NEON on Apple, AVX on x86)
rows.how_to_grade: Learner computes modeled op-count ratio scalar/vector = width (adjusted for tail); rel_err vs reference. Mac today.

rows.title: Modulo-scheduling initiation interval (II)
rows.how_to_grade: Learner computes II = max(resource-bound, recurrence-bound) for a loop body; exact_match on II vs reference. Mac today.

rows.title: MoE expert-routing gather min traffic layout
rows.how_to_grade: Learner groups tokens by expert and lays out gathers to minimize modeled DRAM line traffic; must meet reference budget. Mac today (modeled).

rows.title: Multi-level page-walk cost model
rows.how_to_grade: Learner models cycles of a 4-level page walk (with page-table-cache hits); rel_err on modeled walk cycles vs reference. Mac today.

rows.title: N-way set-associative LRU simulator
rows.how_to_grade: Learner builds N-way set-assoc LRU cache; exact_match on miss count vs reference for a trace. Mac today.

rows.title: Naive vs 1-level vs 2-level miss triple
rows.how_to_grade: Same matmul, three schemes; learner returns miss triple; exact_match. Mac today.

rows.title: Naive vs tiled matmul reuse distances fit L2
rows.how_to_grade: For naive and tiled matmul traces at several sizes, learner returns a per-size boolean 'max reuse distance fits L2 line budget'; exact_match on boolean vector. Mac today.

rows.title: Native NT-store intrinsic kernel

rows.how_to_grade: Return FLOPs/bytes for a prefill matmul (high, compute-bound); harness checks exact at held-out (S,d,dtype). Mac (modeled; real roofline = CUDA phase).

rows.title: Prefill+decode equivalence to no-cache
rows.how_to_grade: Run prefill then N decode steps with cache vs full recompute each step; gate concatenated-output max_abs_err<1e-5. Mac.

rows.title: Prefill vs decode FLOP ratio
rows.concept: Prefill vs decode & arithmetic-intensity roofline (LLM systems view)
rows.how_to_grade: Return FLOPs for a P-token prefill vs one decode step; gate the exact ratio vs reference model. Mac (modeled).

rows.title: Priority-queue BPE reduces work vs naive rescans
rows.how_to_grade: Replace O(n) full-rescan-per-merge with incremental pair updates; settrace pair-comparison count drops below a bound while ids remain byte-exact vs reference. Mac.

rows.title: Prove block-rescaling equals monolithic softmax
rows.how_to_grade: Submit block-computed and full-computed outputs for several block sizes; gate each max_abs_err<1e-6, proving algebraic equivalence. Mac.

rows.title: Quality cost of KV grouping (mean-pool KL)
rows.how_to_grade: Approximate MHA by mean-pooling KV heads into groups; compute mean_kl of resulting attention distribution vs full MHA; gate within tol of reference. Mac.

rows.title: Quantization-aware LayerNorm (int8 activations)
rows.how_to_grade: Feed activation stats to int8 quantized LN output; gate rel_err<threshold vs fp32 LN reference. Mac.

rows.title: Quantized (int8) KV-cache error bound
rows.how_to_grade: Store KV in int8 with per-token scales; compute attention-distribution mean_kl vs fp16 cache; gate below a target bound and within tol of reference. Mac.

rows.title: Real GPU HBM utilization for decode kernel
rows.concept: Prefill vs decode & arithmetic-intensity roofline (LLM systems view)
rows.how_to_grade: Return modeled achievable-bandwidth fraction from the roofline; on Mac graded against the model, and in the CUDA phase cross-checked against measured HBM throughput. Needs CUDA phase for real numbers.

rows.title: Reconstruct applied penalty factor from before/after logits
rows.concept: Logits processing (repetition/frequency/presence penalty, logit bias, banned tokens)
rows.how_to_grade: Given pre- and post-penalty logits, recover the scalar penalty; gate rel_err<1e-4 vs true value. Mac.

rows.title: Reconstruct inverse-Hessian Cholesky structure
rows.how_to_grade: Build (X X^T + lambda I) and its Cholesky-based inverse used by GPTQ; gate rel_err<1e-4 vs reference inverse. Mac.

rows.title: Reconstruct rotation angle from rotated vs original
rows.how_to_grade: Given original and RoPE-rotated vectors, recover per-pair angles (hence position); gate max_abs_err<1e-5 vs true angles. Mac.

rows.title: Reconstruct scale factor from modified freqs
rows.concept: RoPE context extension (NTK-aware, linear/position interpolation, YaRN)
rows.how_to_grade: Given a PI/NTK freq table recover the applied scale factor; gate rel_err<1e-4 vs true factor. Mac.

rows.title: Reconstruct weights from packed int4 + scales
rows.how_to_grade: Unpack nibbles, apply per-group scales/zero-points; gate max_abs_err<1e-6 vs reference dequant. Mac.

rows.title: Recover sublayer contribution from residual write
rows.how_to_grade: Given block input, output, and norm output, recover sublayer(norm(x)) = out - in; gate max_abs_err<1e-7. Mac.

rows.title: Recover the boolean mask from prob zero-pattern
rows.how_to_grade: From attention probability matrix infer the 0/1 mask (P==0 positions); gate exact_match of recovered mask vs true mask. Mac.

rows.title: Repetition penalty applied to logits
rows.concept: Logits processing (repetition/frequency/presence penalty, logit bias, banned tokens)
rows.how_to_grade: Apply HF repetition penalty (divide positive logits, multiply negative) over seen tokens; gate max_abs_err<1e-6 vs reference. Mac.

rows.title: Residual-norm growth: pre vs post over 12 blocks
rows.how_to_grade: Stack 12 identical blocks each way, report ratio of final-to-input residual L2 norm; gate rel_err<1e-3 vs reference growth ratios. Mac.

rows.title: RMSNorm backward from scratch
rows.how_to_grade: Return dx vs finite-difference of forward; gate rel_err<1e-4. Mac.

rows.title: RMSNorm from scratch (Llama-style)
rows.how_to_grade: Compute x/sqrt(mean(x^2)+eps)*weight (no mean subtraction, no bias); gate max_abs_err<1e-6 vs rms_ref.npy. Mac.

rows.title: RoPE relative-position invariance
rows.how_to_grade: Show <RoPE(q,m),RoPE(k,n)> depends only on m-n; submit dot vs (m-n) curve; gate rel_err<1e-3 vs reference. Mac.

rows.title: Round-to-nearest weight-quant baseline error
rows.how_to_grade: RTN-quantize W and report layer-output rel_err on calibration X from gptq.npz; establishes baseline; gate rel_err matches reference. Mac.

rows.title: Round-trip attention stages S->P->O
rows.how_to_grade: Given only P and V recover O; given only S recover P (softmax); chain both; gate each stage max_abs_err<1e-6 vs saved stage fixtures. Mac.

rows.title: Scale-invariance: weights*s, activations/s
rows.how_to_grade: Show (W*s)(X/s) == WX before quantization; gate max_abs_err<1e-6, establishing the equivalence AWQ exploits. Mac.

rows.title: SDPA FLOP closed form
rows.how_to_grade: Student returns FLOPs of QK^T and P@V as f(S,d); harness evaluates for held-out (S,d) triples and checks exact equality to 2*S^2*d + 2*S^2*d model. Mac (modeled).

rows.title: Seeded reproducible sampling sequence
rows.concept: Sampling strategies (greedy, temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p)
rows.how_to_grade: With a fixed numpy Generator seed and given inverse-CDF convention, reproduce the exact sampled id sequence; gate exact_match. Mac.

rows.title: Shift-invariance proof softmax(x)=softmax(x-c)
rows.how_to_grade: Submit softmax(x) and softmax(x-c) for fixture and random c; gate their max_abs_err < machine eps (1e-12) proving identity. Mac.

rows.title: Single-head SDPA vectorized match
rows.how_to_grade: Load Q,K,V from sdpa_qkv.npy; student returns softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_head))@V; compare elementwise to sdpa_out.npy; gate max_abs_err < 1e-6. Mac today.

rows.title: Sliding-window mask width w (Mistral)
rows.how_to_grade: Each query attends only to keys in (i-w, i]; gate output max_abs_err<1e-6 vs window_ref.npy for given w. Mac.

rows.title: Sliding-window ring-buffer cache eviction
rows.how_to_grade: Implement fixed-size ring buffer evicting oldest tokens for windowed attention; gate output max_abs_err<1e-5 vs windowed reference. Mac.

rows.title: Split->merge round-trip identity
rows.how_to_grade: Given per-head outputs recover post-Wo result and verify split(merge(x))==x; gate max_abs_err<1e-7. Mac.

rows.title: Stable softmax survives +300 logits
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture softmax_overflow.npy contains logits up to +300; naive exp gives nan; student max-subtracts; gate max_abs_err<1e-7 vs softmax_ref.npy (no nan). Mac.

rows.title: Stack N blocks + final norm forward
rows.how_to_grade: Compose N shared-weight blocks and a final norm; gate multi-layer output max_abs_err<1e-4 vs stack_ref.npy. Mac.

rows.title: Streaming (online) softmax over row chunks
rows.how_to_grade: Never materialize full logit row: maintain running max m and sum l over chunks; gate final probabilities max_abs_err<1e-6 vs full softmax. Mac.

rows.title: Streaming softmax over KV blocks matches full
rows.how_to_grade: Implement the flash recurrence (running m,l, output rescale) over KV blocks in numpy; gate attention output max_abs_err<1e-5 vs monolithic-softmax attention on sdpa_qkv.npy. Cross-platform (modeled on Mac; real HBM in CUDA phase).

rows.title: SwiGLU FFN match
rows.how_to_grade: Compute down( silu(gate(x)) * up(x) ); gate max_abs_err<1e-5 vs swiglu_ref.npy. Mac.

rows.title: Temperature scaling distribution
rows.concept: Sampling strategies (greedy, temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p)
rows.how_to_grade: Return softmax(logits/T) distribution; gate mean_kl<1e-6 vs reference distribution. Mac.

rows.title: Tile-size invariance (block 1 vs N)
rows.how_to_grade: Run streaming softmax with block=1 and block=N; gate their mutual max_abs_err<1e-7 proving output independent of tiling. Mac.

rows.title: Token count for corpus matches reference
rows.how_to_grade: Report total token count for a fixed corpus under given merges; gate exact_match vs reference integer. Mac.

rows.title: Top-k filter (kept-set exact)
rows.concept: Sampling strategies (greedy, temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p)
rows.how_to_grade: Mask all but top-k logits to -inf; gate exact_match of the surviving index set (and tie handling) vs reference. Mac.

rows.title: Top-p nucleus filter
rows.concept: Sampling strategies (greedy, temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p)
rows.how_to_grade: Keep smallest prefix of sorted probs with cumsum>=p; gate exact_match of kept index set vs reference (including the boundary token). Mac.

rows.title: Trace: decode writes O(1) rows not O(S)
rows.how_to_grade: settrace confirms exactly one new K and one new V row written per decode step (count == step index growth of 1), not full-sequence recompute; gate exact_match on counts. Mac.

rows.title: Trace: residual add appears exactly twice per block
rows.how_to_grade: Instrument a '+=residual' helper; settrace/counter must record exactly 2 residual-add calls per block; gate exact_match on the count. Mac.

rows.title: Train BPE merges from a corpus
rows.how_to_grade: Greedy most-frequent-pair merging for K steps on a fixed corpus; gate exact_match of the ordered merge list vs reference. Mac.

rows.title: Two-pass vs Welford variance in fp16
rows.how_to_grade: Compute LN both ways in fp16 on ill-conditioned fixture; report each path's max_abs_err vs fp32 truth; gate that Welford beats two-pass and matches reference. Mac.

rows.title: Uptrain MHA->GQA by KV mean-pool, bounded KL
rows.how_to_grade: Produce GQA KV from MHA KV minimizing output KL; gate mean_kl below a target bound vs MHA reference. Mac.

rows.title: Vanilla FFN (up, act, down) match
rows.how_to_grade: Compute down(act(up(x))) with GELU from ffn.npz; gate max_abs_err<1e-5 vs ffn_ref.npy. Mac.

rows.title: Vectorize a loopy student SDPA
rows.how_to_grade: Rewrite a triple-loop SDPA into vectorized numpy; settrace inner-region line events must drop below a small constant (e.g. <5*number_of_calls) while max_abs_err<1e-6 vs sdpa_out.npy. Mac.

rows.title: Vectorized gather vs python loop
rows.how_to_grade: Replace per-id loop with fancy indexing; settrace inner-loop events ~0; output max_abs_err<1e-7 vs reference. Mac.

rows.title: Vectorized RoPE, no python loop
rows.how_to_grade: Vectorize a loopy RoPE; settrace inner-loop events ~0; max_abs_err<1e-6 vs rope_ref.npy. Mac.

rows.title: Weight-absorbed RMSNorm (fold gamma into next matmul)
rows.how_to_grade: Fold the RMSNorm weight into the following linear layer and verify combined output equals separate application; gate max_abs_err<1e-5. Mac.

rows.title: Weight tying identity check
rows.how_to_grade: With tied weights, verify lm_head(embed_lookup(one_hot)) reproduces embedding@embedding.T structure; gate max_abs_err<1e-6. Mac.

rows.title: Which values overflow fp16 but not bf16
rows.how_to_grade: Return boolean overflow vector for fp16 (|x|>65504) vs bf16 range; gate exact_match vs reference. Mac.

rows.title: Why 1/sqrt(d): entropy inflation derivation
rows.how_to_grade: Compute mean row Shannon entropy of softmax for scaled vs unscaled scores on sdpa_qkv.npy; submit the entropy ratio; gate rel_err<1e-3 vs precomputed reference ratio. Mac.

rows.title: YaRN ramp + attention temperature
rows.concept: RoPE context extension (NTK-aware, linear/position interpolation, YaRN)
rows.how_to_grade: Apply YaRN per-dimension interpolation ramp and 1/sqrt(t) attention scaling; gate max_abs_err<1e-5 vs yarn_ref.npy. Mac.

rows.title: Z-loss / logit-norm regularization
rows.how_to_grade: Add lambda*logsumexp(logits)^2 auxiliary term (PaLM z-loss); gate combined loss max_abs_err<1e-6 vs reference. Mac.

rows.title: 1D sliding-window via as_strided
rows.how_to_grade: Build (N-w+1, w) window view with correct strides. byte_exact_fraction vs materialized windows reference; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: AI breakdown of attention (QK^T, softmax, PV)
rows.how_to_grade: Return per-stage AI for given seqlen/dim. rel_err vs reference; gate < 1e-6. Mac today.

rows.title: AI of MxKxN matmul with/without reuse
rows.how_to_grade: Return AI under no-reuse and full-cache-reuse assumptions. rel_err vs reference; gate < 1e-6. Mac today.

rows.title: Attainable FLOP/s from roofline
rows.how_to_grade: Return min(peak, AI*bandwidth) per op. rel_err vs reference; gate < 1e-6. Mac today.

rows.title: Back substitution (upper triangular)
rows.how_to_grade: Solve Ux=b bottom-up. rel_err vs reference; gate < 1e-10. Mac today.

rows.title: Batched matmul from scratch
rows.how_to_grade: Loop over batch + triple loop. max_abs_err vs np.matmul batched reference; gate < 1e-6. Mac today.

rows.title: bf16 memory-footprint ratio with bounded error
rows.how_to_grade: Pack fp32 fixture into a bf16 byte buffer. Gate size_ratio == 0.5 exactly AND round-trip max_abs_err < format bound (sub-gate). Mac today.

rows.title: Blelloch work-efficient scan
rows.how_to_grade: Up-sweep/down-sweep exclusive scan. exact_match vs reference on integer fixture; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Blocked/tiled matmul correctness
rows.how_to_grade: BxB tiling over i,j,k. max_abs_err vs naive matmul; gate < 1e-6. Mac today.

rows.title: Branchless stable sigmoid
rows.concept: Stable elementary functions (log1p, expm1, softplus, sigmoid)
rows.how_to_grade: Use exp of -|x| form to avoid overflow for large |x|. max_abs_err vs fp64 reference; gate < 1e-12. Mac today.

rows.title: Broadcasted elementwise op from scratch
rows.how_to_grade: Explicit index arithmetic (no numpy broadcasting) for a+b*c. max_abs_err vs numpy reference; gate < 1e-6. settrace confirms per-element loop (forces from-scratch). Mac today.

rows.title: Broadcasting via 0-stride as_strided
rows.how_to_grade: Emulate np.broadcast_to with 0-strides. byte_exact_fraction vs np.broadcast_to reference; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Build Wengert list + topo order
rows.concept: Reverse-mode autograd tape (Wengert list & topo order)
rows.how_to_grade: Trace a scalar expression into a linearized tape; return node evaluation order. exact_match vs reference topo order (canonicalized); gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: C-contiguous strides from shape
rows.how_to_grade: Compute row-major byte strides from shape+itemsize. exact_match vs np array .strides reference; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Cancellation-free quadratic formula
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture with b^2>>4ac. Use q=-(b+sign(b)sqrt(disc))/2 form. Grade max rel_err of both roots vs high-precision reference; gate < 1e-12. Mac today.

rows.title: Catch a broken analytic gradient
rows.how_to_grade: Provided analytic grad has a bug; learner fixes it so grad-check passes. max_abs_err vs central-diff reference; gate < 1e-5. Mac today.

rows.title: Central-difference gradient check (scalar)
rows.how_to_grade: Central diff on scalar f. rel_err vs analytic gradient reference; gate < 1e-6. Mac today.

rows.title: CGS vs MGS loss of orthogonality
rows.how_to_grade: Ill-conditioned fixture; report ||Q^TQ - I|| for both. Gate: MGS metric < 1e-8 (CGS expected worse, informational). Mac today.

rows.title: Cholesky lower factor, reconstruct A=LL^T
rows.how_to_grade: SPD fixture. max_abs_err of L@L.T - A; gate < 1e-10. settrace forbids np.linalg.cholesky. Mac today.

rows.title: Classical Gram-Schmidt QR
rows.how_to_grade: Return Q,R. max_abs_err of Q@R - A; gate < 1e-9. settrace forbids np.linalg.qr. Mac today.

rows.title: Classify C/F/neither contiguity
rows.how_to_grade: Given (shape,strides) tuples, label C-contig/F-contig/neither. exact_match vs reference (matching numpy flags); gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Classify compute- vs memory-bound
rows.how_to_grade: Given AI + machine (peak FLOP/s, bandwidth), label each op. exact_match vs reference verdicts; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Classify raw 32-bit patterns without float compares
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture of uint32 patterns spanning normal/subnormal/zero/inf/nan. Return integer label array using only integer field tests. exact_match vs labels_ref.npy; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Complex-step differentiation
rows.how_to_grade: Im(f(x+ih))/h with no subtractive cancellation. rel_err vs analytic gradient; gate < 1e-12 (beats finite diff floor). Mac today (f must be complex-analytic in fixture).

rows.title: Compute arithmetic intensity of SAXPY/GEMM
rows.how_to_grade: Return FLOPs, bytes, AI for given op shapes. rel_err vs reference AI; gate < 1e-6. Mac today (pure counting).

rows.title: Condition number of function evaluation
rows.how_to_grade: Return |x f'(x)/f(x)| for f=log near 1, subtraction, etc. rel_err vs analytic reference; gate < 1e-6. Mac today.

rows.title: Condition number via singular values
rows.how_to_grade: kappa = sigma_max/sigma_min. rel_err vs np.linalg.cond; gate < 1e-6. Mac today.

rows.title: Construct a double-rounding counterexample
rows.how_to_grade: Learner returns a value (as fp64/rational) plus both roundings; grader checks fp80/rational->fp32 differs from fp64->fp32->... path bit pattern (exact_match confirms the two differ as predicted); gate: reference verdict matched. Mac today, deterministic.

rows.title: Construct a non-associativity triple
rows.concept: Special values, signed zero, NaN propagation & non-associativity
rows.how_to_grade: Return three fp32 where (a+b)+c != a+(b+c); grader recomputes both and checks bit patterns differ as claimed. exact_match to reference verdict; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Convergence rate ~ |lambda2/lambda1|
rows.how_to_grade: Return measured geometric error-decay ratio. rel_err vs |lambda2/lambda1| from reference spectrum; gate < 5%. Mac today.

rows.title: Cross-entropy gradient = softmax - onehot
rows.how_to_grade: Return dLogits. max_abs_err vs fp64 analytic reference; gate < 1e-9. Mac today.

rows.title: Debug decompose that mishandles subnormals & bias sign
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy decompose (assumes implicit 1 always, wrong bias sign). Fix; run on subnormal-heavy fixture, re-pack, byte_exact_fraction vs original; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Deflation for second eigenpair
rows.how_to_grade: Deflate dominant then power-iterate. rel_err of 2nd eigenvalue vs reference; gate < 1e-5. Mac today.

rows.title: Derive eps for fp32/fp16/bf16 by bit-stepping from 1.0
rows.how_to_grade: No hardcoding; step the integer bit pattern of 1.0 to the next representable and subtract. byte_exact_fraction of the three eps values vs reference; gate 1.0. bf16/fp16 emulated via field math. Mac today.

rows.title: Detect non-SPD matrices
rows.how_to_grade: Return boolean SPD/not (fail on negative diagonal under sqrt). exact_match vs reference (eigval-sign) verdicts; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Determinant from LU
rows.how_to_grade: det = sign(P) * prod(diag U). rel_err vs np.linalg.det; gate < 1e-8. Mac today.

rows.title: Dot product from scratch
rows.how_to_grade: Loop-based dot. rel_err vs np.dot; gate < 1e-9. settrace confirms per-element loop. Mac today.

rows.title: Error growth: naive vs Kahan vs pairwise
rows.how_to_grade: Compute rel_err at fixed N grid for all three; grader checks scaling (naive ~ O(N), Kahan ~ O(1)) via slope of log-log fit within tolerance and final rel_err gates. Deterministic. Mac today.

rows.title: Exact rational value of each float
rows.how_to_grade: Reconstruct numerator/denominator (Python ints / Fraction) from fields, no float math, then compare Fraction to a mpmath/fractions reference. Grade max rel_err over fixture; gate < 1e-15. Mac today, deterministic (exact rationals).

rows.title: Exclusive scan
rows.how_to_grade: Exclusive prefix (identity-first). exact_match vs reference (integer fixture); gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: expm1 for tiny x
rows.concept: Stable elementary functions (log1p, expm1, softplus, sigmoid)
rows.how_to_grade: Stable expm1. rel_err vs mpmath; gate < 1e-14. Mac today.

rows.title: Extract the sign bit
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture sign_in.npy (fp32). Learner views as uint32 and returns uint8 sign array. Grade = fraction of bytes equal to sign_ref.npy; gate == 1.0. Mac today. Deterministic bit op.

rows.title: F-contiguous strides from shape
rows.how_to_grade: Column-major strides. exact_match vs np asfortranarray .strides; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Fast inverse-sqrt bit hack + one Newton step
rows.how_to_grade: Implement 0x5f3759df magic-constant approximation on uint32 view then one Newton iteration. Grade max rel_err vs 1/sqrt(x) reference over positive fixture; gate < 2e-3 (raw) / < 1e-5 (post-Newton), two sub-gates. Mac today, deterministic.

rows.title: Find fp16-overflow / bf16-survives boundary
rows.how_to_grade: Search fixture for the magnitude where emulated fp16 -> inf but bf16 finite (65504 boundary). exact_match of returned boundary index vs reference; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Finite-difference step U-curve minimum
rows.how_to_grade: Sweep h over a fixed geometric grid, compute central-diff error vs analytic derivative fixture; return h* minimizing error. Grade rel_err of achieved-min error vs reference min; gate < 5%. Deterministic (fixed grid). Mac today.

rows.title: Fix bad pivot selection
rows.how_to_grade: Provided LU picks first nonzero pivot (unstable). Change to max-abs. max_abs_err of reconstruction on ill-scaled fixture; gate < 1e-8. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix Cholesky missing diagonal sqrt
rows.how_to_grade: Provided code forgets sqrt on L[j,j]. Fix. max_abs_err of reconstruction; gate < 1e-10. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix Householder sign cancellation
rows.how_to_grade: Provided reflector uses v=x-||x||e1 (cancels). Fix sign = -sign(x0). max_abs_err of reconstruction; gate < 1e-10. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix missing axis-sum after broadcast
rows.how_to_grade: Provided backward returns wrong-shaped grad (no sum over broadcast axis). Fix. max_abs_err vs finite diff; gate < 1e-5. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix NaN cross-entropy via fusion
rows.how_to_grade: Provided -log(softmax(x))[target] NaNs on large logits. Fuse to LSE form. rel_err vs reference; gate < 1e-10. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix NaN-producing naive softmax
rows.how_to_grade: Provided naive softmax NaNs on big logits. Fix to max-subtraction. mean_kl vs reference; gate < 1e-9. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix negative-variance naive formula
rows.how_to_grade: Replace E[x^2]-E[x]^2 (goes negative on shifted fixture) with Welford. rel_err vs fp64; gate < 1e-10. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix off-by-one in back-sub
rows.how_to_grade: Provided back-sub skips last row / wrong range. Fix. rel_err vs reference; gate < 1e-10. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix one-pass variance that returns negatives
rows.how_to_grade: Provided E[x^2]-E[x]^2 on large-offset fixture (mean 1e8). Reformulate (two-pass/shifted). rel_err vs fp64 two-pass reference; gate < 1e-10. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix out-of-bounds as_strided
rows.how_to_grade: Provided as_strided reads past buffer (wrong shape/strides). Fix so window count/strides valid. byte_exact_fraction vs reference AND no read beyond nbytes (grader checks bounds); gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix overflowing softplus
rows.concept: Stable elementary functions (log1p, expm1, softplus, sigmoid)
rows.how_to_grade: Provided naive softplus -> inf for large x. Fix. max_abs_err vs reference; gate < 1e-10. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix transposed-index matmul bug
rows.how_to_grade: Provided matmul indexes B[k][j] as B[j][k]. Fix. max_abs_err vs reference; gate < 1e-6. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix truncating cast to ties-to-even
rows.how_to_grade: Provided cast truncates mantissa (biases down). Fix to RNE; byte_exact_fraction vs numpy astype(fp32) on boundary fixture; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix underflowing log-likelihood
rows.how_to_grade: Provided code multiplies probs -> -inf. Convert to sum of logs. rel_err vs fp64 reference; gate < 1e-10. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix wrong-alignment broadcast (left vs right)
rows.how_to_grade: Provided code aligns dims from the left. Fix to right-alignment. exact_match of result shape+values vs reference; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix wrong topo order breaking grads
rows.concept: Reverse-mode autograd tape (Wengert list & topo order)
rows.how_to_grade: Provided backward visits nodes out of reverse-topo order. Fix. rel_err of grads vs reference; gate < 1e-6. Mac today.

rows.title: Fix wrong-transpose VJP
rows.concept: VJPs for primitive ops (chain rule as code)
rows.how_to_grade: Provided matmul VJP uses B (not B.T). Fix. max_abs_err vs finite diff; gate < 1e-5. Mac today.

rows.title: Flat-index gather from shape/strides/offset
rows.how_to_grade: Given a base buffer + shape/strides/offset, materialize the logical array via index math. byte_exact_fraction vs np.lib.stride_tricks reference; gate 1.0. Mac today.

rows.title: Forward error <= cond * backward error
rows.how_to_grade: Solve Ax=b, perturb, report measured forward error and cond*backward bound. Gate: measured <= bound AND bound rel_err within 10x of measured. Mac today.

rows.title: Forward substitution (lower triangular)

rows.title: Reinterpret cast with .cast()

rows.title: Reorder bases so cooperative super() fires fully

rows.title: Resolve a metaclass conflict
rows.how_to_grade: A multiple-inheritance class fails with a metaclass conflict; introduce a common derived metaclass so it is constructible while preserving behavior; return the resulting MRO names; exact_match. Mac today.

rows.title: Rewrite a generator as an explicit state machine
rows.how_to_grade: Convert a generator to a class with an integer state field and __next__; match outputs; a static check forbids the yield keyword; exact_match. Mac today.

rows.title: Scales-with-threads classifier

rows.title: send/throw/close protocol
rows.how_to_grade: Implement a generator handling .send()/.throw()/.close(); return the value/exception sequence produced by a scripted driver; exact_match. Mac today.

rows.title: Serialize a type's populated-dunder slot table
rows.how_to_grade: For 10 fixture classes emit a uint64 bitmask over a fixed ordered list of 40 dunders indicating presence on the type (via getattr on the type/its C slots); pack masks to bytes; byte_exact_fraction vs reference. Mac today.

rows.title: __set_name__ descriptor naming via metaclass path
rows.how_to_grade: Use __set_name__ so descriptors learn their attribute names during class creation; return the recovered name bindings; exact_match. Mac today.

rows.title: __set_name__ name-binding recovery
rows.how_to_grade: Descriptors capture their own attribute names via __set_name__; return the recovered {class-attr: name} mapping; exact_match. Mac today.

rows.title: set resize points and load factor

rows.title: set vs dict footprint

rows.title: Shape/strides of a memoryview

rows.title: Shared-cell aliasing

rows.title: Simulate the value stack for an opcode subset

rows.title: Small-int interning classifier

rows.title: Split vs combined dict classifier

rows.title: Stack-effect accounting and co_stacksize
rows.how_to_grade: Compute the net stack effect per opcode and the max depth (co_stacksize) for a fixture instruction sequence; return the ints; exact_match. Mac today.

rows.title: str footprint by kind and length
rows.how_to_grade: Predict getsizeof for strings given length and max codepoint (header + kind*len + terminator/ascii-optimization); return the size vector; exact_match under 3.12 pin. Mac today.

rows.title: String interning classifier
rows.how_to_grade: For pairs of strings (identifier-like literals vs runtime-built) output bool whether `is` holds (compile-time interning); exact_match under 3.12 pin. Mac today.

rows.title: Struct-unpack over a buffer without copying

rows.title: sys.modules caching behavior

rows.title: Trace the C3 merge steps

rows.title: Use property and observe recompute

rows.title: Validated property round-trip byte-identity
rows.how_to_grade: A setter enforces dtype/shape and rejects bad assignments; after a scripted sequence of accepted+rejected writes, the backing numpy buffer must be byte-identical to the reference buffer; byte_exact_fraction. Mac today.

rows.title: Walk a traceback object
rows.how_to_grade: From a caught exception walk tb_next and return the (basename, lineno, funcname) chain; exact_match under 3.12 pin. Mac today.

rows.title: Walk the frame stack

rows.title: WeakKeyDictionary identity eviction
rows.how_to_grade: Build an identity-keyed cache that auto-evicts when a key object dies; return survivors after killing some keys; exact_match. Mac today.

rows.title: weakref callback ordering
rows.how_to_grade: Register callbacks on several weakrefs; return the order in which callbacks fire as objects die in a scripted teardown; exact_match. Mac today.

rows.title: __weakref__ slot requirement classifier

rows.title: yield from delegation order

rows.title: Zero-arg super() __class__ cell mechanics
rows.how_to_grade: Show that a method using zero-arg super() carries a __class__ freevar cell; return the cell's referenced class name and confirm methods without super() lack it; exact_match. Mac today.

rows.title: Classify attention config and compute repeat factor
rows.method: Grouped-Query / Multi-Query Attention (GQA / MQA head sharing)

rows.title: Classify a config as MHA / GQA / MQA and compute n_rep
rows.concept: The ratio of query heads to KV heads names the scheme and sets the repeat factor.
rows.method: Grouped-Query / Multi-Query Attention (GQA / MQA head sharing)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle labels MHA (n_kv==n_q), MQA (n_kv==1), else GQA, and computes n_rep=n_q//n_kv; grader diffs the label and n_rep exactly.

rows.title: Classify a query as full-hit / partial-hit / miss
rows.concept: A new request's prefix either fully, partially, or not-at-all matches a cached sequence.
rows.method: Automatic prefix caching / RadixAttention (KV reuse across requests)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle brute-forces the longest common prefix of the query against every cached sequence and labels full-hit (query fully covered), partial-hit (0<lcp<len), or miss (lcp==0); grader diffs the student's label.

rows.title: Classify block-mask tiles as full / partial / empty
rows.concept: create_block_mask marks each (q_block,kv_block) so fully-empty blocks can be skipped.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle evaluates mask_mod(b,h,q_idx,kv_idx) over every element of each block and labels it full (all True), empty (all False), or partial; grader diffs the student's block classification grid against this exhaustive evaluation.

rows.title: Classify causal tiles as full / diagonal / masked
rows.concept: Reason about which (q_block,kv_block) tiles a causal FA kernel must compute, skip, or partially mask.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle iterates every (q_block,kv_block) pair for given seq_len and block_size, checks the causal condition (q_idx>=kv_idx) over the block's index ranges, and labels each 'full' (all pairs valid), 'empty' (all pairs masked, kv_block_start>q_block_end), or 'diagonal' (mixed); grader diffs the student's label grid against this per-tile classification.

rows.title: Classify each past token as sink / window / evicted
rows.concept: StreamingLLM keeps the first k sink tokens and the last w tokens; the middle is evicted.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle labels indices <k as sink, indices in [pos-w,pos) as window, else evicted, for a given position; grader diffs the student's kept/evicted label array exactly.

rows.title: Classify per-step prefill-vs-decode token allocation
rows.concept: Decode tokens are reserved first; remaining budget goes to prefill chunk tokens.
rows.method: Chunked prefill + continuous batching (piggyback prefill on decode)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle, given decode_count and budget, sets prefill_tokens=budget-decode_count per step and the resulting mix; grader diffs the student's per-step allocation exactly.

rows.title: Classify the better quant axis for a key tensor
rows.concept: Keys have per-channel outliers; the axis with larger cross-slice range variance should be quantized along.
rows.method: Low-bit (INT4/INT2) KV cache quantization (KIVI / KVQuant style)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-channel and per-token dynamic-range variance of the key tensor and picks the axis whose per-group quantization yields lower reconstruction MSE; grader checks the student selects the same axis (KIVI predicts per-channel for keys).

rows.title: Classify the masking path SDPA takes for given args
rows.concept: Map (is_causal, attn_mask dtype) to the exact masking semantics and reject illegal combinations.
rows.method: PyTorch Scaled Dot Product Attention (SDPA) dispatcher
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle encodes the documented rule set (is_causal XOR explicit mask; bool mask -> -inf where False; float mask -> added to logits) and labels each argument tuple; grader diffs the student's classification against it.

rows.title: Classify the PyramidKV per-layer budget allocation
rows.concept: PyramidKV gives more KV budget to lower layers, less to upper, summing to the total.
rows.method: KV cache eviction / token dropping (SnapKV, H2O, PyramidKV, Expected-Attention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the pyramid per-layer keep counts from the linear/pyramidal schedule under the total budget; grader diffs the student's per-layer budget vector exactly (and that it sums to the total).

rows.title: Classify values as exact / rounded / overflow in e4m3 vs e5m2
rows.concept: Each fp32 value maps to representable, rounded, or out-of-range under each fp8 format's dynamic range.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle encodes/decodes each value in an e4m3 (max 448) and e5m2 (max 57344) simulator and labels exact (round-trips), rounded (changes but in-range), or overflow (>max); grader diffs both label arrays.

rows.title: Classify which of K,V should get higher bits
rows.concept: Keys typically carry per-channel outliers, so they benefit more from higher precision.
rows.method: On-device quantized KV cache (llama.cpp GGUF / MLX on Mac)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes attention-output error for both bit assignments {K-high/V-low, K-low/V-high} at equal total bits and picks the lower-error one; grader requires the student to select the same assignment (usually K-high) matching the oracle.

rows.title: Compare asymmetric K=q8_0/V=q4_0 vs symmetric configs
rows.concept: Asymmetric (higher-precision K) beats symmetric Q4 at similar KV memory.
rows.method: On-device quantized KV cache (llama.cpp GGUF / MLX on Mac)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes KV under K/V type combos {q8/q8, q4/q4, q8/q4} and attends in fp64; grader requires the student to reproduce that q8_0-K/q4_0-V attention error falls below symmetric-q4 error at the matching size_ratio.

rows.title: Compare block-sparse vs dense: identical output, fewer pairs
rows.concept: Skipping all-False blocks changes compute but not the result; the contribution of skipped blocks is exactly zero.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = dense masked attention in fp64; grader runs the student's block-sparse kernel, requires max_abs_err<1e-5 versus dense, and checks the counted attended-pair total equals total minus (empty_blocks*block_area).

rows.title: Compare e4m3 vs e5m2 on outlier-heavy vs uniform KV
rows.concept: e4m3 has more mantissa (less range); e5m2 has more range (less mantissa).
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes the same KV under both formats with their amax scales and attends in fp64; grader requires the student to reproduce the error ordering (e4m3 lower on well-scaled/uniform, e5m2 lower when raw un-scaled outliers exceed 448).

rows.title: Compare exact-prefix vs block-granular (vLLM APC) reuse
rows.concept: RadixAttention reuses token-exact prefixes; vLLM APC reuses only whole KV blocks.
rows.method: Automatic prefix caching / RadixAttention (KV reuse across requests)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes token-exact LCP and, separately, floor(LCP/block_size)*block_size for block-granular reuse; grader requires the student to report both reuse lengths matching the oracle for each query.

rows.title: Compare fp32-upcast softmax vs pure-fp16 accumulation
rows.concept: The mem-efficient/math backends upcast to fp32 for the softmax reduction; naive fp16 softmax diverges on large logits.
rows.method: PyTorch Scaled Dot Product Attention (SDPA) dispatcher
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = fp64 dense attention; grader runs the student's fp32-accumulated softmax and a pure-fp16 softmax on an adversarial large-magnitude input, and requires the fp32 path within 1e-3 of the oracle while confirming the fp16 path's error is strictly larger.

rows.title: Compare MQA vs GQA vs MHA output reconstruction
rows.concept: Error of reproducing the MHA output grows as KV heads shrink; memory shrinks with it.
rows.method: Grouped-Query / Multi-Query Attention (GQA / MQA head sharing)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle projects the same input through MHA, GQA(g), and MQA (mean-pooled KV) and measures output error vs MHA; grader requires the student to reproduce the monotone error ordering and the matching size_ratio for each.

rows.title: Compare padded-dense vs ragged batching
rows.concept: Padding to max length gives identical valid outputs but wastes compute on pad tokens.
rows.method: FlashInfer attention engine (kernel library for serving)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs padded-dense (mask pad) and ragged (cu_seqlens) attention in fp64; grader requires the student's valid-token outputs to be equal (max_abs_err<1e-5) and the pad-waste ratio (padded_pairs/ragged_pairs) to match exactly.

rows.title: Compare prefix block-sharing (copy-on-write) memory vs duplication
rows.concept: Two sequences sharing a prefix reference the same physical blocks, counted once.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes shared-block memory = unique blocks and duplicated memory = blocks_A+blocks_B, plus independent contiguous attention outputs for both sequences in fp64; grader checks the reported size_ratio exactly and both attention outputs to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Compare recompute vs load-from-CPU crossover
rows.concept: Below some seq_len recompute is cheaper than transferring KV; above it, loading wins.
rows.method: KV cache offloading + disaggregated prefill (CPU/disk tiering)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes recompute cost (FLOP-proportional to seq_len^2) and transfer cost (bytes-proportional to seq_len) and the crossover length; grader requires the student's crossover seq_len to match the oracle.

rows.title: Compare sink+window vs pure sliding-window stability
rows.concept: The pure window loses the attention sink; its distribution entropy destabilizes over a long stream.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-step attention outputs and softmax entropy for both policies in fp64; grader requires the student to reproduce that sink+window stays close to the full-attention reference while pure-window's error/entropy grows, matching the oracle to rel_err<1e-4.

rows.title: Compare SnapKV vs H2O vs Knorm kept-set + error
rows.concept: Different scores keep different tokens and yield different attention-output error.
rows.method: KV cache eviction / token dropping (SnapKV, H2O, PyramidKV, Expected-Attention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes each method's kept set and the resulting attention output vs full in fp64; grader requires the student to reproduce the per-method output error and the pairwise kept-set overlap counts, matching the oracle ordering.

rows.title: Compare the bit-width x group-size error frontier
rows.concept: Smaller groups and more bits lower error but add scale/zero overhead.
rows.method: Low-bit (INT4/INT2) KV cache quantization (KIVI / KVQuant style)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle sweeps bits in {2,4} and group_size in {32,64,128,per-tensor}, recording reconstruction MSE and the scale/zero memory overhead; grader requires the student's MSE curve to match (rel_err<1e-6) and to show monotone decrease as group shrinks.

rows.title: Compare the TTFT-vs-ITL knob as a step-count model
rows.concept: Chunk size trades steps-to-first-token against per-step batched-token load (no wall clock).
rows.method: Chunked prefill + continuous batching (piggyback prefill on decode)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle, for each chunk size c, computes prefill steps=ceil(L/c) and per-step batched-token count (proxy for ITL); grader requires the student's reported step counts and per-step loads to match the oracle exactly across a c-sweep.

rows.title: Compare truncated-rank MLA vs GQA at equal cache budget
rows.concept: At matched bytes/token, low-rank latent MLA can beat GQA on attention-output error.
rows.method: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA, low-rank KV compression)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle sets MLA rank r and a GQA head count so bytes/token match, projects the same input, and measures output error vs full MHA in fp64; grader requires the student to reproduce which achieves lower error at the equal budget.

rows.title: Compare xformers mem-efficient vs SDPA math backend
rows.concept: xformers backs SDPA's mem-efficient path; both are exact and must agree bit-close.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = fp64 dense attention with the same bias; grader requires the student's mem-efficient output and a straightforward math-backend output to each match the oracle and each other to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Debug: accumulator not rescaled when running max grows
rows.concept: The o-accumulator must be multiplied by exp(m_old-m_new) whenever a new block raises the running max.
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads a broken tiled forward that skips the exp(m_old-m_new) correction factor (so earlier blocks stay over-weighted); oracle is the fp64 dense reference; the buggy output must exceed 1e-2 while the student's fix must reach max_abs_err<1e-4.

rows.title: Debug: bias scaled with QK instead of added unscaled
rows.concept: The additive attn_bias must be added after scaling, not multiplied through the scale.
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads an impl that folds bias into the pre-scale product (scaling the bias too); oracle adds unscaled bias to scaled logits in fp64; buggy output errs (>1e-2), fix reaches max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Debug: block-skipper drops a partial diagonal block
rows.concept: A partially-masked block must still be computed with its element mask, not skipped as empty.
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads a kernel that treats 'partial' blocks as 'empty' (skips the causal diagonal); oracle is dense masked attention in fp64; the buggy output errs on boundary rows (>1e-2) while the fix reaches max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Debug: causal mask applied after softmax instead of before
rows.concept: Masking must zero logits with -inf pre-softmax; zeroing probabilities post-softmax skips renormalization.
rows.method: PyTorch Scaled Dot Product Attention (SDPA) dispatcher
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads an SDPA impl that multiplies post-softmax probs by the causal mask (rows no longer sum to 1); oracle is the correct pre-softmax -inf reference in fp64; buggy output must exceed 1e-2, fixed output max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Debug: fp8 KV with scale=1.0 saturates on large values
rows.concept: Without amax scaling, values above the format max clamp/saturate and destroy accuracy.
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads an e4m3 KV path with scale fixed at 1.0 (saturates values >448); oracle uses scale=amax/448 in fp64; the buggy attention output errs (>1e-1) while the fix reaches the calibrated tolerance.

rows.title: Debug: gather ignores the partial last-block length
rows.concept: The final block is only partially filled; reading a full block pulls in stale/garbage slots.
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads a gather that always reads block_size tokens from the last block (ignoring seq_len%block_size); oracle is contiguous attention over true seq_len in fp64; buggy output errs (>1e-2), fix reaches max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Debug: global causal mask leaks across ragged segments
rows.concept: A single global mask over a packed batch lets sequence i attend to sequence i-1.
rows.method: FlashInfer attention engine (kernel library for serving)
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads a ragged-prefill impl with one global causal mask; oracle enforces per-segment boundaries via cu_seqlens in fp64; the buggy output errs on segment-boundary rows (>1e-2) while the fix reaches max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Debug: keys quantized per-token instead of per-channel
rows.concept: Quantizing keys along the token axis smears per-channel outliers across the group and collapses accuracy.
rows.method: Low-bit (INT4/INT2) KV cache quantization (KIVI / KVQuant style)
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads a KIVI impl that quantizes keys per-token; oracle is the per-channel-key reference; grader requires the fixed per-channel MSE to fall below the buggy per-token MSE by the expected margin.

rows.title: Debug: matcher ignores position and matches a suffix
rows.concept: Prefix reuse requires positional prefix equality, not mere token-id membership.
rows.method: Automatic prefix caching / RadixAttention (KV reuse across requests)
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads a matcher that reports reuse from any matching subsequence (over-reports); oracle is the true positional LCP; grader requires the fixed matcher's reuse length to equal the oracle on every query.

rows.title: Debug: offload path truncates dtype on serialize
rows.concept: Serializing KV to a narrower dtype silently corrupts the reloaded cache.
rows.method: KV cache offloading + disaggregated prefill (CPU/disk tiering)
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads an offload path that casts fp32 KV to fp16 on serialize (or drops a layer); oracle keeps full precision in fp64; buggy decode diverges (>1e-3) while the lossless fix reaches max_abs_err<1e-6.

rows.title: Debug: per-tensor scale instead of ggml per-32-block scale
rows.concept: ggml stores a scale per 32-value block; a single per-tensor scale blows up error on varying magnitude.
rows.method: On-device quantized KV cache (llama.cpp GGUF / MLX on Mac)
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads a Q4_0 impl using one per-tensor scale; oracle uses per-32-block scales; grader requires the fixed per-block reconstruction MSE to fall below the buggy per-tensor MSE by the expected margin.

rows.title: Debug: RoPE applied inside the absorbed latent path
rows.concept: Rotating the latent breaks weight absorption because the rotation is position-dependent.
rows.method: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA, low-rank KV compression)
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads an MLA impl that applies RoPE to the absorbed/latent path; oracle keeps RoPE only on the decoupled head in fp64; buggy output errs (>1e-2) while moving RoPE to the decoupled head reaches max_abs_err<1e-4.

rows.title: Debug: running max reset between chunks
rows.concept: Failing to carry m across chunks mis-normalizes later chunks.
rows.method: Chunked prefill + continuous batching (piggyback prefill on decode)
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads a chunked-prefill impl that resets m at each chunk; oracle carries it in fp64; buggy output errs (>1e-2) while the carried-stats fix reaches max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Debug: sinks dropped, keeping only the recent window
rows.concept: Without sink tokens the softmax loses its 'sink', destabilizing the attention distribution.
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads a streaming impl that evicts the sink tokens; oracle keeps them in fp64; grader requires the fixed (sink-keeping) per-step output to match the oracle to max_abs_err<1e-5 while the buggy one diverges.

rows.title: Debug: SnapKV pools across heads instead of the window
rows.concept: Pooling must be over the observation-window token axis, not the head axis.
rows.method: KV cache eviction / token dropping (SnapKV, H2O, PyramidKV, Expected-Attention)
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads a SnapKV impl that avg-pools across heads; oracle pools over the observation window; grader requires the fixed impl's selected index set to equal the oracle's.

rows.title: Debug: tile/repeat instead of repeat_interleave
rows.concept: repeat_interleave keeps each query head with its own KV group; tile mismatches the grouping.
rows.method: Grouped-Query / Multi-Query Attention (GQA / MQA head sharing)
rows.how_to_grade: Grader loads a GQA impl using np.tile (wrong interleave) so query head h attends to the wrong KV head; oracle uses repeat_interleave in fp64; buggy output errs (>1e-2), fix reaches max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Derive commuting of additive score_mods through max-subtraction
rows.concept: Additive biases (ALiBi) commute with the stable-softmax max shift; combine ALiBi+window+soft-cap in one pass.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle applies ALiBi bias, then tanh soft-cap, then the window mask, then a max-subtracted softmax in fp64; grader requires the student's single fused pass (in whatever internal order preserves the math) to match to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Derive effective bits-per-value and the compression ratio
rows.concept: Real cost = nbits + 2*scale_bits/group_size; the vs-fp16 ratio follows.
rows.method: Low-bit (INT4/INT2) KV cache quantization (KIVI / KVQuant style)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes effective_bpv = nbits + (scale_bits+zero_bits)/group_size and ratio = effective_bpv/16; grader compares the student's reported effective bpv and compression ratio to rel_err<1e-9 for several (nbits,group_size).

rows.title: Derive exactness of variable-size causal chunking
rows.concept: Each later-chunk query must attend to all earlier chunks' KV; combining partials equals full causal attention.
rows.method: Chunked prefill + continuous batching (piggyback prefill on decode)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = full causal prefill in fp64; grader runs the student's chunked pass under several variable chunk schedules (respecting the cross-chunk causal mask) and requires identical output to max_abs_err<1e-5 for every schedule.

rows.title: Derive Expected-Attention scores under a query Gaussian
rows.concept: Score each key by its expected softmax weight over a Gaussian model of future queries.
rows.method: KV cache eviction / token dropping (SnapKV, H2O, PyramidKV, Expected-Attention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle fits mean/cov of the observed queries, computes each key's expected pre-softmax score (mu.k) and a Gaussian-variance correction, and ranks; grader compares the student's per-key expected scores to rel_err<1e-4 and the selected indices exactly.

rows.title: Derive & implement the FlashAttention backward (dQ,dK,dV)
rows.concept: Closed-form softmax-attention gradient with P recomputed from (m,l): dS=P*(dP-rowsum(dP*P)).
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = torch.autograd.grad (or finite differences) through the naive attention in fp64; the student implements the flash backward from saved stats, and the grader compares all of dQ,dK,dV to max_abs_err<1e-4.

rows.title: Derive & implement the mem-efficient backward with bias
rows.concept: Same recompute-from-stats backward as flash, extended to the additive-bias case.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = autograd/finite-difference gradients through the biased naive attention in fp64; grader requires the student's dQ,dK,dV to match to max_abs_err<1e-4.

rows.title: Derive is_causal == explicit -inf mask (and + ALiBi bias)
rows.concept: The causal flag equals adding a -inf triangular float mask; a finite bias (ALiBi) shifts logits linearly.
rows.method: PyTorch Scaled Dot Product Attention (SDPA) dispatcher
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle builds the -inf upper-triangular additive mask and, separately, adds ALiBi slope*(kv_idx-q_idx); grader requires the student's is_causal output to equal the explicit-mask output bit-close (max_abs_err<1e-6) and the ALiBi-biased output to match the analytic reference to 1e-5.

rows.title: Derive low-rank KV reconstruction error vs singular energy
rows.concept: The KV matrix's captured singular-value energy at rank r bounds the reconstruction error.
rows.method: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA, low-rank KV compression)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle SVDs the stacked KV, computes rank-r reconstruction error and the captured energy fraction sum(s[:r]^2)/sum(s^2); grader compares the student's reported error and energy fraction to rel_err<1e-6.

rows.title: Derive mean-pool uptraining init for KV heads
rows.concept: Mean-pooling the n_rep MHA K/V heads into one GQA head best preserves the original logits in L2.
rows.method: Grouped-Query / Multi-Query Attention (GQA / MQA head sharing)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes attention-logit reconstruction MSE for mean-pooled KV vs pick-one-head vs the original MHA; grader requires the student's mean-pool init to yield lower logit MSE than pick-one and match the oracle MSE to rel_err<1e-6.

rows.title: Derive output-side absorption of W_UV into W_O
rows.concept: The value up-projection folds into the output projection so decode reads only the latent.
rows.method: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA, low-rank KV compression)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes attention over full V then W_O in fp64; grader requires the student to fold W_UV into W_O (output = W_O W_UV (P@c_V)) and match the reference to max_abs_err<1e-4.

rows.title: Derive query-side weight absorption W_Q^T W_UK
rows.concept: Since (W_Q x).(W_UK c)=x^T(W_Q^T W_UK)c, the up-proj can be precomputed into the query weight.
rows.method: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA, low-rank KV compression)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the naive up-project-then-score path in fp64; grader requires the student's absorbed path (score = (W_absorbed x).c with W_absorbed=W_Q^T W_UK, never materializing full K) to match to max_abs_err<1e-4.

rows.title: Derive symmetric-Q4_0 vs asymmetric-affine-int4 error
rows.concept: Symmetric Q4_0 step=2*amax/15 vs asymmetric (max-min)/15; skewed data favors asymmetric.
rows.method: On-device quantized KV cache (llama.cpp GGUF / MLX on Mac)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes both quantizers' reconstruction error on a skewed KV block analytically and empirically; grader requires the student's reported per-scheme error and the winner (asymmetric on skewed data) to match the oracle to rel_err<1e-4.

rows.title: Derive the disaggregation KV transfer byte count
rows.method: KV cache offloading + disaggregated prefill (CPU/disk tiering)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the transfer bytes from the config formula; grader compares the student's reported byte count exactly and the recompute-vs-transfer break-even seq_len (given a bytes-per-FLOP ratio) to rel_err<1e-6.

rows.title: Derive the e4m3 relative step from mantissa bits
rows.concept: 3 mantissa bits give a relative quantization step of ~2^-(3+1); measured error should track it.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the analytic max relative rounding error 2^-(mantissa_bits+1) and the empirical max relative error of the e4m3 simulator on a mid-range tensor; grader requires the student's measured relative step to match the analytic value to rel_err<0.1.

rows.title: Derive the position-id remap for kept tokens
rows.concept: StreamingLLM assigns RoPE positions by cache slot, not original token index.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle applies RoPE using cache-slot positions (0..k+w-1) for the kept tokens, then attends in fp64; grader requires the student's remapped-position output to match to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Derive the radix node split on partial-prefix insert
rows.concept: Inserting a sequence that shares only part of an existing edge splits that node at the divergence point.
rows.method: Automatic prefix caching / RadixAttention (KV reuse across requests)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the split index (first differing token) and the resulting node count after insertion; grader diffs the student's reported split position and total node count exactly.

rows.title: Derive the split-KV partial-output merge (log-sum-exp combine)
rows.concept: Attention split across KV ranges in parallel, each yielding (m_i,l_i,o_i), then merged into one exact result.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the single-pass fp64 attention; grader gives the student two+ independent KV-range partials and requires the log-sum-exp merge (m=max(m_i), l=sum(exp(m_i-m)*l_i), o=sum(exp(m_i-m)*o_i)/l) to reproduce it to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: FlashAttention backward recompute dS from saved softmax statistics
Implement an ALiBi score_mod attention
rows.concept: flex_attention applies score_mod(score,b,h,q_idx,kv_idx) to each logit before softmax.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes dense QK^T*scale, adds ALiBi slope*(kv_idx-q_idx) as the score_mod, then softmax@V in fp64; grader requires the student's fused-style application to match to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Implement append_paged_kv for a ragged batch
rows.concept: Write each request's new K,V into the correct physical paged slots given per-request append positions.
rows.method: FlashInfer attention engine (kernel library for serving)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the target slots from per-request seq positions + block tables and the resulting pool contents; grader requires the student's post-append pool (at the written slots) to match the oracle exactly, then attention to match to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Implement batched paged decode
rows.concept: One query token per request attends over paged KV via block tables.
rows.method: FlashInfer attention engine (kernel library for serving)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle attends each request's single query over its logically-contiguous KV in fp64; grader has the student gather from the paged pool via block tables and requires max_abs_err<1e-5 across the batch.

rows.title: Implement BlockDiagonalMask for packed sequences
rows.concept: Block-diagonal attention over packed variable-length sequences (xformers fmha) blocks cross-sequence flow.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs per-sequence attention (block-diagonal, sliced by sequence lengths) in fp64; grader requires the student's block-diagonal output to match to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Implement chunked prefill via carried online softmax
rows.concept: Process the prompt in chunks, carrying (m,l,acc) so the final output equals a single-shot prefill.
rows.method: Chunked prefill + continuous batching (piggyback prefill on decode)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = single-shot causal prefill attention in fp64; grader requires the student's chunked pass (carrying running stats across chunks) to match to max_abs_err<1e-5 for a given chunk schedule.

rows.title: Implement FlashAttention-2 forward via tiled online softmax
rows.concept: Block-by-block attention with running (m,l,acc) rescaling that never materializes the N*N score matrix.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = pure-numpy dense attention softmax(Q@K.T*scale)@V in fp64; grader compares the student's tiled fp32 output element-wise (max_abs_err<1e-4) AND asserts via a shape/allocation probe that no (N,N) array is ever created (peak intermediate <= O(block^2)).

rows.title: Implement Gemma2 tanh soft-capping score_mod
rows.concept: Soft-cap logits with cap*tanh(score/cap) inside the attention before the softmax.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle applies score_mod = cap*tanh((Q@K.T*scale)/cap) then softmax@V in fp64; grader compares the student output to max_abs_err<1e-5 across two cap values.

rows.title: Implement GQA head expansion + SDPA
rows.concept: repeat_interleave KV heads by n_rep, then standard attention; degenerate case equals MHA.
rows.method: Grouped-Query / Multi-Query Attention (GQA / MQA head sharing)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = numpy MHA and analytic byte count; grader checks numerical equivalence when n_kv==n_q (max_abs_err<1e-5), correct grouping for n_rep>1, and the reported memory ratio.

rows.title: Implement H2O heavy-hitter eviction trajectory
rows.concept: Accumulate attention mass per token; each step keep recent tokens + top-scoring heavy hitters within budget.
rows.method: KV cache eviction / token dropping (SnapKV, H2O, PyramidKV, Expected-Attention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = deterministic numpy H2O simulator (accumulate scores, evict argmin among evictable each step); grader replays and diffs the kept-index set step by step and checks cache size <= budget throughout.

rows.title: Implement int2 quant with a full-precision recent-token residual
rows.concept: KIVI keeps the most-recent R tokens in fp16 and 2-bit-quantizes the rest.
rows.method: Low-bit (INT4/INT2) KV cache quantization (KIVI / KVQuant style)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes all-but-last-R tokens to int2 (4 levels, per-group affine), keeps the last R in fp16, dequants and attends in fp64; grader requires the student's output to match to max_abs_err<tol and the residual window to be exactly R tokens.

rows.title: Implement KIVI: per-channel key + per-token value quant
rows.concept: Asymmetric axis choice (keys per-channel, values per-token) makes low-bit KV viable.
rows.method: Low-bit (INT4/INT2) KV cache quantization (KIVI / KVQuant style)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = numpy affine quantizer (scale/zero from per-group min-max) in each axis config, dequant, attend in fp64; grader checks the student reproduces the MSE ordering (per-channel-K < per-tensor) and the attention-output error thresholds on a fixed KV.

rows.title: Implement KnormPress L2-norm scoring
rows.concept: Score keys by L2 norm; low-norm keys are dropped.
rows.method: KV cache eviction / token dropping (SnapKV, H2O, PyramidKV, Expected-Attention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-token key L2 norm and top-k by norm under the budget; grader requires the student's kept index set to equal the oracle exactly.

rows.title: Implement lossless offload round-trip attention
rows.concept: Offloading KV to CPU/disk and reloading must not change the attention numerics.
rows.method: KV cache offloading + disaggregated prefill (CPU/disk tiering)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle attends on the resident KV in fp64; grader requires the student's offload (serialize to a buffer) then reload then attend path to match to max_abs_err<1e-6 (bit-close, no dtype loss).

rows.title: Implement LowerTriangularMask causal attention
rows.concept: Causal masking expressed as a -inf upper-triangular additive bias.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle builds the -inf upper-triangular bias, adds to logits, softmax@V in fp64; grader requires the student output to match to max_abs_err<1e-5 and to equal an is_causal reference.

rows.title: Implement mem-efficient attention with an additive attn_bias
rows.concept: Apply an arbitrary additive bias tensor to logits before softmax, tiled without an N*N buffer.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = dense attention with bias added to QK^T*scale, softmax@V in fp64; grader requires the student's tiled output to match to max_abs_err<1e-5 and asserts no N*N materialization.

rows.title: Implement MLA down/up projection with latent cache
rows.concept: Down-project K/V to latent c_KV, cache only the latent, up-project at decode.
rows.method: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA, low-rank KV compression)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = full MHA with the same random W matrices in fp64; grader verifies the student's down-then-up path reproduces it when the latent is full-rank (max_abs_err<1e-4) and that only the latent (kv_lora_rank per token) is stored.

rows.title: Implement MQA single-KV-head broadcast
rows.concept: MQA (n_kv=1) broadcasts one K/V head to every query head.
rows.method: Grouped-Query / Multi-Query Attention (GQA / MQA head sharing)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle broadcasts the single KV head to all query heads and runs attention in fp64; grader requires the student's MQA output to match to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Implement ragged batched prefill with cu_seqlens
rows.concept: Variable-length sequences packed contiguously, with per-segment attention (no cross-sequence).
rows.method: FlashInfer attention engine (kernel library for serving)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle loops per sequence (sliced by cu_seqlens) and runs causal attention in fp64; grader requires the student's ragged-batched output to match to max_abs_err<1e-5 with no cross-segment attention.

rows.title: Implement scaled_dot_product_attention semantics
rows.concept: Faithful SDPA: scaling, optional causal, additive float mask, and boolean mask, matching F.scaled_dot_product_attention.
rows.method: PyTorch Scaled Dot Product Attention (SDPA) dispatcher
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = numpy reference applying scale, then the chosen mask on logits, then row-softmax and @V in fp64; grader feeds several mask-kind cases and requires max_abs_err<1e-5 on every one.

rows.title: Implement scaled-fp8 KV: per-head vs per-tensor scales
rows.concept: Quantize K,V to e4m3 with a scale, dequant, and attend; per-head scales beat one global scale on outlier heads.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle simulates e4m3 with reference scale=amax/448 (per-head and per-tensor), dequants, and attends in fp64; grader requires the student's output within tol of the fp16 reference AND per-head error strictly < per-tensor error on outlier-heavy heads.

rows.title: Implement sink + sliding-window eviction over a stream
rows.concept: Replay a long stream keeping sinks + recent window; per-step output must match attention over the kept set.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = numpy attention masked to the kept index set {sinks union recent-window} in fp64; grader replays the stream, checks per-step outputs match to max_abs_err<1e-5, and that the live cache length never exceeds k+w.

rows.title: Implement sliding-window + document mask_mod
rows.concept: Combine a banded window (q_idx-kv_idx<w) with a same-document constraint as a single mask_mod.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle builds the boolean mask kv_idx<=q_idx AND q_idx-kv_idx<w AND doc_id[q]==doc_id[kv], applies -inf on logits, softmax@V in fp64; grader requires exact mask (index-set match) and output max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Implement SnapKV observation-window pooled selection
rows.concept: Pool the observation-window attention over the prefix, then top-k select KV positions.
rows.method: KV cache eviction / token dropping (SnapKV, H2O, PyramidKV, Expected-Attention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = reference numpy SnapKV (avg-pool the observation-window attention columns, argtopk over the budget); grader compares the chosen index set exactly and the resulting compressed-cache attention output within tol.

rows.title: Implement the block-table gather then attend
rows.concept: A per-request block_table maps logical KV positions to fixed-size physical blocks.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = numpy attention on the logically-contiguous KV in fp64; grader builds a shuffled physical pool + block_table, runs the student's gather-then-attend, and requires max_abs_err<1e-5 with no out-of-block reads.

rows.title: Implement the decoupled RoPE head concatenation
rows.concept: RoPE can't be absorbed into the latent (position-dependent), so a separate rope head is concatenated for scoring.
rows.method: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA, low-rank KV compression)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle scores on [latent(no-rope) concat decoupled-rope-head(with RoPE)] and softmax@V in fp64; grader requires the student's concatenated-scoring path to match to max_abs_err<1e-4.

rows.title: Implement the e4m3 encode/decode round-trip
rows.concept: fp8 e4m3 = 1 sign, 4 exponent, 3 mantissa with subnormals, round-to-nearest-even, clamp to 448.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle is a reference numpy e4m3 simulator (decompose sign/exp/mantissa, handle subnormals, RNE, clamp); grader requires the student's decoded tensor to match to max_abs_err 0 (bit-exact) on a fixed input array.

rows.title: Implement the enable_gqa broadcast path
rows.concept: When K/V have fewer heads than Q, SDPA repeats each KV head across its query-head group.
rows.method: PyTorch Scaled Dot Product Attention (SDPA) dispatcher
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle repeats KV heads by n_rep=n_q/n_kv then runs dense attention in fp64; grader checks the student's grouped SDPA matches to max_abs_err<1e-5 and that query head h uses KV group h//n_rep.

rows.title: Implement the ggml Q4_0 block quantizer
rows.concept: Q4_0 = 32-value blocks, symmetric 4-bit (values -8..7, scale=amax/-8), per-block fp16 scale.
rows.method: On-device quantized KV cache (llama.cpp GGUF / MLX on Mac)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle is a reference numpy Q4_0 simulator (32-elem blocks, scale=amax/-8, clamp to [-8,7], dequant); grader compares the student's per-block dequant MSE to the reference within 1e-8.

rows.title: Implement the ggml Q8_0 block quantizer
rows.concept: Q8_0 = 32-value blocks, per-block fp16 scale=amax/127, int8 values.
rows.method: On-device quantized KV cache (llama.cpp GGUF / MLX on Mac)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle is a reference numpy Q8_0 simulator (32-elem blocks, scale=amax/127, round to int8, store fp16 scale) that dequants; grader requires the student's per-block dequant MSE to match to 1e-8 and the round-trip max error under tol.

rows.title: Implement the int4 group-affine quantizer to a target error
rows.concept: Group-wise affine int4: per-group scale=(max-min)/15, zero=round(-min/scale), q=clamp(round(x/scale+zp),0,15).
rows.method: Low-bit (INT4/INT2) KV cache quantization (KIVI / KVQuant style)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle is the exact numpy affine quantizer above for group_size in {32,64,128}; grader compares the student's dequantized tensor per-group MSE to the reference within 1e-8 and the end-to-end attention error under threshold.

rows.title: Implement the MLX group-affine kv quantizer
rows.concept: MLX kv-bits with kv-group-size: per-group asymmetric affine quant of the KV cache.
rows.method: On-device quantized KV cache (llama.cpp GGUF / MLX on Mac)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle is a numpy affine quantizer with group_size=kv_group_size and nbits=kv_bits (scale=(max-min)/(2^b-1), zero-point), dequant; grader compares the student's per-group dequant MSE to the reference within 1e-8 and the attention output under tol.

rows.title: Implement the paged append (slot_mapping write) path
rows.concept: New K,V for appended tokens are written into physical slots that may cross block boundaries.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle appends T tokens to a contiguous KV and attends in fp64; grader requires the student to write via slot_mapping into the paged pool (spanning >=2 blocks) and, after gather, match to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Implement the prefix tree: reuse length + recompute count
rows.concept: A radix/prefix tree finds the longest cached prefix; the remainder must be recomputed.
rows.method: Automatic prefix caching / RadixAttention (KV reuse across requests)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = O(n*L) brute-force LCP scan over the cached set; grader replays a stream of insert/query ops and diffs the tree's reuse length and recompute count (len-reuse) against the oracle for every op.

rows.title: Measure batch KV memory: paged vs max-length pre-allocation
rows.concept: Contiguous serving pre-allocates max_len per request; paging allocates only ceil(len/bs) blocks.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle sums ceil(len_i/block_size)*block_size across the batch (paged) and batch_size*max_len (contiguous) and forms the waste ratio; grader compares the student's reported ratio to rel_err<1e-9.

rows.title: Measure bits-per-weight and KV size for Q8_0 / Q4_0
rows.concept: Q8_0 = 34 bytes/32 (8.5 bpw); Q4_0 = 18 bytes/32 (4.5 bpw), including the fp16 block scale.
rows.method: On-device quantized KV cache (llama.cpp GGUF / MLX on Mac)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes bytes/block (32*int8+2 scale = 34 for Q8_0; 32*0.5+2 = 18 for Q4_0), bpw, and the KV size ratio vs f16 (2 bytes/val); grader compares the student's reported bpw and ratio to rel_err<1e-9.

rows.title: Measure blocks, slot mapping, and internal fragmentation
rows.concept: Paging allocates ceil(seq/block_size) blocks; the last block wastes the unused tail slots.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes num_blocks=ceil(seq_len/block_size), the slot_mapping (physical slot per logical token given a block_table), and waste=num_blocks*block_size-seq_len; grader diffs all three exactly.

rows.title: Measure cache hit rate and tokens-saved over a stream
rows.concept: Across a request stream, hit rate and reused-token count summarize reuse effectiveness.
rows.method: Automatic prefix caching / RadixAttention (KV reuse across requests)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle replays the stream against the brute-force matcher, accumulating hits and reused tokens; grader compares the student's hit rate and total reused-token count to rel_err<1e-6.

rows.title: Measure HBM saved by layer-wise offload scheduling
rows.concept: Keeping only k active layers' KV resident bounds peak HBM.
rows.method: KV cache offloading + disaggregated prefill (CPU/disk tiering)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes resident bytes = k*per_layer_KV vs full = n_layers*per_layer_KV and the ratio; grader compares the student's reported peak-resident bytes and ratio exactly.

rows.title: Measure kept-token count and memory from compression_ratio
