rows.concept: compression_ratio sets how many tokens survive and the KV memory saved.
rows.method: KV cache eviction / token dropping (SnapKV, H2O, PyramidKV, Expected-Attention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes kept=round((1-ratio)*seq_len) and KV memory saved=ratio*full_bytes; grader compares the student's kept count exactly and the saved-bytes ratio to rel_err<1e-9.

rows.title: Measure mixed-batch paged read count and gather indices
rows.concept: A batch mixing prefill and decode reads a specific set of KV slots via block tables.
rows.method: FlashInfer attention engine (kernel library for serving)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes total KV slots read and the flat gather-index list for the mixed batch; grader diffs the student's slot count and gather indices exactly.

rows.title: Measure MLA cached bytes/token vs GQA
rows.concept: MLA caches only a latent of size kv_lora_rank instead of n_kv_heads*head_dim.
rows.method: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA, low-rank KV compression)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes cached bytes/token = kv_lora_rank*dtype_bytes (MLA) vs 2*n_kv_heads*head_dim*dtype_bytes (GQA) and the ratio; grader compares the student's reported bytes/token and ratio exactly.

rows.title: Measure per-channel-K vs per-token-K reconstruction MSE
rows.concept: KIVI's core finding: keys quantize better per-channel than per-token at low bits.
rows.method: Low-bit (INT4/INT2) KV cache quantization (KIVI / KVQuant style)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs an int4 affine quantizer along each axis and computes reconstruction MSE; grader requires the student's per-channel-K MSE to be below per-token-K MSE and both values within rel_err<1e-6 of the oracle.

rows.title: Measure per-row online-softmax statistics (m,l)
rows.concept: Compute the running max m and softmax denominator l a streaming kernel accumulates, matching a stable logsumexp.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes S=Q@K.T*scale, then per row m=max(S), l=sum(exp(S-m)) in fp64 (numpy logsumexp form); grader compares the student's streamed final (m,l) per query row within rel_err<1e-6, independent of the block schedule used.

rows.title: Measure prefill FLOPs saved by prefix reuse
rows.concept: Reused prefix tokens skip their prefill attention/MLP FLOPs.
rows.method: Automatic prefix caching / RadixAttention (KV reuse across requests)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-request prefill FLOPs analytically (proportional to sum over positions) for full vs reuse-offset prefill and forms the saved fraction; grader compares the student's saved-FLOP fraction to rel_err<1e-6.

rows.title: Measure skipped-block count and dense-FLOP fraction
rows.concept: Block-sparsity turns an empty-block count into a compute-saving ratio versus dense attention.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle counts empty blocks from the exhaustive block-mask and computes attended_pairs/total_pairs; grader compares the student's skipped-block count exactly and the FLOP fraction to rel_err<1e-9.

rows.title: Measure the attention-sink probability mass on first tokens
rows.concept: First tokens absorb a disproportionate share of softmax mass (the sink phenomenon).
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the column sums of the softmax attention matrix and the fraction of total mass on the first k tokens; grader compares the student's reported sink-mass fraction to rel_err<1e-6.

rows.title: Measure the chunk schedule under a token budget
rows.concept: max_num_batched_tokens slices a length-L prompt into a fixed number of steps.
rows.method: Chunked prefill + continuous batching (piggyback prefill on decode)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes num_steps=ceil(L/budget) and the per-step prefill-token counts (last step remainder); grader diffs the student's chunk schedule exactly.

rows.title: Measure the constant cache size and attended pairs
rows.concept: The cache stays at k+w regardless of sequence length.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes cache_size=min(k+w, seq_so_far) at each step and the attended-pair count per step; grader requires the student's reported sizes to equal the oracle and never exceed k+w.

rows.title: Measure the default SDPA scale and top pre-softmax logit
rows.concept: SDPA scales QK^T by 1/sqrt(head_dim) unless an explicit scale is given.
rows.method: PyTorch Scaled Dot Product Attention (SDPA) dispatcher
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes scale=1/sqrt(E) (or the passed scale) and logit[0,0]=scale*(Q[0].K[0]) in fp64; grader compares the student's reported scale and logit to rel_err<1e-6.

rows.title: Measure the KV-cache byte reduction ratio
rows.concept: GQA shrinks the KV cache by exactly n_kv_heads/n_q_heads.
rows.method: Grouped-Query / Multi-Query Attention (GQA / MQA head sharing)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes KV bytes/token = 2*n_kv_heads*head_dim*dtype_bytes and the ratio n_kv/n_q vs MHA; grader compares the student's reported bytes/token and ratio exactly.

rows.title: Measure the O(N) memory of the mem-efficient path
rows.concept: The kernel stores O(N) softmax stats, never the N*N score matrix.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the naive O(N^2) buffer size vs the mem-efficient O(N) stats size and their ratio; grader compares the student's reported intermediate-buffer size and asserts (via instrumentation) no (N,N) array is allocated.

rows.title: Measure the optimal per-tensor scale and its max error
rows.concept: The library scale is amax/max_repr; it maps the tensor peak to the format's largest value.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes scale=amax/448 for e4m3 (amax/57344 for e5m2) and the max abs dequant error after quantize; grader compares the student's reported scale (rel_err<1e-6) and confirms the error ordering e4m3<e5m2 on well-scaled data.

rows.title: Optimize: block-size-invariant exactness + safe-softmax stability
rows.concept: Prove tiled output is identical across block sizes and that max-subtraction prevents overflow that naive softmax hits.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle = fp64 dense attention; grader runs the student's kernel for block in {1,8,32,N}, requires all outputs agree with the oracle to max_abs_err<1e-4, and on a large-magnitude score input requires the stable path to stay finite while flagging that the unstable (no-max) variant overflows.

rows.title: Optimize LRU eviction under a node budget
rows.concept: When the tree exceeds capacity, evict the least-recently-used leaf; hit rate depends on the policy.
rows.method: Automatic prefix caching / RadixAttention (KV reuse across requests)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle is a reference LRU-over-radix simulator with a fixed node budget; grader replays insert/query ops and diffs the student's final cached set and cumulative hit count against it.

rows.title: Optimize minimal block allocation + verify no OOB reads
rows.concept: Compute the smallest block set covering a batch and the gather indices, with every read in-bounds.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the minimal block count and a valid slot assignment; grader checks the student's block count equals the minimum and asserts every gather index lies inside an allocated block (no out-of-bounds).

rows.title: Optimize per-head scale: amax vs percentile clipping
rows.concept: A percentile (e.g. 99.9%) scale clips rare outliers, lowering error when a few values dominate amax.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes attention-output error under scale=amax/448 and scale=p99.9/448 (outliers clipped) in fp64; grader requires the student to reproduce that percentile clipping lowers output error on a heavy-tailed head and report which scale wins.

rows.title: Optimize the sink/window split under a fixed budget
rows.concept: Given B=k+w, choosing k trades sink coverage against recency to minimize output error.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle sweeps k in [1,B-1], measures attention-output error vs full attention in fp64, and picks the argmin k; grader requires the student's chosen k to match the oracle's optimal split.

rows.title: Optimize which prefixes stay in HBM vs tier out
rows.concept: Under an HBM budget, keep the highest reuse-value prefixes to maximize hit rate.
rows.method: KV cache offloading + disaggregated prefill (CPU/disk tiering)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle solves the value-density knapsack/greedy over prefixes (reuse_freq*len vs bytes) under the budget; grader requires the student's kept set and resulting hit rate to match the oracle.

rows.title: Reconstruct decode output from a disaggregated prefill KV
rows.concept: A prefill worker serializes the full KV; a decode worker loads it and continues.
rows.method: KV cache offloading + disaggregated prefill (CPU/disk tiering)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs a single fused prefill+decode in fp64; grader has the student compute+serialize the prefill KV, reload it in a separate decode stage, and requires the decode output to match the fused run to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Reconstruct full prefill by merging per-chunk partials
rows.concept: Combine per-chunk (m,l,o) partials via log-sum-exp into the full-prefill output.
rows.method: Chunked prefill + continuous batching (piggyback prefill on decode)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the full prefill output in fp64; grader gives the student independent per-chunk partial stats and requires the log-sum-exp merge to reconstruct the full output to max_abs_err<1e-5.

rows.title: Reconstruct P and O from saved (m,l) log-sum-exp stats
rows.concept: Given only Q,K,V and per-row (m,l) from a forward pass, rebuild the normalized probabilities and output without a second max pass.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle recomputes S, then P=exp(S-m)/l using the SAVED m,l and O=P@V in fp64; grader checks the student reconstructs P (rows sum to 1) and O to max_abs_err<1e-5, verifying the backward-pass recompute identity.

rows.title: Reconstruct per-sequence tensors from a packed ragged batch
rows.concept: cu_seqlens delimits the packed layout back into a list of per-sequence Q/K/V.
rows.method: FlashInfer attention engine (kernel library for serving)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle slices the packed tensor at cu_seqlens offsets; grader requires the student's unpacked per-sequence tensors to equal the oracle exactly.

rows.title: Reconstruct the contiguous KV from a fragmented pool
rows.concept: Given a shuffled physical block pool and a block_table, rebuild the logical KV tensor exactly.
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle holds the original contiguous KV; grader shuffles it into blocks with a random block_table, and requires the student's reconstructed tensor to match element-wise to max_abs_err<1e-6 (byte-close).

rows.title: Reconstruct the full per-query-head KV view from packed GQA
rows.concept: Given packed KV and n_rep, expand to the per-query-head layout with correct index math.
rows.method: Grouped-Query / Multi-Query Attention (GQA / MQA head sharing)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle expands packed KV[:, kv_head] to query-head h via kv_head=h//n_rep; grader requires the student's expanded tensor to equal the oracle element-wise (exact).

rows.title: Achieved-batch-size histogram
rows.method: Dynamic request batching + queue-delay scheduling (general/non-autoregressive ML)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture arrivals.npy + policy. Learner returns the histogram (count per formed batch size). Oracle recomputes from the sim. Grade exact_match of the histogram; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Admission order minimizing mean completion latency
rows.concept: SJF vs FIFO admission under a fixed slot count
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture queued.json: gen_len per waiting request, slot count S, all present at t=0. Learner returns an admission order and the resulting mean completion latency. Oracle computes the shortest-remaining-first optimal mean latency by simulation. Grade rel_err of learner's achieved mean latency vs the SJF-optimal; gate met when rel_err < 1e-9 (must equal the optimum). Deterministic.

rows.title: Aggregate vs single-stream throughput
rows.concept: Tokens/step across N slots vs one stream
rows.method: Local / edge batched serving (no-CUDA: Metal / CPU / Windows)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture the per-step slot-occupancy trace. Learner returns aggregate tokens/step (mean busy slots) and the single-stream rate (1 token/step). Oracle recomputes. Grade rel_err; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: APC with LRU eviction
rows.concept: Fixed-capacity block pool with least-recently-used eviction
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture requests.json + pool_capacity C (blocks). Learner maintains an LRU dict keyed by chain hash; on each request reuse hits, insert misses, evict LRU when full (touching reused blocks updates recency). Return (hit_count, list of evicted hashes in eviction order). Oracle = reference LRU APC. Grade exact_match of hit_count and eviction order; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Apply a token bitmask to logits
rows.concept: Mask disallowed tokens to -inf before sampling
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture logits.npy + allowed-token-id sets per step. Learner sets disallowed logits to -inf and returns the greedy argmax per step. Oracle recomputes the masked argmax. Grade exact_match of the argmax sequence (all inside the allowed sets); gate 1.0.

rows.title: Attention FLOP count
rows.concept: FLOPs of QK^T + softmax + PV for given shapes
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture shapes (batch, heads, seqlen_q, seqlen_k, head_dim, causal flag). Learner returns total multiply-add FLOPs = 2*b*h*(sq*sk*d for QK^T + sq*sk*d for PV), halved for the causal triangle. Oracle recomputes the closed form. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Attention FLOPs: packed vs padded
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture lens.npy + head_dim + heads. Learner returns total attention FLOPs for packed (proportional to sum(len_i^2)) vs padded (batch*max_len^2) using the same per-pair constant. Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match of both; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Batch-width efficiency as slots fill
rows.method: Local / edge batched serving (no-CUDA: Metal / CPU / Windows)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture the per-step occupancy trace + configured batch width N. Learner returns per-step utilization = busy_slots / N and its mean. Oracle recomputes. Grade rel_err; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: Block count and last-block slack for a sequence
rows.concept: block_size arithmetic: ceil(len/block_size) and internal slack
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture seqlens.npy + block_size B. Learner returns per-seq (num_blocks = ceil(len/B), wasted_slots = num_blocks*B - len). Oracle recomputes closed-form. Grade exact_match of both integer arrays; gate 1.0. Deterministic.

rows.title: Block-diagonal varlen attention
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture packed q,k,v + cu_seqlens (real skewed-length batch). Learner attends with a block-diagonal mask (each token attends only within its segment). Oracle loops SDPA per unpacked sequence and concatenates (fp64). Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-5.

rows.title: Block-size sensitivity of hit rate
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture requests.json where prefixes diverge mid-block. Learner computes total reused blocks (in tokens) for block_size B1 and B2 and returns both plus which yields more token reuse. Oracle recomputes both. Grade exact_match of both token-reuse counts; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Block-table gather attention equivalence
rows.concept: Paged KV indirection produces identical attention to contiguous KV
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture k.npy,v.npy,q.npy for one real GQA layer (fp32). Learner splits K/V into B-token blocks, builds a block_table per seq, gathers via the table, and runs attention. Oracle = contiguous attention over the same tokens in fp64. Grade max_abs_err element-wise; gate < 1e-6.

rows.title: Break-even acceptance for a cost ratio
rows.concept: Minimum alpha where spec decoding beats vanilla
rows.method: Speculative decoding (draft model / EAGLE / Medusa / n-gram / MTP)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture draft:target cost ratio c and block length k. Learner returns the minimum acceptance rate alpha* at which expected cost per accepted token with speculation equals vanilla. Oracle solves the cost equation numerically. Grade rel_err vs ref; gate < 1e-6.

rows.title: Bucket set minimizing waste under a memory cap
rows.concept: Each bucket costs memory proportional to its size
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture size_histogram + per-bucket memory = size*unit + total memory cap. Learner chooses a bucket set minimizing pad waste s.t. sum(size*unit) <= cap. Oracle = constrained DP/knapsack over sizes. Grade exact_match of the chosen buckets and the achieved waste; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Build cu_seqlens from lengths
rows.concept: Cumulative-sum offset array for a packed batch
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture lens.npy. Learner returns cu_seqlens = [0, len0, len0+len1, ...] (int32). Oracle = numpy cumsum with leading 0. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Cache-salt isolation
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture pairs.json: pairs of requests with identical tokens but possibly different cache_salt. Learner labels each pair 'blocks collide' or 'isolated' by whether their block-0 chain hashes (which fold in salt) match. Oracle recomputes hashes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Causal-masked tiled attention
rows.concept: Lower-triangular masking inside the tiled kernel
rows.how_to_grade: Same tensors + is_causal. Learner adds the causal mask in the tiled loop (skip upper-triangle tiles, mask the diagonal tile). Oracle = causal SDPA fp64. Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-4.

rows.title: Choose token budget minimizing tail ITL under a TTFT cap
rows.concept: Budget tuning: trade TTFT against inter-token stalls
rows.method: Chunked prefill / Dynamic SplitFuse / stall-free scheduling
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture workload.json + candidate budgets + TTFT cap. Learner returns the budget minimizing max ITL (worst decode gap) subject to every request's TTFT <= cap. Oracle sweeps candidates with the reference sim. Grade exact_match of the chosen budget; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Chunked vs monolithic iteration count and TTFT
rows.concept: Effect of chunking on total iterations and per-request time-to-first-token
rows.method: Chunked prefill / Dynamic SplitFuse / stall-free scheduling
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture workload.json + budget C. Learner simulates both policies and returns (iters_chunked, iters_mono, per-request TTFT_iter for each). Oracle runs both reference sims. Grade exact_match of iteration counts and TTFT arrays; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Classify accept/reject given u, p, q
rows.method: Speculative decoding (draft model / EAGLE / Medusa / n-gram / MTP)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture rows of (draft_token, u, p_vec, q_vec). Learner labels each accepted iff u <= p[token]/q[token] (clamp p/q to 1). Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Classify batch trigger: size vs timeout
rows.method: Dynamic request batching + queue-delay scheduling (general/non-autoregressive ML)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture the formed-batch log (queue depth + oldest wait at dispatch). Learner labels each batch 'size' (reached preferred size) or 'timeout' (delay cap fired first). Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Classify captured vs eager-fallback batches
rows.concept: Sizes above the max captured bucket fall back to eager
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture captured buckets + incoming batch sizes. Learner labels each 'graph' (<= max bucket) or 'eager' (> max bucket). Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Classify each request prefill- vs decode-bound
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture reqs.json (prompt_len, gen_len) + a rule comparing prefill compute demand vs decode bandwidth demand. Learner labels each request. Oracle recomputes from the rule. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Classify each step compute- vs memory-bound
rows.method: Chunked prefill / Dynamic SplitFuse / stall-free scheduling
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture iter_compositions.json ((decode_tokens, prefill_tokens) per step) + threshold rule (given). Learner labels each step. Oracle recomputes from the rule. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Classify eligible SDPA backend
rows.concept: PyTorch flash / mem-efficient / math backend selection rules
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture cases.json ((dtype, head_dim, has_attn_mask, is_causal, device_is_cpu) tuples). Learner labels each with the backend PyTorch would pick per the documented rules (flash needs fp16/bf16 + head_dim constraints + no arbitrary mask; CPU falls to math). Oracle recomputes from the rule table. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Classify representable format per value
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture values.npy. Learner labels each value: which of E4M3 / E5M2 gives the smaller round-trip abs error (ties -> E4M3). Oracle computes both casts and errors. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Classify slot free/busy at each step
rows.concept: Slot state from the assignment trace
rows.method: Local / edge batched serving (no-CUDA: Metal / CPU / Windows)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture the slot->seq_id trace with gaps. Learner labels each (step, slot) 'busy' or 'free'. Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Classify static vs continuous from an iteration trace
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture sched_traces.json: a list of runs, each a per-iteration active-sequence-id set. Learner labels each run static (the active set is frozen until every member finishes, then swaps wholesale) or continuous (a finished seq is replaced by a waiting one mid-run). Oracle re-derives the label by scanning for any admission that occurs before all current members complete. Grade exact_match vs labels_ref; gate 1.0. Deterministic.

rows.title: Compute block chain hashes
rows.concept: vLLM chain hash: h_i = H(h_{i-1}, block_token_ids, salt)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture tokens.npy + block_size B + salt + the exact folding rule (h_0=salt; h_i = a 64-bit FNV-style fold of (h_{i-1}, tuple(block_i tokens)) specified in the prompt). Learner returns the per-block hash array. Oracle recomputes with the same rule. Grade exact_match of the uint64 hash sequence; gate 1.0. Deterministic.

rows.title: Concurrency admitted: paged vs contiguous
rows.concept: Max concurrent sequences fitting a VRAM block budget
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture length distribution (seqlens.npy), block budget N_blocks, block_size B, max_len L. Learner returns (max_concurrent_paged: greedily admit seqs by ceil(len/B) until blocks run out, max_concurrent_contig: floor(N_blocks / ceil(L/B))). Oracle recomputes both. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Constrained vs free argmax divergence
rows.concept: Steps where masking changes the greedy choice
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture logits.npy per step + the FSM. Learner counts steps where the constrained argmax (over the allowed set) differs from the unconstrained argmax. Oracle recomputes both argmax sequences. Grade exact_match of the divergence count; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Continuous vs static throughput on one trace
rows.concept: Speedup accounting: tokens/makespan for both policies
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture reqs.json. Learner runs both the static and continuous sims and returns (makespan_static, makespan_cont, throughput_ratio = (tok/makespan_cont)/(tok/makespan_static)). Oracle runs both reference sims. Grade rel_err on all three scalars vs ref; gate < 1e-9. Deterministic.

rows.title: Debug a batcher that ignores the delay cap
rows.concept: A partial batch must flush when the cap fires
rows.method: Dynamic request batching + queue-delay scheduling (general/non-autoregressive ML)
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy batcher only dispatches at preferred size, so a trailing partial batch waits forever. Learner fixes it to also flush at max_queue_delay. Re-run on arrivals.npy. Oracle = correct sim. Grade exact_match of formation times and sizes; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Debug a hash that drops the parent link
rows.concept: Position-dependence: chaining prevents false prefix hits
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy hash uses H(block_token_ids, salt) with no parent, so a block with identical tokens hits regardless of preceding context. Learner restores the parent chain. Re-run hit accounting on requests.json where the same block content appears under different prefixes. Oracle = correctly chained APC. Grade exact_match of the per-block hit map; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Debug a mask that allows early EOS
rows.concept: EOS is permitted only in an accepting state
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy FSM mask always leaves EOS unmasked, letting decode stop mid-string. Learner fixes it to allow EOS only when the current state is accepting. Re-run per-step masks. Oracle = correct FSM. Grade exact_match of the allowed sets; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Debug a mask that leaks across boundaries
rows.concept: Replace a global causal mask with a per-segment block-diagonal one
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy code applies one global causal mask over the whole packed buffer, letting seq k attend to seq k-1's tail. Learner fixes it to reset the mask at each cu_seqlens boundary. Oracle = per-sequence SDPA. Grade max_abs_err (and verify zero weight across boundaries); gate < 1e-5.

rows.title: Debug a merge that forgets the accumulator rescale
rows.concept: Each partial must be scaled by e^{L_i - m} before summing
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy merge sums partial outputs weighted by e^{L_i} without subtracting the global max m (and without renormalizing correctly). Learner fixes the rescale. Oracle = full SDPA fp64. Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-5.

rows.title: Debug a missing 1/sqrt(d) scale
rows.concept: The softmax scale must divide the logits
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy attention omits the 1/sqrt(head_dim) scale (or applies sqrt(d) instead). Learner fixes it. Oracle = correctly scaled SDPA fp64. Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-6.

rows.title: Debug a packer that starves decodes
rows.concept: Reserve one decode slot per running seq before spending budget on prefill
rows.method: Chunked prefill / Dynamic SplitFuse / stall-free scheduling
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy packer fills the whole budget with a long prefill chunk, dropping decodes to zero that step (spiking ITL). Learner fixes it to seat decodes first. Re-run on state.json. Oracle = correct packer. Grade exact_match of per-iteration (decode_tokens, prefill_chunk); gate 1.0.

rows.title: Debug a scale that clips outliers
rows.concept: Use absmax, not mean/std, for the quant scale
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy quantizer sets scale from 3*std (or mean), saturating outliers. Learner fixes it to absmax. Re-quantize k.npy; oracle = correct absmax cast. Grade rel_err of dequant vs ref; gate < 1e-6.

rows.title: Debug a scheduler that never frees finished slots
rows.concept: Slot reclamation on completion enables mid-flight admission
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy_sched.py keeps a seq occupying its slot after it hits gen_len, so waiting requests never admit. Learner fixes the retirement step. Re-run on reqs.json; oracle is the correct continuous sim. Grade exact_match of the per-iteration active-set trace; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Debug a scheduler that overflows -np slots
rows.concept: Never assign more than N concurrent slots
rows.method: Local / edge batched serving (no-CUDA: Metal / CPU / Windows)
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy scheduler admits a new request even when all N slots are busy (N+1 active). Learner fixes it to queue until a slot frees. Re-run on reqs.json. Oracle = correct slot sim. Grade exact_match of per-step occupancy; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Debug an insert that never splits nodes
rows.concept: Divergence must break an edge, not append a sibling at the root
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy insert only matches whole existing edges (no partial-edge split), undercounting reuse. Learner fixes the split. Re-run saved-token accounting on seqs.json. Oracle = correct radix tree. Grade exact_match of total_saved; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Debug an off-by-one in slot_mapping
rows.concept: Correct (block_idx, block_offset) mapping for a token position
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy slot_mapping computes block_offset = pos % B but block_idx = pos // (B-1). Learner fixes to pos // B. Re-gather K/V and run attention; oracle = contiguous attention (fp64). Grade max_abs_err of output; gate < 1e-6.

rows.title: Debug an SGMV segment off-by-one
rows.concept: Correct segment offsets so each row uses its own adapter
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy SGMV uses segment start offsets shifted by one, applying the wrong adapter to a segment. Learner fixes the offset. Oracle = per-row reference (fp64). Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-5.

rows.title: Debug bucket assignment that rounds down
rows.concept: Rounding down would drop rows; must round up
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy code assigns each batch to the NEAREST bucket, sometimes smaller than the batch (dropping rows). Learner fixes it to the smallest bucket >= batch (eager if none). Re-run on the batch sizes. Oracle = correct assignment. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Debug KV byte accounting (GQA + factor of 2)
rows.concept: Use num_kv_heads (not attention heads) and count both K and V
rows.how_to_grade: Provided buggy formula uses num_attention_heads and omits the *2 for K and V. Learner fixes to 2*num_kv_heads. Recompute transfer bytes on cfg.json. Oracle = correct formula. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Derive minimum max_num_seqs to hit a throughput target
rows.concept: Smallest concurrency that saturates the trace
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture reqs.json + target makespan M*. Learner returns the smallest integer S such that the continuous sim's makespan <= M*. Oracle sweeps S upward with the reference sim and reports the first qualifying S (or -1 if unreachable). Grade exact_match of the integer; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Detect cross-sequence leakage in a mask
rows.concept: A valid varlen mask is block-diagonal
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture masks.json + cu_seqlens. Learner labels each mask 'leaks' iff any allowed (query,key) pair crosses a segment boundary. Oracle recomputes from cu_seqlens. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Detect illegal block aliasing
rows.concept: A physical block may be shared read-only but not written by two live seqs
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture block_tables.json: per-seq (physical_block_ids, is_prefix_shared flags). Learner labels each configuration valid/invalid: invalid iff two distinct live seqs map the same physical block in a non-shared (writable) slot. Oracle re-derives from the tables. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Does the string parse against the grammar?
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture candidate strings + the regex/grammar. Learner labels each accepted/rejected by running the FSM to completion. Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: DP-optimal bucket selection (K buckets)
rows.concept: Choose K capture sizes minimizing padding waste
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture size_histogram + budget K. Learner returns the K bucket sizes minimizing total pad waste (each size rounds up to the nearest chosen bucket >= it; the max distinct size must be a bucket). Oracle = DP over the sorted sizes. Grade exact_match of the chosen bucket set and the minimized waste; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Dynamic-batcher event simulator
rows.concept: Form a batch at preferred size or when the delay cap fires
rows.method: Dynamic request batching + queue-delay scheduling (general/non-autoregressive ML)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture arrivals.npy (timestamps) + preferred_batch_size + max_queue_delay. Learner simulates Triton's dynamic batcher: dispatch when the queue reaches preferred size OR the oldest waiting request has waited max_queue_delay. Return (batch_formation_times, batch_sizes). Oracle = reference event sim. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Dynamic SplitFuse budget packer
rows.concept: Seat 1 decode token per running seq, then chunk pending prefills into remaining budget
rows.method: Chunked prefill / Dynamic SplitFuse / stall-free scheduling
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture state.json: running decode seqs, pending prefill (prompt_len) queue, max_num_batched_tokens C. Learner produces per-iteration (decode_tokens, prefill_chunk_tokens) by seating decodes first then greedily consuming the rest with prefill chunks. Oracle = reference greedy packer. Grade exact_match of the per-iteration allocation sequence and iteration count; gate 1.0.

rows.title: E4M3 encode/decode round-trip
rows.concept: Cast to float8_e4m3 and back, bit-exact to the reference cast
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture x.npy (fp32). Learner encodes to E4M3 (1-4-3, bias 7, no inf, saturating) and decodes to fp32. Oracle = ml_dtypes/torch float8_e4m3fn cast round-trip. Grade max_abs_err vs the reference dequant; gate == 0 (bit-exact).

rows.title: E5M2 vs E4M3 dynamic range
rows.concept: Max representable and smallest normal from the bit split
rows.how_to_grade: Learner returns (max_normal, min_normal) for E4M3 (1-4-3, bias 7) and E5M2 (1-5-2, bias 15) derived from the exponent/mantissa fields. Oracle computes the closed-form values. Grade rel_err on all four; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: Enumerate accepted strings up to length L
rows.concept: All strings the regex accepts within a length bound
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture a regex + length bound L over a small vocab. Learner returns the sorted set (or count) of accepted strings of length <= L via BFS over FSM states. Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Expected acceptance = 1 - TV(p,q)
rows.method: Speculative decoding (draft model / EAGLE / Medusa / n-gram / MTP)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture p.npy,q.npy. Learner returns the expected single-token acceptance probability = sum(min(p,q)) = 1 - 0.5*sum|p-q|. Oracle recomputes both equivalent forms. Grade rel_err vs ref; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: First-fit-decreasing bin packing into fixed bins
rows.concept: Assemble packed batches under a max_seqlen bin size
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture lens.npy + bin_size. Learner packs sequences into bins using first-fit-decreasing (sort desc, place each in the first bin that fits, else open a new bin). Return (num_bins, per-sequence bin assignment). Oracle = reference FFD. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0. Deterministic heuristic (matches the library's packer, not the NP-hard optimum).

rows.title: Fixed-slot (-np N) batched decode scheduler
rows.concept: llama.cpp slot occupancy: a request holds a slot until it finishes
rows.method: Local / edge batched serving (no-CUDA: Metal / CPU / Windows)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture reqs.json (arrival, gen_len) + N slots. Learner simulates llama.cpp continuous batching: each step decodes 1 token per busy slot, retires finished sequences, and admits waiting requests into freed slots (FIFO). Return per-step slot->seq_id occupancy. Oracle = reference slot sim. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Fork/branch continuation savings
rows.concept: Two continuations reuse a shared trunk once
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture forks.json: a shared prefix followed by K divergent continuations (agent/chat branches). Learner inserts all branches into the radix tree and returns total saved tokens (the trunk counted once, reused by each branch beyond the first). Oracle = reference tree over the forks. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: fp16 vs fp32 accumulation error
rows.concept: Precision of the attention accumulation path
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture q,k,v. Learner computes attention accumulating in fp16 and in fp32 and returns each output's rel_err vs the fp64 reference. Oracle computes the reference and both errors. Grade: reported errors match ref within tol and fp32 error < fp16 error; gate met when both hold and the fp32-path rel_err < 1e-3.

rows.title: Goodput: colocated vs disaggregated under SLO
rows.concept: Requests meeting TTFT/ITL SLOs with phase interference vs isolation
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture trace.json + SLOs + interference model (colocated: a prefill inflates concurrent decode ITL by a given factor; disaggregated: no interference). Learner returns (goodput_colocated, goodput_disagg) = count of requests meeting both SLOs. Oracle runs both reference sims. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: GQA / MQA broadcast attention
rows.concept: K/V head groups broadcast across query heads
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture q (H_q heads), k,v (H_kv < H_q heads). Learner repeats each KV head across its query-head group and attends. Oracle = reference grouped attention fp64. Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-5.

rows.title: Group batch rows into adapter segments
rows.concept: Sort rows by adapter id and emit segment boundaries
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture adapter_id per row (unsorted). Learner returns the stable sort permutation and the segment start offsets per adapter. Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match of the permutation and offsets; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Internal fragmentation: paged vs contiguous pre-alloc
rows.concept: Wasted KV slots under per-block vs max-length contiguous allocation
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture seqlens.npy, block_size B, max_len L. Learner returns (paged_waste = sum(ceil(len/B)*B - len), contig_waste = sum(L - len)). Oracle recomputes. Grade rel_err on both scalars; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: JSON-subset pushdown-automaton mask
rows.concept: Stack-based bracket matching for constrained JSON
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture a JSON-subset grammar (objects/arrays/strings/numbers) + a decode prefix. Learner runs a pushdown automaton (bracket stack) and returns the allowed next tokens (e.g. '}' only when the stack top is '{'). Oracle = reference PDA. Grade exact_match of the per-step allowed set; gate 1.0.

rows.title: K=4 vs K=8 waste tradeoff
rows.concept: More buckets reduce waste at more capture memory
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture size_histogram. Learner returns min pad waste for K=4 and K=8 (each via the DP) and the waste reduction. Oracle recomputes both. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: KV-cache transfer bytes for a request
rows.concept: KV size = 2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * seq_len * dtype_bytes
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture cfg.json (num_layers, num_kv_heads, head_dim, dtype_bytes) + seq_len. Learner returns KV transfer bytes = 2*layers*kv_heads*head_dim*seq_len*dtype_bytes. Oracle recomputes the closed form. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: KV memory and max concurrency: fp8 vs fp16
rows.concept: Bytes/token and sequences fitting a VRAM budget
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture cfg.json (layers, kv_heads, head_dim, seq_len) + VRAM budget bytes. Learner returns KV bytes/token at fp8 (1) and fp16 (2), and max concurrent sequences for each = floor(budget / (bytes_per_token*seq_len)). Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: KV memory for N contiguous slots
rows.concept: Each slot preallocates n_ctx KV (no paging)
rows.method: Local / edge batched serving (no-CUDA: Metal / CPU / Windows)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture cfg.json (layers, kv_heads, head_dim, dtype_bytes, n_ctx) + N slots. Learner returns total slot KV bytes = N * 2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * n_ctx * dtype_bytes, and compares to a paged pool sized to actual lengths. Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Launch-overhead step-time model
rows.concept: One graph launch replaces N per-kernel launches
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture per-kernel launch cost L, kernel count N, GPU compute time C. Learner returns modeled step time eager (N*L + C) vs graph (L + C) and the fraction of overhead removed. Oracle recomputes. Grade rel_err on both times and the fraction; gate < 1e-9. (Modeled counts, no wall-clock.)

rows.title: Longest cached prefix length for a new request
rows.concept: Prefix caching stops at the first diverging block
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture cache_state.json (set of cached chain hashes) + new request tokens + block_size B. Learner returns the number of leading blocks that hit before the first miss. Oracle walks the chain hash and counts consecutive membership. Grade exact_match of the integer; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Longest match length of a query against the tree
rows.concept: Walk edges token-by-token to the first mismatch
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture built_tree.json + query token sequence. Learner returns the longest prefix-match length (walk root-to-leaf matching tokens until mismatch or query end). Oracle recomputes on the reference tree. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: LoRA FLOPs: factored vs merged
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture d, r, sequence length range. Learner returns per-token FLOPs of factored apply (2*d*r + 2*r*d) vs merged apply (2*d*d after a one-time A@B merge of 2*d*d*r) and the seq length at which merging amortizes. Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match of the FLOP formulas and break-even length; gate 1.0.

rows.title: LRU eviction on the radix tree under capacity
rows.concept: Evict least-recently-used leaves while preserving shared trunks
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture access_trace.json (inserts/queries with timestamps) + capacity C tokens. Learner evicts LRU leaf tokens when total tokens exceed C, never evicting a node with live children before its children. Return (evicted_token_total, hit_rate on a held-out follow-up trace). Oracle = reference LRU-radix. Grade exact_match of both; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Mask density over a constrained decode
rows.concept: Fraction of vocab masked out per step
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture a decode trace + the FSM. Learner returns the per-step fraction of the vocabulary masked to -inf and the mean over the decode. Oracle recomputes from the FSM allowed sets. Grade rel_err vs ref; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: Max prefill tokens in any step (ITL proxy)
rows.concept: Chunking caps the worst-case decode stall
rows.method: Chunked prefill / Dynamic SplitFuse / stall-free scheduling
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture workload.json (mixed long prefills + running decodes) + budget C. Learner returns max prefill tokens processed in a single iteration with chunking ON (bounded by C) vs OFF (whole prompt in one step). Oracle recomputes both. Grade exact_match of both integers; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Mean added queue latency
rows.concept: Average wait each request spends batching
rows.method: Dynamic request batching + queue-delay scheduling (general/non-autoregressive ML)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture arrivals.npy + policy params. Learner runs the batcher and returns mean (dispatch_time - arrival_time) over all requests. Oracle recomputes from the reference sim. Grade rel_err; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: Measure padding waste of static batching
rows.concept: Token-slot waste from padding a static batch to its longest member
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture batch_lens.npy: total (prompt+gen) length per request grouped into static batches. Learner returns wasted_fraction = sum(max_len_in_batch - len)/sum(max_len_in_batch) summed over batches. Oracle recomputes from lengths. Grade rel_err vs ref scalar; gate < 1e-9. Deterministic.

rows.title: Memory: N adapters vs N full models
rows.concept: Weight bytes for shared base + rank-r adapters
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture hidden dim d, rank r, layer count, adapter count N, dtype bytes. Learner returns bytes for (1 base + N adapters of 2*d*r per layer) vs (N full copies of the base). Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Min delay-cap meeting a p99 latency SLO
rows.concept: Smallest cap keeping tail latency in budget while filling batches
rows.method: Dynamic request batching + queue-delay scheduling (general/non-autoregressive ML)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture arrivals.npy + candidate caps + p99 latency SLO. Learner returns the smallest cap whose per-request p99 (queue wait + fixed service time) <= SLO. Oracle sweeps caps with the sim. Grade exact_match of the chosen cap; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Mixed-rank SGMV
rows.concept: Adapters of differing rank in one batch
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture x (N rows), adapter_id per row, adapters with different ranks r_i (ragged A_i,B_i). Learner computes the segmented apply handling ragged ranks. Oracle = per-row loop over the correct-rank adapter (fp64). Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-5.

rows.title: Modified rejection-sampling accept step
rows.concept: Accept with prob min(1,p/q), else resample from normalize(max(p-q,0))
rows.method: Speculative decoding (draft model / EAGLE / Medusa / n-gram / MTP)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture p.npy,q.npy (target/draft distributions), draft token ids, and a fixed uniform RNG stream. Learner accepts each draft token when u <= p[t]/q[t], else emits a residual sample from normalize(max(p-q,0)) using the next RNG draw. Return the emitted token per position. Oracle = reference fixed-seed implementation. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Multi-token block verify with bonus sample
rows.concept: Accept the longest valid draft prefix, then sample a bonus token
rows.method: Speculative decoding (draft model / EAGLE / Medusa / n-gram / MTP)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture a k-token draft block with per-position p,q and an RNG stream. Learner accepts tokens left-to-right until the first rejection, then samples one bonus token from the residual (or from p after a full accept). Return (accepted_length, emitted_tokens). Oracle = reference block-verify. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: N-gram / prompt-lookup proposer
rows.method: Speculative decoding (draft model / EAGLE / Medusa / n-gram / MTP)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture sequence.npy + prompt_lookup_min/max + num_speculative_tokens. Learner finds the longest earlier occurrence of the current suffix (length in [min,max]) and proposes the following k tokens (empty if no match). Return the proposal at each step. Oracle = brute-force suffix search. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Naive exp-sum merge vs LSE merge stability
rows.concept: Why the running-max subtraction is required
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture with large-magnitude scores. Learner returns the merged output from a naive merge (sum e^{L_i} directly, no max subtraction) and from the LSE merge, plus each one's max_abs_err vs the fp64 reference. Oracle computes the reference and both errors. Grade: the LSE error must be < 1e-5 and reported errors match ref within 1e-9; gate met when LSE stable and naive error reproduced.

rows.title: Naive SDPA reference
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture q,k,v.npy for a real attention layer (fp32). Learner returns softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V. Oracle = F.scaled_dot_product_attention equivalent in fp64. Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-6.

rows.title: Order-invariance of the merge
rows.concept: Merging chunks in any order gives the identical result
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture partials for S chunks. Learner merges them in the given order and in reversed order and returns both outputs. Oracle merges in fp64. Grade max_abs_err between the two learner orders (< 1e-12) AND vs the fp64 reference (< 1e-10); gate met when both hold.

rows.title: P:D worker ratio for a balanced pipeline
rows.concept: Balance prefill vs decode throughput for an input:output length mix
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture: prefill throughput (tok/s/worker), decode throughput (tok/s/worker), mean input_len, mean output_len. Learner returns the smallest integer P:D ratio that balances tokens/s produced by prefill workers against tokens/s consumed by decode workers. Oracle computes the reduced integer ratio. Grade exact_match of (P,D); gate 1.0.

rows.title: Pack a llama_batch (tokens, pos, seq_id)
rows.concept: Interleave N sequences' tokens into one decode batch
rows.method: Local / edge batched serving (no-CUDA: Metal / CPU / Windows)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture per-slot (token, position, seq_id, wants_logits) for one decode step across N active sequences. Learner assembles the flat llama_batch arrays (token[], pos[], n_seq_id[], seq_id[][], logits[]) in slot order. Oracle = reference packer. Grade exact_match of all arrays; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Padding waste eliminated by packing
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture lens.npy. Learner returns (padded_tokens = batch*max_len, packed_tokens = sum(len), waste_fraction). Oracle recomputes. Grade rel_err on all three; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: Paged block allocator over an arrival/free trace
rows.concept: Peak block usage and admitted-request count vs contiguous
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture trace.json: (arrive_t, depart_t, seq_len) per request, pool size in blocks, block_size B, max_len L. Learner simulates a free-list allocator (alloc ceil(len/B) blocks on arrival, return on departure; reject if insufficient) and reports (peak_blocks_used, admitted_count). Also compute admitted_count under contiguous (ceil(L/B) blocks each). Oracle = reference allocator sim. Grade exact_match of all three integers; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Peak aggregate KV transfer bandwidth
rows.concept: Instantaneous KV bandwidth demand across a request trace
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture trace.json + KV-bytes-per-token. Learner computes the peak KV transfer bandwidth demanded at any instant (sum over requests whose prefill completes in that window). Oracle recomputes. Grade rel_err vs ref; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: Per-head absmax scaling
rows.concept: Each attention head gets its own scale
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture k.npy shaped (heads, seq, head_dim). Learner computes one absmax scale per head, quantizes/dequantizes per head to E4M3, returns the dequantized tensor. Oracle = reference per-head cast. Grade rel_err vs ref dequant; gate < 1e-6.

rows.title: Per-tensor KV reconstruction MSE
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture k.npy,v.npy from a real layer. Learner computes a per-tensor absmax scale, quantizes K and V to E4M3 (scaled), dequantizes, and returns reconstruction MSE for each. Oracle recomputes with the reference cast. Grade rel_err of the reported MSE vs ref; gate < 1e-6.

rows.title: Per-tensor vs per-head attention-output delta
rows.concept: Finer scaling lowers the end-to-end attention error
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture q,k,v. Learner quantizes KV per-tensor and per-head to E4M3, runs attention each way, and returns each output's rel_err vs fp32-KV attention. Oracle recomputes both. Grade: per-head delta < per-tensor delta AND reported deltas match ref within tol; gate met when both hold.

rows.title: preferred_batch_size A vs B
rows.method: Dynamic request batching + queue-delay scheduling (general/non-autoregressive ML)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture arrivals.npy + two preferred_batch_size values (same cap). Learner returns (mean_latency, throughput) for each. Oracle runs both sims. Grade rel_err on all four scalars; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: Prefill chunk count for a fixed budget
rows.method: Chunked prefill / Dynamic SplitFuse / stall-free scheduling
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture prompt_lens.npy + chunk token budget C. Learner returns per-prompt (num_chunks = ceil(len/C), last_chunk = len - (num_chunks-1)*C). Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match of both arrays; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Prefill FLOPs saved by APC
rows.concept: Compute avoided by not re-prefilling cached blocks
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture requests.json + a per-token prefill FLOP constant f (given). Learner computes saved_flops = reused_tokens * f from the APC hit accounting. Oracle recomputes. Grade rel_err vs ref scalar; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: Prefix cache hit rate over a request stream
rows.concept: Block-level reuse: computed vs reused block counts
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture requests.json: list of tokenized prompts sharing prefixes, block_size B. Learner hashes blocks (chain hash) and, walking each request left-to-right, counts a hit while the running chain hash is already in the cache, a miss (and insert) at the first divergence and onward. Return (total_reused_blocks, total_computed_blocks). Oracle = reference APC over a dict. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Radix (token-level) vs block-level reuse
rows.concept: Token granularity reuses partial-block prefixes that block hashing cannot
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture seqs.json engineered to diverge mid-block, plus block_size B. Learner returns (radix_saved_tokens, block_saved_tokens) where block-level only reuses whole matching blocks. Oracle computes both. Grade exact_match; radix_saved >= block_saved must hold; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Radix tree insert with node split
rows.concept: Split an edge/node when a new sequence diverges mid-node
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture seqs.json: token sequences inserted in order. Learner builds a radix (compressed-prefix) tree, splitting a node at the divergence point when a new insert shares only part of an edge. Return a canonical serialization (sorted (parent_path, edge_tokens) tuples). Oracle = reference radix tree. Grade exact_match of the serialization; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Rank-r LoRA vs full delta approximation
rows.concept: Best rank-r factorization of a full weight delta
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture a full delta matrix W.npy. Learner computes the optimal rank-r approximation via truncated SVD (return A=U_r*sqrt(S_r), B=sqrt(S_r)*V_r^T) and its Frobenius rel_err, and compares to a provided (A0,B0). Oracle = numpy SVD truncation error (Eckart-Young). Grade rel_err of the reported best error vs the SVD reference; gate < 1e-6 and the learner error must not beat Eckart-Young.

rows.title: Reconstruct global attention weights from per-chunk LSE
rows.concept: Recover each token's softmax weight from partial statistics
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture per-chunk partial outputs + LSEs + the raw chunk scores. Learner reconstructs the global softmax weight assigned to each KV token: w_j = e^{score_j - m} / sum_all e^{score - m}. Oracle computes weights directly from full scores in fp64. Grade rel_err over the weight vector; gate < 1e-6.

rows.title: Regex FSM allowed-token mask
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture a regex over a small char vocabulary + a decode prefix. Learner compiles the regex to a DFA and, at each step, returns the set of vocab tokens that keep a path to an accept state (Brzozowski derivative). Oracle = reference derivative FSM. Grade exact_match of the per-step allowed set; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Reset RoPE position ids at boundaries
rows.concept: Positions restart per sequence in a packed buffer
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture packed q,k + cu_seqlens. Learner builds per-token position ids that restart at 0 for each segment, applies RoPE, and attends. Oracle applies RoPE per unpacked sequence (positions 0..len_i-1) and attends per sequence. Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-5.

rows.title: Round a batch up to the nearest captured bucket
rows.concept: Static-shape capture: pad to the next captured size
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture captured_sizes (sorted) + batch sizes. Learner returns per-batch (chosen_bucket = smallest captured >= batch, padded_rows = bucket-batch); if batch exceeds the max bucket, mark eager (-1). Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Route requests to prefill/decode pools
rows.concept: Disaggregated scheduler assigns phases to separate workers
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture trace.json (arrivals, prompt_len, gen_len) + P prefill workers + D decode workers, each with a service-time model. Learner simulates least-loaded assignment of prefill and decode phases and returns per-worker assigned-request lists. Oracle = reference sim. Grade exact_match of assignments; gate 1.0.

rows.title: S-way split-KV merge
rows.how_to_grade: Same tensors, split KV into S chunks (S given). Learner merges all S partials with the numerically-stable rescale. Oracle = full SDPA fp64. Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-5.

rows.title: SGMV: per-row adapter selection
rows.concept: Segmented gather matmul over a mixed-adapter batch
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture x (N rows), adapter_id per row, a bank of (A_i,B_i,scale_i) all rank r. Learner applies each row's selected adapter (segmented gather matmul). Oracle applies each row's adapter in a Python loop (fp64). Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-5.

rows.title: Shared-prefix block table (copy-on-write)
rows.concept: Two sequences alias the same physical blocks for a common prefix
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture two token-id arrays sharing a P-token prefix + block_size B. Learner builds both block_tables so prefix blocks point to the SAME physical block ids, allocates only divergent tail blocks, and returns the count of unique physical blocks used. Oracle = ceil(P/B) shared + ceil(tail_i/B) each. Grade exact_match of the physical-block count and the two block_tables; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Simulate continuous-batching active set under max_num_seqs
rows.concept: Iteration-level admission: fill freed slots from the waiting queue
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture reqs.json: (arrival_iter, prompt_len, gen_len) per request, plus max_num_seqs S. Learner runs a discrete-event sim: each iteration decodes 1 token per active seq, retires seqs that hit gen_len, then admits waiting arrivals into free slots (FIFO) up to S. Output the active-seq-id list per iteration. Oracle = reference sim. Grade exact_match of the full per-iteration active-set sequence; gate 1.0. Deterministic.

rows.title: Single-adapter LoRA delta
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture x.npy, base output, A.npy (d x r), B.npy (r x d), scale. Learner returns base + scale*(x@A)@B. Oracle recomputes in fp64. Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-5.

rows.title: Slot-based vs paged admission
rows.concept: Max concurrency under per-slot n_ctx preallocation vs paged
rows.method: Local / edge batched serving (no-CUDA: Metal / CPU / Windows)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture length distribution + memory budget + n_ctx + block_size. Learner returns max concurrent requests under contiguous per-slot n_ctx allocation vs a paged pool (ceil(len/B) blocks). Oracle recomputes both. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Speedup vs acceptance-rate model
rows.method: Speculative decoding (draft model / EAGLE / Medusa / n-gram / MTP)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture per-step acceptance rate alpha, block length k, draft:target cost ratio c. Learner returns expected accepted tokens per verification = (1-alpha^{k+1})/(1-alpha) and the speedup vs vanilla; compare two draft configs. Oracle recomputes the closed form. Grade rel_err on both configs; gate < 1e-9.

rows.title: Split count vs parallel work
rows.concept: Choosing S: added combine cost vs decode parallelism
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture (batch, query_rows, kv_len) + a work model (parallel tiles = batch*query_rows*S, combine cost proportional to S). Learner returns effective parallel work for a list of S and the S that maximizes work minus combine penalty. Oracle recomputes from the model. Grade exact_match of the chosen S and the work array; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Static request-level batching makespan
rows.concept: Batch-blocking: a new batch cannot start until the whole prior batch drains
rows.how_to_grade: Same reqs.json + fixed batch size S. Learner simulates static batching: form a batch of up to S arrived requests, run until the LONGEST finishes (short ones idle-pad), only then form the next batch. Return makespan (total iterations) and per-batch iteration counts. Oracle = reference static sim. Grade exact_match of makespan + counts; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Streaming softmax running max/sum
rows.concept: Online softmax over a vector processed in chunks
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture scores.npy (fp32). Learner computes softmax by streaming chunks, maintaining running max m and running sum l with rescale, then normalizing. Oracle = one-pass numpy softmax in fp64. Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-6.

rows.title: Throughput vs budget saturation point
rows.concept: Tokens processed per iteration as a function of budget
rows.method: Chunked prefill / Dynamic SplitFuse / stall-free scheduling
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture workload.json. Learner returns tokens-processed-per-iteration for a set of budgets and the smallest budget at which per-iteration throughput saturates (no further gain). Oracle recomputes via the packer. Grade rel_err on the throughput curve and exact_match on the saturation budget; gate met when rel_err < 1e-9 and budget matches.

rows.title: Throughput vs delay-cap curve
rows.concept: Achieved batch size and throughput as the cap varies
rows.method: Dynamic request batching + queue-delay scheduling (general/non-autoregressive ML)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture arrivals.npy + a set of max_queue_delay values + fixed service model. Learner returns mean achieved batch size and throughput (requests per service-time) per cap. Oracle recomputes via the sim. Grade rel_err on the curves; gate < 1e-9. (No wall-clock; service time is a fixed model constant.)

rows.title: Tiled flash-attention forward (no NxN matrix)
rows.how_to_grade: Same q,k,v. Learner implements block-tiled attention with running max/sum, never materializing the full score matrix. Oracle = full SDPA fp64. Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-4.

rows.title: Total padding waste over a batch-size histogram
rows.concept: Sum of pad rows across a workload
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture size_histogram (count per batch size) + captured buckets. Learner returns total padded rows = sum over sizes of count*(bucket-size) for captured sizes. Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Total prefix tokens saved
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture seqs.json. Learner inserts sequentially; for each insert, tokens matched against existing tree edges are 'saved' (not recomputed), the rest are 'computed'. Return (total_saved, total_computed). Oracle = reference radix tree. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: Transfer-vs-recompute break-even length
rows.concept: Seq length above which shipping KV beats recomputing prefill
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture: KV-bytes-per-token, link bandwidth (B/s), prefill throughput (tokens/s) on the decode node. Learner returns the seq_len where transfer_time(len) == recompute_time(len). Oracle solves the linear equation. Grade rel_err vs ref; gate < 1e-6.

rows.title: Two-chunk split-KV log-sum-exp merge
rows.concept: Merge two partial attentions via the running-max rescale
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture q.npy,k.npy,v.npy (one decode query, long KV). Learner splits KV into 2 chunks, computes each chunk's partial output O_i and log-sum-exp L_i, then merges O = (O_1*e^{L_1-m} + O_2*e^{L_2-m}) / (e^{L_1-m}+e^{L_2-m}). Oracle = full single-pass SDPA in fp64. Grade max_abs_err; gate < 1e-5.

rows.title: Unbiasedness: output histogram equals target
rows.concept: Speculative sampling preserves the target distribution
rows.method: Speculative decoding (draft model / EAGLE / Medusa / n-gram / MTP)
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture p,q + seed + N samples. Learner runs the accept/resample loop N times and returns the empirical token histogram. Oracle = the target distribution p. Grade rel_err of histogram vs p within Monte-Carlo tolerance (rel_err < 3*sqrt(1/N) per bin); gate met when within CI.

rows.title: Would this pair share a prefix node?
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture pairs.json of token sequences. Learner labels each pair 'shares prefix' iff their first tokens agree (common prefix length > 0). Oracle recomputes. Grade exact_match; gate 1.0.

rows.title: 2:4 magnitude-prune reconstruction MSE
rows.concept: Accuracy cost of the constraint: MSE between the 2:4-masked weight and the dense weight
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle applies the 2:4 magnitude mask and computes the reconstruction MSE vs the dense weight. Compare the student's MSE against the recomputed value.

rows.title: 2:4 prune + compressed (values+2-bit idx) + matmul
rows.concept: Compressed representation: store the 2 kept values plus 2-bit indices per group and reconstruct the masked matmul
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle builds the 2:4 mask, computes (W*mask) @ X in numpy, and the compressed (values, indices) form. Compare the student's mask (exact) and the reconstructed matmul output within tolerance.

rows.title: 8da4w vs 8-bit weight-only error and size
rows.concept: On-device tradeoff: 8da4w (int8 act x int4 weight) vs 8-bit weight-only on accuracy and stored size
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes both schemes' layer error and stored size on a real Linear. Compare the student's error pair, size ratios, and the reported tradeoff against the recomputed values.

rows.title: act-order (desc_act) column reordering reduces error
rows.concept: Activation-order heuristic: quantize columns in decreasing diag(H) order, then invert the permutation, lowering final error
rows.method: GPTQ post-training weight quant (W4A16, layer-wise inverse-Hessian)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the desc_act permutation from diag(H), runs GPTQ in that order, un-permutes, and records the resulting layer error. Compare the student's permutation (exact) and final error (rel_err) against the oracle, and that it beats the natural-order error.

rows.title: Affine group quant/dequant matches mlx
rows.concept: MLX affine quant: w_q = round((w-bias)/scale) clamped, w_hat = scale*w_q + bias, per group of 64
rows.method: MLX affine group quantization (Apple silicon export)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle implements the numpy affine group quant matching mlx.core.quantize/dequantize. Compare the student's integer codes exactly and reconstruction (max_abs_err) on real weight rows.

rows.title: Apply per-channel scale, 4-bit quant, fold reciprocal
rows.concept: AWQ transform for a fixed scale: W' = Q(W diag(s)), output = W' diag(1/s) X, preserving math while easing weight quant
rows.method: AWQ activation-aware weight quant (W4A16, per-channel scale search)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle applies a given per-channel scale, group-wise fake-quantizes to 4-bit, folds 1/s into activations, and computes the layer output in numpy. Compare the student's output within tolerance.

rows.title: AWQ vs plain RTN 4-bit on a salient-heavy weight
rows.concept: Show the scaling benefit: error reduction of AWQ-scaled 4-bit vs plain RTN 4-bit on a weight with salient channels
rows.method: AWQ activation-aware weight quant (W4A16, per-channel scale search)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes both layer errors and their ratio on the same fixture. Compare the student's reported error pair and ratio against the recomputed values.

rows.title: Baseline RTN 4-bit layer-output MSE
rows.concept: Round-to-nearest 4-bit per-group quant as the accuracy floor GPTQ must beat: measure ||WX - Q(W)X||
rows.method: GPTQ post-training weight quant (W4A16, layer-wise inverse-Hessian)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle does per-group RTN 4-bit quant of a real weight and computes the layer-output MSE against the calibration activations. Compare the student's MSE against the recomputed value.

rows.title: Build the damped inverse Hessian and its Cholesky
rows.concept: H = 2 X X^T + lambda*mean(diag(H))*I; GPTQ works from the Cholesky of H^-1
rows.method: GPTQ post-training weight quant (W4A16, layer-wise inverse-Hessian)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle builds H from real calibration activations, applies the standard damping, and computes H^-1 (and its Cholesky) via numpy linalg. Compare the student's matrix entries within tolerance.

rows.title: Classify values: exact, subnormal, or saturated in e4m3
rows.concept: e4m3fn ranges: values >448 saturate, tiny values (<~2^-9) fall into subnormals/zero, the rest are normal
rows.method: FP8 post-training quant (W8A8-FP8, e4m3) for Hopper/Ada/Blackwell
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle classifies each input value by the e4m3fn range boundaries. Compare the student's per-value label vector exactly on adversarial magnitudes.

rows.title: Combine two block softmax stats (online softmax lemma)
rows.concept: Online softmax: given per-block (m,l,o) running stats, merge to global stats with the exp(m_old-m_new) rescaling
rows.method: Fused attention backend selection (SDPA / FlashAttention / FlexAttention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the numerically-stable combine of two blocks' (max, denom, weighted-value) into the global softmax result. Compare the student's merged (l,o) against the oracle within tolerance.

rows.title: Compare DRAM traffic: fused vs unfused elementwise chain
rows.concept: Quantify memory-traffic reduction from fusion: fused chain reads/writes 2N bytes vs unfused K+1 buffer round-trips
rows.method: Graph capture + JIT kernel codegen (torch.compile / TorchInductor)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes analytic DRAM bytes for both strategies given N elements, K ops, and dtype size (unfused = (K+1) full-tensor read/writes per the naive schedule; fused = one read + one write). Compare the student's two byte counts against the recomputed values.

rows.title: Compute 8da4w Linear size / bits-per-param
rows.concept: PTE sizing: int4 weights plus FP16 per-group scales -> effective bits/param and size ratio vs fp16
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the packed weight bytes plus scale overhead for given shape and group size, and the ratio vs the fp16 weight. Compare the student's bits/param and size_ratio against the recomputed values.

rows.title: Compute NF4 bits/param with and without double-quant
rows.concept: Bit-budget accounting: 4 + 32/block (fp32 absmax) vs 4 + 8/block1 + 32/(block1*block2) with nested quant
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes both analytic bits/param values from the block sizes. Compare the student's two numbers against the recomputed values within a small tolerance.

rows.title: Compute the blockwise absmax (block=64)
rows.concept: Blockwise scaling: per-block absmax constant c = max|w| that normalizes each 64-element block before code lookup
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle reshapes a real weight into 64-element blocks and takes per-block max|w|. Compare the student's absmax vector within fp tolerance.

rows.title: Compute the folded weight-blob size of the .pt2 artifact
rows.concept: Artifact sizing: sum the bytes of all folded constants/params at their stored dtypes to get the packaged weight-blob size
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle sums numel*dtype_bytes over the constant/param set of a real module and forms the ratio vs the fp32 baseline. Compare the student's total byte count and size_ratio against the recomputed values.

rows.title: Compute the max-calibration amax and its clipping error
rows.concept: Max calibrator: amax = max|X| accumulated over calibration batches; then measure the resulting quant MSE
rows.method: TensorRT-LLM engine build (+ NVIDIA ModelOpt quantization)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle accumulates max|X| across provided calibration batches, quantizes with scale=amax/127, and computes the reconstruction MSE. Compare the student's amax and MSE against the recomputed values.

rows.title: Compute the MXFP4 shared E8M0 block scale (block=32)
rows.concept: OCP MX shared exponent: a block of 32 shares a power-of-two E8M0 scale chosen so elements fit the e2m1 max (6.0)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the E8M0 exponent per the OCP MXFP4 rule (from block amax) for real weight blocks. Compare the student's integer exponent per block exactly.

rows.title: Compute the per-channel activation scale statistic
rows.concept: s_X_j = mean over tokens of |X_j|, the per-input-channel importance vector AWQ's scale is built from
rows.method: AWQ activation-aware weight quant (W4A16, per-channel scale search)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the per-channel mean-abs activation vector in numpy on real activations. Compare the student's vector within fp tolerance.

rows.title: Compute the per-channel migration scale s_j
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes s in numpy for a given alpha from real per-channel activation and weight maxima. Compare the student's scale vector within fp tolerance.

rows.title: Constant-fold frozen weights into a baked constant
rows.concept: Weight/constant folding at package time: a subgraph with all-constant inputs (weight*scale+bias) folds to one precomputed tensor
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the folded constant in numpy from the real frozen weights/constants and counts how many nodes collapse. Compare the student's folded tensor within fp tolerance and the folded-node count.

rows.title: Count Dynamo graph breaks in a traced function
rows.concept: Enumerate the events that force a graph break (.item(), data-dependent branch, unsupported builtin, print/side-effect) and count resulting subgraphs
rows.method: Graph capture + JIT kernel codegen (torch.compile / TorchInductor)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle walks a provided op/event trace, applies the break-trigger rules, and computes break_count and subgraph_count. Compare the student's two integers against the oracle-derived counts (never hardcoded; recomputed from the trace).

rows.title: Decompose SDPA into ONNX primitives and match fused attention
rows.concept: Attention lowering: express scaled_dot_product_attention as MatMul/Div/Add(mask)/Softmax/MatMul (base opset has no fused SDPA) with identical numerics
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes naive softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d)+mask)V in numpy on real Q,K,V. Compare the student's primitive-decomposition output within fp tolerance across causal and non-causal masks.

rows.title: Double-quantize the NF4 absmax constants
rows.concept: QLoRA double quantization: the per-block FP32 absmax constants are themselves 8-bit blockwise quantized (~0.37 bit/param saved)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes both quantization levels in numpy (8-bit quant of the absmax constants) and the full two-level dequant plus analytic bits/param. Compare the student's reconstructed weights (max_abs_err) and the bits/param number.

rows.title: e4m3 vs e5m2 vs int8 error on an outlier weight
rows.concept: Format tradeoff: on heavy-tailed data, e4m3's wider mantissa vs e5m2's wider range vs INT8's uniform grid
rows.method: FP8 post-training quant (W8A8-FP8, e4m3) for Hopper/Ada/Blackwell
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes the same real weight with all three formats (each with its best per-tensor scale) and computes each error plus the argmin. Compare the student's three errors and the reported lowest-error format.

rows.title: e4m3fn encode/decode (RNE + saturation)
rows.concept: FP8 e4m3fn codec: 1-4-3 layout, subnormals, round-to-nearest-even, saturate to +/-448 (no inf/nan)
rows.method: FP8 post-training quant (W8A8-FP8, e4m3) for Hopper/Ada/Blackwell
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle is a reference bit-level e4m3fn codec in numpy. Compare the student's encoded bytes exactly and decoded values (max_abs_err) on adversarial magnitudes (denormals, values near 448, overflow).

rows.title: e5m2 encode/decode (with inf/nan)
rows.concept: The other FP8 format: 1-5-2 layout, wider exponent, RNE, supports inf/nan (unlike e4m3fn)
rows.method: FP8 post-training quant (W8A8-FP8, e4m3) for Hopper/Ada/Blackwell
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle is a reference bit-level e5m2 codec in numpy including inf/nan handling. Compare the student's encoded bytes exactly and decoded values, including overflow-to-inf cases.

rows.title: Effective bits/weight including scale+bias overhead
rows.concept: Storage accounting: b + (16+16)/group_size effective bits when scale and bias are FP16 per group
rows.method: MLX affine group quantization (Apple silicon export)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the analytic effective bits/weight from b and group_size. Compare the student's number against the recomputed value within a small tolerance.

rows.title: Epilogue-fuse bias-add + activation into a matmul
rows.concept: Epilogue fusion: C = act(A@B + bias) computed as one kernel instead of matmul then separate pointwise passes
rows.method: Graph capture + JIT kernel codegen (torch.compile / TorchInductor)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes act(A@B + bias) in numpy on real weight/activation fixtures. Student's fused-epilogue result is compared within fp tolerance; a separate check confirms no standalone post-matmul buffer for the bias/activation stage.

rows.title: Fix 2:4 selection done per-row instead of per-group-of-4
rows.concept: Debugging: a buggy variant keeps the global top-half of each row, violating the strict 2-of-every-4 constraint
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle builds the correct per-group-of-4 mask. Compare the student's fixed mask against the correct reference exactly and confirm every group of 4 keeps exactly 2.

rows.title: Fix a flash accumulator missing the max-update rescale
rows.concept: Debugging: when the running max grows, the accumulator must be multiplied by exp(m_old - m_new); a bug omits it
rows.method: Fused attention backend selection (SDPA / FlashAttention / FlexAttention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the correct flash output equal to naive attention. Compare the student's fixed implementation against the reference within tolerance and confirm the unfixed version diverged.

rows.title: Fix a GPTQ loop that skips the remaining-column update
rows.concept: Debugging: a broken variant quantizes each column independently (degenerates to RTN) or uses H instead of H^-1
rows.method: GPTQ post-training weight quant (W4A16, layer-wise inverse-Hessian)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle produces the correct GPTQ output on the fixture. Compare the student's fixed implementation's weights/output against the correct reference (rel_err) and confirm it diverges from the RTN degenerate result.

rows.title: Fix a max-calibration scale wrecked by one outlier
rows.concept: Calibration debugging: a lone huge activation inflates amax so normal values underflow; switch max->percentile to recover
rows.method: TensorRT-LLM engine build (+ NVIDIA ModelOpt quantization)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the percentile-based amax and the improved reconstruction error on the outlier-contaminated calibration set. Compare the student's corrected amax (exact within tol) and improved error against the oracle.

rows.title: Fix a per-tensor activation scale that should be per-token
rows.concept: Debugging: a per-tensor activation scale lets one outlier token dominate and underflows the rest; fix to per-token
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the correct per-token 8da4w output on an outlier-heavy activation batch. Compare the student's fixed per-token output against the correct reference and confirm the per-tensor version had larger error.

rows.title: Fix a scale folded on the wrong side
rows.concept: Debugging: an AWQ impl scales W but never folds 1/s into activations (or folds it back into weights), breaking the equivalence
rows.method: AWQ activation-aware weight quant (W4A16, per-channel scale search)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the correct folded output. Compare the student's fixed output against the correct reference within tolerance and confirm the pre-fix version diverged.

rows.title: Fix a too-narrow dynamic-shape range that fails at runtime
rows.concept: Dynamic-shape spec debugging: a Dim(min,max) baked too tight makes a valid input violate a guard at load/run time
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle determines which guard the failing input violates and the minimal corrected (min,max) range that admits it, then re-runs to get the reference output. Compare the student's corrected range and the re-run output (max_abs_err) against the oracle.

rows.title: Fix a wrong Transpose perm that corrupts the export
rows.concept: Export debugging: an emitted Transpose has an incorrect permutation so ORT output diverges from the torch reference
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle derives the correct permutation that makes the exported subgraph output equal the torch reference on real fixtures. Compare the student's corrected perm (exact) and the re-run output (max_abs_err) against the oracle.

rows.title: Fix an inverted scale direction
rows.concept: Debugging: an impl folds diag(s) into activations and diag(1/s) into weights (backwards), amplifying rather than migrating outliers
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the correctly migrated tensors and their reduced activation range. Compare the student's fixed direction against the correct reference (folded product ~0 error) and confirm the range reduction now holds.

rows.title: Fix the off-by-one scale denominator
rows.concept: Debugging: a buggy scale=(max-min)/2^b instead of /(2^b-1) misplaces the top level and inflates error
rows.method: MLX affine group quantization (Apple silicon export)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the correct affine quant with the /(2^b-1) denominator. Compare the student's fixed reconstruction against the correct reference and confirm the buggy version had larger error.

rows.title: Flag export-incompatible ops (guard/break sources)
