rows.concept: Identify ops that block a clean torch.export: data-dependent (.item, nonzero, bool(tensor)), in-place mutation, python side-effects
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle rule-labels each op in a given graph as export-safe or export-blocking by category. Compare the student's per-op label vector against the oracle-derived labels.

rows.title: Flag the outlier activation channels SmoothQuant targets
rows.concept: Identify per-channel activation outliers (max|X_j| far above the channel median) that break naive INT8 activation quant
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-channel max|X| and flags channels exceeding a factor*median threshold. Compare the student's flagged index set exactly.

rows.title: Flash backward (dQ, dK, dV) with recomputation
rows.concept: FA2 backward: recompute S from stored logsumexp rather than storing the full matrix, then form the gradient blocks
rows.method: Fused attention backend selection (SDPA / FlashAttention / FlexAttention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle uses autograd on the naive attention forward to get reference dQ/dK/dV. Compare the student's recomputation-based gradients within tolerance on random fixtures (causal and non-causal).

rows.title: Flash forward via online softmax (no NxN buffer)
rows.concept: Tiled attention with running max, denominator, and rescaled accumulator; never materialize the full score matrix
rows.method: Fused attention backend selection (SDPA / FlashAttention / FlexAttention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes naive softmax-attention in numpy. The student's tiled implementation must match within fp tolerance across seq lengths and block sizes, and an instrumentation check confirms no O(N^2) score buffer is allocated.

rows.title: Flatten pytree inputs per the ExportedProgram signature
rows.concept: Graph signature: flatten a structured (dict/list/tensor) input into the flat positional call order (params, buffers, user inputs) the packaged callable expects
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle flattens the structured input via the provided input_spec/signature ordering. Compare the student's flat argument list order and each tensor's contents against the oracle flattening.

rows.title: FlexAttention score_mod (ALiBi / soft-cap / sliding-window)
rows.concept: FlexAttention: apply a per-(query,key) additive/functional score modification before softmax and match the reference
rows.method: Fused attention backend selection (SDPA / FlashAttention / FlexAttention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle applies the same score_mod (e.g. ALiBi bias, tanh soft-cap, or sliding-window mask) inside naive attention in numpy. Compare the student's output within tolerance for each mod variant.

rows.title: Fold Conv/Linear + BatchNorm into one layer
rows.concept: BN folding (a core TRT fusion): W' = gamma*W/sqrt(var+eps), b' = gamma*(b-mean)/sqrt(var+eps) + beta
rows.method: TensorRT-LLM engine build (+ NVIDIA ModelOpt quantization)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the folded W',b' and the layer output in numpy from real weights and BN params. Compare the student's folded params and output within fp tolerance.

rows.title: Fold diag(1/s) into X, diag(s) into W, prove equivalence
rows.concept: Migration folding: W X = (W diag(s)) (diag(1/s) X) exactly, while activation dynamic range shrinks
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle verifies the folded matmul equals the original to float tolerance and reports the per-channel range-reduction ratio max|X|/max|X diag(1/s)|. Compare the student's folded product (must be ~0 error) and range-reduction stats.

rows.title: FP4 (e2m1) blockwise quant/dequant
rows.concept: bitsandbytes FP4: 16 signed e2m1 levels (not the NF4 quantiles), same blockwise absmax normalization
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle enumerates the FP4/e2m1 level set, block-normalizes, and maps each value to the nearest level. Compare the student's codes exactly and dequant (max_abs_err), and confirm it differs from the NF4 mapping on the same data.

rows.title: Full 8da4w linear matches reference
rows.concept: 8da4w end-to-end: int8 per-token activations x int4 per-group weights, integer matmul with dual (per-token, per-group) dequant
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs the full 8da4w linear in numpy (quantize both operands, integer matmul, apply both scale sets). Compare the student's output against the 8da4w oracle within tolerance.

rows.title: Full alpha grid search picks the best scale
rows.concept: AWQ core: s = s_X^alpha searched over a 20-point alpha grid, choosing the alpha minimizing quantized-layer output error
rows.method: AWQ activation-aware weight quant (W4A16, per-channel scale search)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle enumerates the same 20-alpha grid in numpy, computes ||WX - Q(W diag(s))diag(1/s)X|| for each, and returns the argmin. Compare the student's selected alpha index and the full per-alpha loss curve.

rows.title: Full GPTQ column loop matches reference W_q and output
rows.concept: End-to-end layer-wise GPTQ: left-to-right per-group quantize with lazy-batched inverse-Hessian error propagation
rows.method: GPTQ post-training weight quant (W4A16, layer-wise inverse-Hessian)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs a reference GPTQ in pure numpy (H from X, Cholesky of damped inverse, block update) on fixed W,X. Compare the student's quantized weight entries and the reconstructed layer output ||Q(W)X|| within tolerance.

rows.title: Functionalize in-place ops to match eager output
rows.concept: Functionalization: rewrite add_/relu_/copy_ as out-of-place equivalents preserving value semantics without mutating inputs
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs the equivalent functional program in numpy on real fixtures and records the final output plus the (unchanged) input tensors. Compare the student's output within tolerance AND assert the original input tensors are byte-unmodified.

rows.title: Fuse an elementwise op chain into a single-pass kernel
rows.concept: Vertical pointwise fusion: compose a chain of elementwise ops in one traversal producing output identical to the op-by-op reference
rows.method: Graph capture + JIT kernel codegen (torch.compile / TorchInductor)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle composes the given elementwise op sequence sequentially in numpy on real activation fixtures. Student returns the fused single-pass output; compare within fp tolerance and assert at most one intermediate buffer was materialized (buffer-count check from an instrumented trace).

rows.title: Fuse the LayerNorm subgraph into one LayerNormalization op
rows.concept: ORT graph fusion: detect the ReduceMean/Sub/Pow/ReduceMean/Add/Sqrt/Div/Mul/Add pattern and replace it with a single fused op of identical output
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes true LayerNorm (mean/var over the axis, affine) on real hidden-state fixtures. Compare the student's fused-op output within tolerance and require the reported fused-node span to match the oracle's detected subgraph node set.

rows.title: GPTQ vs RTN error-reduction ratio
rows.concept: Quantify GPTQ's benefit: ||WX - Q_gptq(W)X|| / ||WX - Q_rtn(W)X|| on the same weight
rows.method: GPTQ post-training weight quant (W4A16, layer-wise inverse-Hessian)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes both layer errors and their ratio on a real weight/activation fixture. Compare the student's reported ratio against the recomputed value.

rows.title: GQA/MQA attention with KV-head broadcast
rows.concept: Grouped-query attention: fewer KV heads than query heads, each KV head shared across a group of query heads
rows.method: Fused attention backend selection (SDPA / FlashAttention / FlexAttention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle repeats/broadcasts the KV heads across query-head groups and computes attention in numpy. Compare the student's GQA output within tolerance for several group ratios.

rows.title: Identify the salient (top-1%) input channels
rows.concept: AWQ saliency: rank input channels by activation magnitude s_X = mean|X| and mark the top 1% as salient
rows.method: AWQ activation-aware weight quant (W4A16, per-channel scale search)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-channel s_X over real calibration activations and returns the top-1% channel index set. Compare the student's index set exactly.

rows.title: imatrix-weighted scale search (make_qx_quants)
rows.concept: Importance-matrix quant: search candidate block scales minimizing the importance-weighted error sum w_i (x_i - d*q_i)^2
rows.method: GGUF k-quant export (llama.cpp) with importance matrix
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle replicates ggml's make_qx_quants candidate-scale RMSE search using a provided per-weight importance vector, returning the chosen scale and codes. Compare the student's selected scale (argmin over the candidate set) and codes against the oracle.

rows.title: Implement ONNX DynamicQuantizeLinear (uint8) exactly
rows.concept: ONNX DynamicQuantizeLinear: scale = (max(0,amax)-min(0,amin))/255, zero_point = round(saturate_uint8(-amin/scale)), y = saturate_uint8(round(x/scale)+zp)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle implements the ONNX spec's exact integer/rounding math in numpy on real activation tensors. Compare the student's scale, zero_point, and every uint8 code bit-exactly against the oracle.

rows.title: Implement ONNX Gemm op semantics (alpha, beta, transA, transB)
rows.concept: ONNX Gemm: Y = alpha * (A or A^T) @ (B or B^T) + beta * C with optional broadcasting of C
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes Y per the ONNX Gemm spec in numpy across several (transA,transB,alpha,beta) combos on real matrices. Compare the student's Y within fp tolerance for every flag combination.

rows.title: Implement the percentile (99.9%) activation calibrator
rows.concept: Percentile calibrator: amax is the 99.9th percentile of the collected |activation| magnitudes, clipping rare outliers
rows.method: TensorRT-LLM engine build (+ NVIDIA ModelOpt quantization)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle collects the |X| distribution over calibration data and takes the 99.9 percentile as amax. Compare the student's selected amax (rel_err) and the resulting quant error against the oracle.

rows.title: Implement the TensorRT entropy (KL) calibrator threshold
rows.concept: IInt8EntropyCalibrator2: over a |X| histogram, for each candidate threshold clip+requantize the reference into 128 bins and pick the threshold minimizing KL divergence
rows.method: TensorRT-LLM engine build (+ NVIDIA ModelOpt quantization)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle builds a 2048-bin histogram of |X|, and for each candidate threshold computes KL(reference || requantized-to-128-bins), returning the argmin bin. Compare the student's chosen threshold bin index and the per-candidate KL curve against the oracle.

rows.title: int4 groupwise (group=32) symmetric weight quant
rows.concept: 8da4w weight half: per 32-group symmetric int4 quant, scale = group_amax/8, codes clamped to -8..7
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-group scales and int4 codes in numpy on a real weight. Compare the student's codes exactly and dequant within tolerance.

rows.title: int4 weight-only groupwise (group=32) asymmetric
rows.concept: torchao Int4WeightOnly: per-group scale+zero asymmetric 4-bit weight quant, dequant then matmul in bf16 activations
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-group scale/zero, 4-bit codes, dequant, and the matmul in numpy on a real weight. Compare the student's codes exactly and matmul output (max_abs_err).

rows.title: int8 dynamic-act (per-token) x int8 weight (per-channel) W8A8
rows.concept: torchao int8 dynamic-activation path: per-token activation scale, per-output-channel weight scale, int32 matmul, dequant
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes activations per-row and weights per-column to int8, does an int32 matmul, and dequants with the outer product of scales. Compare the student's output within fp tolerance on real fixtures.

rows.title: INT8 quant error with vs without SmoothQuant
rows.concept: Show the payoff: W8A8 quant error on outlier-heavy activations, smoothed vs raw
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the W8A8 layer error for both the raw and the migrated tensors and their ratio. Compare the student's reported errors and improvement ratio against the recomputed values.

rows.title: KV memory saving ratio + attention output error
rows.concept: The core tradeoff: fp16 vs fp8 KV byte ratio and the induced attention-output error
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the KV byte ratio (2x) and the attention-output max_abs_err from FP8 KV vs fp16 KV. Compare the student's size_ratio and error against the recomputed values.

rows.title: Magnitude 2:4 vs SparseGPT 2:4 error
rows.concept: Pruning-quality gap: layer-output error of naive magnitude 2:4 vs Hessian-aware SparseGPT 2:4
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes both methods' layer-output error and their ratio on the same weight/activation fixture. Compare the student's error pair and improvement ratio against the recomputed values.

rows.title: Map PyTorch ops to native ONNX ops vs decompositions
rows.concept: Op coverage: classify which torch ops have a direct ONNX op vs which must be decomposed into primitives at export
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle labels each op in a given list as direct-onnx or needs-decomposition using a reference opset table. Compare the student's per-op label vector.

rows.title: MLX affine (asymmetric) vs symmetric absmax int4
rows.concept: Asymmetric vs symmetric: min/max affine grid vs absmax symmetric grid error on a skewed weight
rows.method: MLX affine group quantization (Apple silicon export)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes the same real weight both ways and computes each reconstruction error plus the argmin. Compare the student's two errors and the reported lower-error scheme.

rows.title: MXFP4 (blk32) vs NVFP4 (blk16) reconstruction error
rows.concept: Block-size/scale-precision tradeoff: NVFP4's smaller blocks + fp8 scale vs MXFP4's power-of-two scale
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes the same real weight with both schemes and computes each reconstruction error and the argmin. Compare the student's two errors and the reported lower-error scheme.

rows.title: MXFP4 quant/dequant (block=32, e2m1 + E8M0)
rows.concept: MXFP4: divide each 32-block by its 2^scale, quantize elements to nearest e2m1, dequant = code * 2^scale
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle implements the OCP MXFP4 quant/dequant in numpy. Compare the student's e2m1 codes exactly and reconstruction (max_abs_err) on real weight blocks.

rows.title: NF4 quantize/dequant matches the reference codebook
rows.concept: 4-bit NormalFloat: fixed 16-level codebook from the quantiles of a standard normal, blockwise absmax normalize, argmin to nearest level
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle uses the 16 NF4 quantile levels, per-block absmax-normalizes, argmins to the nearest level for the code, and dequants = level*absmax. Compare the student's 4-bit codes bit-exactly and reconstruction (max_abs_err) on random and real Linear-weight fixtures.

rows.title: NF4 vs FP4 vs int4-RTN on a normal weight
rows.concept: Codebook choice matters: NF4 should reconstruct near-Gaussian weights best vs FP4 and uniform int4
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes the same real weight with all three schemes and computes each reconstruction error plus the argmin winner. Compare the student's three errors and the reported best scheme.

rows.title: NVFP4 two-level scaling (block=16, e4m3 block-scale + fp32 global)
rows.concept: NVFP4: per-16 block scale stored in e4m3 times a per-tensor fp32 scale, with e2m1 elements
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the per-tensor fp32 scale, the per-block e4m3 scales, quantizes elements to e2m1, and reconstructs. Compare the student's e2m1 codes (exact), block scales, and reconstruction (max_abs_err).

rows.title: One OBQ column update with error propagation
rows.concept: Single GPTQ step: quantize column i, err = (w_i - q_i)/[H^-1]_ii, then W[:,i+1:] -= outer(err, H^-1[i, i+1:])
rows.method: GPTQ post-training weight quant (W4A16, layer-wise inverse-Hessian)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle performs exactly one column quantize + error-propagation step from a fixed W and H^-1 fixture. Compare the student's quantized column and the updated remaining-column block within tolerance.

rows.title: Optimal per-tensor scale amax/448 for e4m3
rows.concept: Scaling for FP8: scale = amax/448 maps the tensor max to the top e4m3 magnitude, minimizing clipping
rows.method: FP8 post-training quant (W8A8-FP8, e4m3) for Hopper/Ada/Blackwell
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes scale=amax/448, casts x/scale to e4m3, and dequants. Compare the student's scale (exact within tol) and the quantized-dequantized output (max_abs_err) against the oracle.

rows.title: Pack b-bit codes into uint32 words (MLX layout)
rows.concept: MLX storage: 64 codes at 4 bits pack into 8 uint32 words in a defined nibble order; pack and unpack losslessly
rows.method: MLX affine group quantization (Apple silicon export)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle packs the codes into uint32 words per the documented order and unpacks them back. Compare the student's packed words bit-exactly and verify unpack recovers the original codes.

rows.title: Paged FP8 KV gather + dequant + attention
rows.concept: Compose paging with quantization: gather FP8 blocks via a block table, dequant per-head, and attend
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle de-references the block table to build the logical FP8 KV, dequants per head, and runs naive attention. Compare the student's gather+dequant+attention output against the oracle (including a partially filled last block).

rows.title: Partition ops: XNNPACK-delegatable vs portable fallback
rows.concept: Delegate partitioning: given the XNNPACK op-support set, tag each graph node as delegated or portable-fallback
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle labels each node using the provided delegate support table. Compare the student's per-node partition assignment exactly.

rows.title: Per-channel FP8 weight quant
rows.concept: Per-output-row FP8: each row gets scale = row_amax/448 before e4m3 cast, reducing error vs one global scale
rows.method: FP8 post-training quant (W8A8-FP8, e4m3) for Hopper/Ada/Blackwell
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-row scales, casts to e4m3, and dequants a real weight. Compare the student's per-channel scales and reconstruction within tolerance.

rows.title: Per-group asymmetric 4-bit quant (scale+zero)
rows.concept: The per-group affine quant GPTQ applies: scale=(max-min)/15, zero=round(-min/scale), 4-bit codes, dequant
rows.method: GPTQ post-training weight quant (W4A16, layer-wise inverse-Hessian)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-group scale/zero, codes, and dequant in numpy with group_size=128 on a real weight. Compare the student's codes exactly and the dequant (max_abs_err).

rows.title: Per-group min/max/scale/bias (group=64)
rows.concept: MLX affine params: per 64-element group, scale=(max-min)/(2^b-1), bias=min
rows.method: MLX affine group quantization (Apple silicon export)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-group min/max/scale/bias in numpy on a real weight row for group=64, b=4. Compare the student's scale and bias vectors within tolerance.

rows.title: Per-head KV scales
rows.concept: Finer granularity: a separate FP8 scale per KV head reduces error when heads have different ranges
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-head amax scales, quantizes each head's K,V to e4m3, dequants, and attends. Compare the student's output within tolerance against the per-head oracle.

rows.title: Per-tensor FP8 e4m3 KV quant + attention
rows.concept: FP8 KV cache: one scale per K and per V, cast to e4m3, dequant, then attend
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle scales K,V by amax/448, casts to e4m3, dequants, and runs naive attention in numpy. Compare the student's attention output against the FP8-KV oracle within tolerance.

rows.title: Per-tensor INT8 symmetric fake-quant with amax scaling
rows.concept: ModelOpt INT8 fake-quant: scale = amax/127, q = clamp(round(x/scale), -127, 127), dq = q*scale
rows.method: TensorRT-LLM engine build (+ NVIDIA ModelOpt quantization)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the symmetric per-tensor codes and dequant in numpy on a real weight tensor. Compare the student's int8 codes exactly and the dequantized tensor (max_abs_err) against the oracle.

rows.title: Per-tensor vs per-channel INT8: which halves the error?
rows.concept: Granularity tradeoff: per-tensor (single amax) vs per-output-channel (row amax) INT8 weight quant error
rows.method: TensorRT-LLM engine build (+ NVIDIA ModelOpt quantization)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes a real weight both ways and computes each reconstruction MSE plus the argmin winner. Compare the student's two errors (rel_err) and the reported lower-error scheme.

rows.title: Per-tensor vs per-head FP8 KV on an outlier head
rows.concept: Granularity payoff: attention error with one shared scale vs per-head scales when one head has large-range KV
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes both schemes' attention error and the argmin on an outlier-head fixture. Compare the student's error pair and the reported lower-error scheme.

rows.title: Per-token int8 dynamic activation quant
rows.concept: 8da4w activation half: per-row (per-token) symmetric int8 quant with scale = row_amax/127
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-row scales and int8 codes in numpy on real activations. Compare the student's per-token scales and codes exactly and dequant (max_abs_err).

rows.title: Pick layers to keep in fp16 by sensitivity
rows.concept: Skip-list selection: given per-layer FP8 KV error, keep the top-k highest-error layers in fp16
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle ranks layers by measured FP8-KV error and returns the top-k skip set. Compare the student's selected layer set exactly.

rows.title: Pick the eligible SDPA backend from constraints
rows.concept: SDPA dispatch: from head_dim, dtype, mask type, and causal flag, decide flash / mem-efficient / math eligibility
rows.method: Fused attention backend selection (SDPA / FlashAttention / FlexAttention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle applies the documented backend eligibility rules to each config and returns the selected backend. Compare the student's per-config backend choice exactly.

rows.title: Pick the max-autotune tile via wave-quantization cost
rows.concept: max-autotune config selection: model the wave-quantization/occupancy cost of candidate (BM,BN) tiles for a GEMM and choose the argmin
rows.method: Graph capture + JIT kernel codegen (torch.compile / TorchInductor)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes for each candidate tile CTAs = ceil(M/BM)*ceil(N/BN), waves = ceil(CTAs/num_SMs), and a padding-waste tiebreak, then returns the argmin config index for given (M,N,K,num_SMs). Compare the student's selected index and the full per-config cost vector.

rows.title: Propagate symbolic shapes and emit dim guards
rows.concept: Symbolic shape propagation: through reshape/view/cat/matmul compute output symbolic shapes and the divisibility/equality guards implied
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle applies shape-propagation rules to a graph with a dynamic dim s0, deriving the output shape expression and the guard set (e.g. s0 % 8 == 0, s0*s1 == numel). Compare the student's output-shape expression and guard set (as normalized strings/sets).

rows.title: Push the scale into the preceding LayerNorm params
rows.concept: Where the scale lives: fold diag(1/s) into the prior LayerNorm gamma/beta and diag(s) into the next Linear W, output unchanged
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle modifies LN weight/bias (divide by s) and the next-layer W (multiply by s), then runs LN->Linear on real fixtures. Compare the student's modified params and end-to-end output within tolerance against the unmodified reference.

rows.title: Q4_0 symmetric 4-bit (fp16 scale) matches ggml
rows.concept: GGUF Q4_0: 32-block, single FP16 scale d = absmax/-8, 4-bit codes stored as round(w/d)+8 clamped to 0..15
rows.method: GGUF k-quant export (llama.cpp) with importance matrix
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle ports the ggml Q4_0 quant/dequant (including the negative-divisor convention and FP16 scale) to numpy. Compare the student's codes exactly and dequant within FP16 tolerance.

rows.title: Q4_0 vs Q4_K vs imatrix-Q4_K error on a real row
rows.concept: Quality ladder: importance-weighted reconstruction error across a legacy 4-bit, a k-quant, and an imatrix k-quant
rows.method: GGUF k-quant export (llama.cpp) with importance matrix
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes the same real weight row three ways and computes each importance-weighted MSE plus the argmin. Compare the student's three errors and the reported best variant.

rows.title: Q4_1 asymmetric (scale+min) matches ggml
rows.concept: GGUF Q4_1: 32-block with FP16 scale d=(max-min)/15 and FP16 min m, codes = round((w-m)/d)
rows.method: GGUF k-quant export (llama.cpp) with importance matrix
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle ports the ggml Q4_1 formula (asymmetric with stored min) to numpy. Compare the student's scale, min, codes (exact) and dequant within FP16 tolerance.

rows.title: Q4_K super-block (256) two-level k-quant
rows.concept: Q4_K: 256-block split into 8 sub-blocks of 32, each with a 6-bit scale and 6-bit min, plus two FP16 super-block scales
rows.method: GGUF k-quant export (llama.cpp) with importance matrix
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle ports ggml dequantize_row_q4_K (w = d*q - dmin*m with 6-bit scale/min unpacking) to numpy. Compare the student's reconstruction within tolerance and the packed 4-bit codes exactly on real weight rows.

rows.title: Q6_K super-block reconstruction
rows.concept: Q6_K: 256-block with 16 int8 sub-scales times one FP16 super-scale and 6-bit quantized weights
rows.method: GGUF k-quant export (llama.cpp) with importance matrix
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle ports ggml dequantize_row_q6_K to numpy (6-bit quants, per-16 int8 scales, FP16 super-scale). Compare the student's reconstruction within tolerance and the 6-bit codes exactly.

rows.title: Q8_0 block quant/dequant matches ggml
rows.concept: GGUF Q8_0: 32-element blocks, one FP16 scale d = absmax/127, int8 codes
rows.method: GGUF k-quant export (llama.cpp) with importance matrix
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle implements the ggml Q8_0 formula in numpy with FP16 scale rounding. Compare the student's per-block scale and codes bit-exactly and the dequantized tensor within FP16 tolerance.

rows.title: QuantizedLinear matmul (per-group dequant) equals dense
rows.concept: Dequant-and-matmul: reconstruct grouped weights and multiply by activations, matching a dense reference within quant error
rows.method: MLX affine group quantization (Apple silicon export)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle dequantizes the grouped weight and does the matmul in numpy. Compare the student's QuantizedLinear-style output against the oracle within fp tolerance on real activations.

rows.title: Reconstruct dense from compressed values+metadata
rows.concept: Round-trip the sparse format: from packed 2-bit index metadata and the kept values, rebuild the dense weight
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle produces the compressed values+metadata from a real weight and the reference dense form. The student must scatter values back to positions from the indices; compare the reconstructed dense weight (max_abs_err) and positions (exact).

rows.title: Reconstruct dense weight from AffineQuantizedTensor fields
rows.concept: Subclass storage: given int_data (packed int4), per-group scale and zero_point, rebuild the dense dequantized weight
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle produces the AffineQuantizedTensor fields from a real weight and the reference dense dequant. The student must unpack int_data and apply scale/zero per group; compare the reconstructed dense weight within tolerance.

rows.title: Reference SDPA (scaled, causal mask)
rows.concept: The attention baseline: softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d) + mask) V with optional causal masking
rows.method: Fused attention backend selection (SDPA / FlashAttention / FlexAttention)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes naive scaled-dot-product attention in numpy on real Q,K,V. Compare the student's output within fp tolerance across causal and non-causal cases.

rows.title: Replay a CUDA-graph static-buffer capture correctly
rows.concept: reduce-overhead semantics: copy inputs into fixed static input buffers, replay into a fixed static output buffer that is overwritten on the next replay
rows.method: Graph capture + JIT kernel codegen (torch.compile / TorchInductor)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle models a captured graph: each call copies inputs into fixed buffers, computes, writes into one fixed output buffer, and returns a snapshot. Run a scripted sequence of N calls (with the aliasing pitfall where output must be copied out before the next replay). Compare the student's returned outputs for the whole call sequence.

rows.title: Run ONNX shape inference through dynamic axes
rows.concept: Symbolic shape inference: propagate dynamic axes through MatMul/Reshape/Concat/Gather to the output symbolic shapes
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle applies ONNX shape-inference rules to a small graph with named dynamic dims and produces each intermediate/output shape (with symbols). Compare the student's shape list (normalized) against the oracle.

rows.title: Search alpha to balance activation vs weight quant error
rows.concept: Alpha tuning: grid alpha and minimize max(activation-INT8-error, weight-INT8-error) after migration
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle grids alpha, applies migration, quantizes both operands to INT8, and computes the max of the two errors per alpha, returning the argmin. Compare the student's selected alpha index and the per-alpha error curve.

rows.title: Search the FP8 scale to minimize MSE (clip vs round)
rows.concept: Scale search: grid scales around amax/448 to trade clipping error against rounding error, picking the MSE argmin
rows.method: FP8 post-training quant (W8A8-FP8, e4m3) for Hopper/Ada/Blackwell
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle grids candidate scales, quantizes to e4m3 and dequants for each, computing per-scale MSE and the argmin. Compare the student's selected scale index and per-scale MSE curve.

rows.title: Search the per-channel weight clip ratio
rows.concept: AWQ's clip search: grid a max-clip ratio in [0.5,1.0] per group and pick the ratio minimizing quantization MSE
rows.method: AWQ activation-aware weight quant (W4A16, per-channel scale search)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle grids the clip ratios, clamps then quantizes, and computes per-ratio MSE to return the argmin. Compare the student's selected ratio index and per-ratio MSE curve against the oracle.

rows.title: Select the kept 2-of-4 per group (mask)
rows.concept: Semi-structured 2:4: keep the 2 largest-magnitude of every 4 consecutive weights
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle selects the top-2 of each group of 4 by |w| and builds the boolean mask. Compare the student's mask exactly on real weight rows.

rows.title: SparseGPT 2:4 mask via Hessian saliency + compensation
rows.concept: Prune well: choose which 2 to keep by minimal saliency w^2/[H^-1]_ii and compensate remaining weights via inverse-Hessian error
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs a reference SparseGPT 2:4 pass in numpy (build H from X, per-group saliency selection, error compensation). Compare the student's selected mask (exact) and compensated weights/layer-output within tolerance.

rows.title: Tag pointwise-fusible ops vs fusion barriers in an op chain
rows.concept: Recognize which ops TorchInductor can vertically fuse into one pointwise kernel (elementwise/broadcast) vs barriers (matmul, reduction, view-with-copy)
rows.method: Graph capture + JIT kernel codegen (torch.compile / TorchInductor)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle labels each op in a given fx-like op list as pointwise-fusible or barrier by op-type rules (add/mul/relu/sigmoid/broadcast=fusible; mm/bmm/conv/reduction/nonzero=barrier). Compare the student's per-op label vector element-wise.

rows.title: Two-level accumulation beats naive FP8 accumulation
rows.concept: Long-context fix: dequant FP8 per block to fp32 then accumulate, vs naive low-precision accumulation that regresses
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes the fp32 reference plus both accumulation strategies over a long context, and their errors. Compare the student's two-level result and error (rel_err) and confirm it beats the naive-accumulation error.

rows.title: Unpack the Q4_K 6-bit scales/mins blob
rows.concept: Bespoke bit-packing: the 12-byte Q4_K scales blob encodes 8 six-bit scales and 8 six-bit mins via ggml's get_scale_min_k4
rows.method: GGUF k-quant export (llama.cpp) with importance matrix
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle ports ggml's get_scale_min_k4 bit-unpacking to numpy. The student must reproduce the 8 scales and 8 mins from the packed 12 bytes; compare all 16 values exactly.

rows.title: Unpack two nibbles per byte and dequant
rows.concept: 4-bit storage: two NF4 codes packed per uint8 (high/low nibble); unpack, map to levels, multiply by absmax
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle packs the NF4 codes two-per-byte and the student must unpack the correct nibble order, map to levels, and dequant. Compare recovered codes (exact) and dequantized weight (max_abs_err).

rows.title: 8-bit vs 4-bit vs fp8 optimizer-state error ordering
rows.concept: Precision/memory tradeoff of low-bit optimizer states
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle returns reconstruction MSE and bytes for each of AdamW8bit/4bit/Fp8 on real gradient-derived state; grader checks the submission's three MSEs match the oracle and follow the oracle-observed error ordering.

rows.title: Activation memory: full store vs checkpoint-every-k
rows.method: Activation / gradient checkpointing (recompute instead of store)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes full = L*S*H and checkpointed = (L/k)*S*H stored boundaries plus one segment's recompute buffer; grader compares both peak figures for random (L,S,H,k).

rows.title: Activation memory with/without checkpoint+offload
rows.concept: Activation footprint of a transformer under checkpointing
rows.method: FSDP parameter/optimizer CPU offload + activation offload/checkpoint
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes stored-activation bytes = depth*seq*hidden*dtype for full store, sqrt-spaced boundaries for checkpoint, and ~0 GPU for activation-offload; grader compares the three peak figures for random (L,S,H).

rows.title: All-gather + unflatten back to original tensors
rows.concept: Reconstructing unsharded params from N shards
rows.method: FSDP parameter/optimizer CPU offload + activation offload/checkpoint
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle concatenates the N shards, strips padding, and splits/reshapes back to the original parameter shapes; grader checks every reconstructed parameter equals the original tensor to 1e-6.

rows.title: Allocate a KV bit budget across nbits_K, nbits_V, window
rows.concept: Choosing quant config to minimize total KV MSE under a byte budget
rows.method: KV-cache quantization (KIVI-style int2/int4, per-channel K / per-token V)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle enumerates feasible (nbits_K,nbits_V,R) under the byte budget, computes total reconstruction MSE for each, and returns the argmin config; grader checks the submission selects the same config (and matching MSE) for random tensors + budgets.

rows.title: Assign each layer to GPU/CPU/disk under a sequential device_map
rows.concept: device_map placement by greedy capacity fill
rows.method: Weight offloading for inference (big-model streaming to CPU/disk)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle fills GPU up to max_memory[gpu] with whole layers in order, then CPU up to its cap, then disk; grader compares the per-layer device assignment for random layer sizes + caps.

rows.title: Asymmetric int4 group quant/dequant of K (channel) and V (token)
rows.concept: Asymmetric scale+zero-point grouped quant along the KIVI axes
rows.method: KV-cache quantization (KIVI-style int2/int4, per-channel K / per-token V)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-group scale=(max-min)/(2^n-1), zp=round(-min/scale), q=clip(round(x/scale)+zp,0,2^n-1), dequant=(q-zp)*scale along the specified axis; grader checks max relative error of the submission's dequant vs oracle < 1e-6.

rows.title: Best-fit caching allocator with split + free-list reuse
rows.method: CUDA caching-allocator tuning (fragmentation control + memory profiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle rounds sizes, best-fits into the free list, splits remainders, returns freed blocks to the pool, and grows reserved on miss; grader replays a trace and compares reserved bytes and each allocation's success/OOM outcome.

rows.title: Block allocator with free list + logical->physical table
rows.concept: vLLM paged KV allocator over an append/free trace
rows.method: PagedAttention KV-cache block manager (+ swap/recompute preemption, prefix caching)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle is a reference allocator (block_size=16) with a LIFO free list; it replays an (append k tokens / free seq) trace and records physical-block count and freed-block reuse order; grader checks identical block ids assigned and peak physical blocks.

rows.title: Build the FlatParameter: flatten, pad, chunk into N shards
rows.method: FSDP parameter/optimizer CPU offload + activation offload/checkpoint
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle concatenates module params into a 1D buffer, pads to a multiple of N, splits into N equal shards, and records each shard's byte size and the padding count; grader compares shard sizes + padding to the oracle.

rows.title: Bytes-per-param -> optimizer variant
rows.concept: Identifying optimizer precision from its state footprint
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle maps state bytes/param (8 for fp32 m+v, 2 for 8-bit, 1 for 4-bit, 2 for fp8) to the variant label; grader compares the predicted labels for a set of footprints.

rows.title: CacheBlend non-prefix chunk reuse + boundary recompute
rows.concept: Reusing matching non-contiguous chunks, recomputing only selected boundary tokens
rows.method: Tiered KV-cache offload / reuse across requests (CPU/SSD/remote)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle matches chunks by content hash regardless of position, reuses their KV, and marks the small set of boundary/selective tokens to recompute at chunk seams; grader compares the reused-chunk set and the recompute-token set on crafted overlapping documents.

rows.title: Chained chunk hashing + store lookup (LMCache)
rows.method: Tiered KV-cache offload / reuse across requests (CPU/SSD/remote)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes hash_i = H(hash_{i-1} || chunk_i) per chunk and returns the set of reused chunk indices+positions found in the store; grader checks the reused chunk index/position set matches the oracle.

rows.title: checkpoint(segment) autograd: recompute + verify grads
rows.concept: Custom checkpoint Function, discard-then-recompute in backward
rows.method: Activation / gradient checkpointing (recompute instead of store)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs plain autograd for reference grads and computes the expected saved-tensor count for the segmentation; grader checks parameter grads match to 1e-5 and the saved-tensor count equals the oracle on a small MLP/block.

rows.title: Closed-form per-rank bytes incl. offload subtraction
rows.concept: ZeRO memory formula with CPU/NVMe offload target
rows.method: ZeRO optimizer/gradient/param offload to CPU & NVMe (ZeRO-Offload / ZeRO-Infinity)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle subtracts offloaded components (optimizer and/or params) from the on-GPU total and adds them to the off-device total per the offload target; grader compares both the on-GPU and off-device byte figures for random (Phi,N,stage,target).

rows.title: Communication volume per step: stage-2 vs stage-3
rows.concept: All-gather/reduce-scatter volume as multiples of Phi
rows.method: ZeRO optimizer/gradient/param offload to CPU & NVMe (ZeRO-Offload / ZeRO-Infinity)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-step comm volume per the ZeRO analysis (2*Phi for stage-1/2 reduce-scatter+all-gather, 3*Phi for stage-3 with the extra forward param all-gather); grader compares the volumes in units of Phi to the oracle.

rows.title: Copy-on-write block fork for beam/parallel sampling
rows.concept: COW ref-counted block sharing on sequence fork
rows.method: PagedAttention KV-cache block manager (+ swap/recompute preemption, prefix caching)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle forks a sequence sharing all full blocks (ref++), and on the next write to a shared partial block allocates a copy (ref--, new block); grader replays fork+append traces and checks total physical blocks and per-block ref counts match.

rows.title: CPU-offload vs disk-offload byte traffic per forward
rows.method: Weight offloading for inference (big-model streaming to CPU/disk)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle, given a layer->device placement, sums bytes read from CPU and from disk per forward pass (each non-GPU layer streamed once); grader compares the two totals to the oracle.

rows.title: CPU offload vs NVMe offload residency (ZeRO-Infinity)
rows.concept: Where each state lives for offload=cpu vs nvme
rows.method: ZeRO optimizer/gradient/param offload to CPU & NVMe (ZeRO-Offload / ZeRO-Infinity)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes on-GPU, CPU-resident, and NVMe-resident bytes for offload_optimizer=cpu vs offload_optimizer+param=nvme; grader compares the three-way byte split for both configs.

rows.title: CPU-offloaded Adam step equals single-device step
rows.concept: Correctness of grad->CPU, step on CPU, param->GPU
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs one on-device AdamW step; grader runs the submission's offloaded step (copy grad to CPU, update CPU-resident state+param, copy param back) and checks the updated param matches to 1e-6.

rows.title: Double-quantize the absmax scales (0.4 bits/param)
rows.concept: Second-level 8-bit quant of NF4 block scales
rows.method: NF4 4-bit weight storage for frozen base (QLoRA)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes bits/param for single-quant (4 + 32/bs) vs double-quant (4 + 8/bs + 32/(bs*256)) and the two-level dequant tensor; grader compares the bits/param figure and the end-to-end dequant error to the oracle.

rows.title: Dynamic-map vs linear int8 error on log-normal v-states
rows.concept: Error advantage of the dynamic map on heavy-tailed state
rows.method: Paged / 8-bit optimizers (spill optimizer state on memory spikes)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle returns MSE for both quantizers on sampled log-normal v; grader checks the submission's two MSEs match the oracle and that MSE(dynamic) < MSE(linear-int8) on the skewed input.

rows.title: Dynamic-map vs linear int8: which wins per input block
rows.concept: When non-linear 8-bit quant beats uniform on skewed state
rows.method: Paged / 8-bit optimizers (spill optimizer state on memory spikes)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes each block with both the dynamic map and linear int8, computes MSE for each, and labels the winner; grader compares the per-block winner labels on sampled Adam second-moment (v) blocks.

rows.title: Emit the async prefetch/evict resident set per step
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle produces, per decode step and per layer index, the resident-layer set after prefetch(next) and evict(current); grader checks per-step set equality and that peak resident layers == 2 over the whole generation.

rows.title: Enumerate the 256 dynamic-map levels from the bit budget
rows.concept: Deriving the representable value set of the dynamic map
rows.method: Paged / 8-bit optimizers (spill optimizer state on memory spikes)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle constructs the level array from the sign/exponent/fraction bit allocation (including the 0.0 entry) and sorts it; grader checks the submission's 256-level array matches the oracle to 1e-4.

rows.title: Fix a checkpoint that drops RNG state (dropout mismatch)
rows.concept: RNG save/restore so recompute reproduces the forward
rows.method: Activation / gradient checkpointing (recompute instead of store)
rows.how_to_grade: Supplied checkpoint recomputes with a fresh RNG so dropout masks differ and grads diverge. Oracle saves/restores RNG state; grader checks the fixed version reproduces autograd grads to 1e-5 on a dropout-containing block.

rows.title: Fix a global-absmax 8-bit optimizer quantizer -> blockwise
rows.concept: Blockwise scaling to survive local state spikes
rows.method: Paged / 8-bit optimizers (spill optimizer state on memory spikes)
rows.how_to_grade: Supplied code uses one global absmax; oracle uses per-block absmax; grader checks the fixed blockwise dequant matches the oracle rel-err < 1e-6 on state with a few localized spikes.

rows.title: Fix a hasher that hashes chunks independently (false hits)
rows.concept: Position/prefix-aware hashing to avoid mid-sequence false reuse
rows.method: Tiered KV-cache offload / reuse across requests (CPU/SSD/remote)
rows.how_to_grade: Supplied code hashes each chunk in isolation, so an identical chunk at a different position falsely hits. Oracle uses chained prefix hashing; grader checks the fixed code produces the correct no-false-hit reuse set on crafted traces.

rows.title: Fix a KIVI cache quantizing K per-token and dropping the residual
rows.concept: Correct axis assignment + fp16 residual window
rows.method: KV-cache quantization (KIVI-style int2/int4, per-channel K / per-token V)
rows.how_to_grade: Supplied code quantizes K per-token and keeps no residual window. Oracle computes correct per-channel-K + per-token-V with the last R tokens in fp16; grader checks the fixed dequant matches oracle rel-err < 1e-6 and that the residual-region error is exactly 0.

rows.title: Fix a symmetric-int4 global-scale codec -> NF4 blockwise
rows.concept: Replacing uniform int4 + global scale with NF4 quantile levels + blockwise absmax
rows.method: NF4 4-bit weight storage for frozen base (QLoRA)
rows.how_to_grade: Supplied codec uses uniform int4 levels and one global scale, giving high error on normal weights. Oracle uses NF4 quantile levels with blockwise absmax; grader checks the fixed codec's reconstruction error matches the NF4 oracle.

rows.title: Fix an off-by-one prefetch that evicts the layer still in use
rows.concept: Correct compute-before-evict ordering in the double buffer
rows.how_to_grade: A supplied scheduler evicts layer i before its attention is read (prefetches i+1 into i's slot too early). Oracle computes correct full-cache attention; grader checks the fixed scheduler reproduces every layer's attention output to 1e-6.

rows.title: Fix H2O accumulating attention without the causal mask
rows.concept: Correct causal masking before heavy-hitter ranking
rows.method: KV-cache eviction / compression (StreamingLLM sinks, H2O, SnapKV)
rows.how_to_grade: Supplied code sums the full (non-causal) attention, corrupting the ranking. Oracle applies the causal mask before accumulation; grader checks the fixed retained set matches the oracle.

rows.title: Fix tiled attention that skips accumulator rescaling
rows.concept: Stale-normalization bug when the running max updates
rows.how_to_grade: Supplied kernel updates m but does not rescale the accumulator/denominator, giving wrong output. Oracle computes full attention; grader checks the fixed kernel matches to 1e-6.

rows.title: Fix VAE tiling with no overlap (seam artifacts)
rows.concept: Adding overlap+blend to remove tile-border discontinuities
rows.method: Diffusion-model offloading (model/sequential/group offload, layerwise casting, slicing/tiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Supplied tiling stitches non-overlapping tiles, producing border discontinuities vs the untiled decode. Oracle uses overlap+blend; grader checks the fixed decode matches the untiled reference to tolerance.

rows.title: Fixed-budget KV memory and compression ratio
rows.method: KV-cache eviction / compression (StreamingLLM sinks, H2O, SnapKV)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes kept bytes = B*d*dtype vs full = T*d*dtype and the ratio; grader compares both for random (T,B,d).

rows.title: FlashAttention backward from stored logsumexp (no score matrix)
rows.concept: Recomputing softmax in backward to get dQ,dK,dV
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes analytic dQ,dK,dV; grader runs the submission's backward that recomputes P from Q,K and the stored row logsumexp and checks the three gradients to 1e-5.

rows.title: fp8 (e4m3) layerwise-casting store + bf16 compute
rows.concept: float8_e4m3fn storage cast with per-layer upcast
rows.method: Diffusion-model offloading (model/sequential/group offload, layerwise casting, slicing/tiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle implements e4m3 encode/decode (1-4-3 fields with bias and saturation rules), stores weights in fp8, upcasts to bf16 for a matmul, and reports reconstruction error + storage bytes; grader checks both against the oracle.

rows.title: Fragmentation OOM with vs without max_split_size cap
rows.concept: Effect of the split cap on reuse
rows.method: CUDA caching-allocator tuning (fragmentation control + memory profiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle replays the same trace with and without the split cap and reports whether each ends in OOM plus peak reserved; grader compares both outcomes.

rows.title: FSDP CPU offload vs ZeRO-3 CPU offload per-rank GPU bytes
rows.concept: Equivalence/differences of the two full-shard+offload schemes
rows.method: FSDP parameter/optimizer CPU offload + activation offload/checkpoint
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-rank on-GPU bytes for both schemes (both shard by N and offload sharded states, differing in transient buffers); grader compares the two figures and the reported difference for random (Phi,N).

rows.title: Gather logical KV from the block table and attend
rows.concept: Reconstructing a contiguous sequence view from scattered blocks
rows.method: PagedAttention KV-cache block manager (+ swap/recompute preemption, prefix caching)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle stores KV in shuffled physical blocks with a logical->physical table, gathers the logical order, and computes attention; grader checks the submission's gathered-attention output matches the contiguous-cache reference to 1e-6.

rows.title: GPU bytes freed: on-GPU AdamW vs CPUOffloadOptimizer
rows.concept: VRAM accounting for CPU-offloaded optimizer state/step
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes freed = optimizer-state bytes (K*Phi) plus, if offload_gradients, grad bytes (2*Phi) moved off-GPU; grader compares the freed-byte figure to the oracle for random Phi/dtype.

rows.title: GPU prefill tokens saved by prefix-chunk reuse
rows.concept: Reuse savings accounting over a multi-turn trace
rows.method: Tiered KV-cache offload / reuse across requests (CPU/SSD/remote)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle counts, per request, the length of the longest cached chunk-aligned prefix and sums saved tokens across the trace; grader compares total saved-token count to the oracle for random request sequences.

rows.title: Group-offload peak VRAM with prefetch
rows.concept: Two-group-resident peak vs sequential leaf vs model offload
rows.method: Diffusion-model offloading (model/sequential/group offload, layerwise casting, slicing/tiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes peak = 2*max_group (current + prefetched) for group offload vs 1*max_leaf for sequential vs full-module for model offload; grader compares the three peaks for random group partitions.

rows.title: H2D transfer bytes: offloaded dynamic vs offloaded_static over a generation
rows.concept: Comparing dynamic vs static offloaded-cache transfer volume
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle simulates both: dynamic re-stages grown KV each step, static uses a fixed max-len slab; it sums host<->device bytes over T decode steps for each; grader compares both totals for random (L,layer_bytes,T,max_len).

rows.title: H2O heavy-hitter accumulated-attention eviction set
rows.concept: Top-k by column-summed attention + recent window
rows.method: KV-cache eviction / compression (StreamingLLM sinks, H2O, SnapKV)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle accumulates column-summed causal attention scores, takes heavy hitters + recent window under the budget, and sums preserved attention mass; grader checks the retained index set and the preserved-mass figure on random attention matrices.

rows.title: Hit rate of a shared-prefix workload vs chunk size
rows.concept: Analytic reuse fraction from chunk size and prefix distribution
rows.method: Tiered KV-cache offload / reuse across requests (CPU/SSD/remote)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes expected reused fraction = mean over requests of floor(shared_prefix_len/chunk)*chunk divided by total tokens over a given prefix-length distribution; grader checks the submitted hit rate within 1e-6 of the oracle.

rows.title: How many GPU KV buffers a depth-K prefetch needs
rows.concept: Deriving the (K+1)-buffer requirement for depth-K lookahead
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes required_buffers = prefetch_depth + 1 (current plus K prefetched) for random prefetch depths and verifies its schedule is stall-free; grader compares the submitted buffer count and stall-free flag.

rows.title: Identify which eviction policy produced a retained set
rows.concept: Distinguishing sink+window vs heavy-hitter vs recent-only
rows.method: KV-cache eviction / compression (StreamingLLM sinks, H2O, SnapKV)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle generates retained sets from each policy for a token stream and, given a retained set, matches it to the producing policy; grader compares the predicted policy labels.

rows.title: infer_auto_device_map greedy allocator with no-split blocks
rows.concept: Balanced/sequential device map respecting no-split module boundaries
rows.method: Weight offloading for inference (big-model streaming to CPU/disk)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle greedily packs modules (keeping no-split groups whole) into devices by max_memory in order; grader checks the produced {module: device} map equals the oracle for random module trees + budgets.

rows.title: int2 V with an exact fp16 residual window
rows.concept: Residual window guarantees recent-token exactness under aggressive quant
rows.method: KV-cache quantization (KIVI-style int2/int4, per-channel K / per-token V)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle int2-quantizes V outside the last R tokens and keeps the last R in fp16; grader checks reconstruction max-abs error on the residual region == 0 and on the quantized region matches the int2 group-quant oracle.

rows.title: knorm press: evict lowest key-norm tokens
rows.method: KV-cache eviction / compression (StreamingLLM sinks, H2O, SnapKV)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle keeps the top-B tokens by ||k||_2 and evicts the rest; grader checks the retained index set on random key tensors.

rows.title: Label each request's chunks hit vs miss against the KV store
rows.method: Tiered KV-cache offload / reuse across requests (CPU/SSD/remote)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle splits each request's token ids into CHUNK_SIZE chunks, computes chained prefix hashes, and marks a chunk a hit iff its prefix hash is present in a prepopulated store; grader compares the per-chunk hit/miss vector.

rows.title: Label which KV layers are GPU-resident at each decode step
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle simulates the offloaded-cache schedule over L layers x T decode steps: while attending at layer i the resident set is {i, (i+1) mod L}; it emits a GPU/CPU label per (layer,step). Grader compares the submitted label matrix elementwise for random (L,T).

rows.title: LRU CPU/SSD tiering under a CPU capacity cap
rows.concept: Tiered eviction to maximize reuse under MAX_LOCAL_CPU_SIZE
rows.method: Tiered KV-cache offload / reuse across requests (CPU/SSD/remote)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs LRU over the access trace with the CPU byte cap (evicted chunks spill to the SSD tier), then reports which chunks are CPU-resident at the end and total GPU-token savings; grader compares the resident set and savings figure.

rows.title: Mark each KV block full vs partially-filled
rows.method: PagedAttention KV-cache block manager (+ swap/recompute preemption, prefix caching)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle, given per-sequence lengths and block_size, labels each allocated block full or last-partial (slots used = len mod block_size, 0 meaning full); grader compares the per-block full/partial labels.

rows.title: Mark stored vs recomputed activations for a segmentation
rows.concept: Reading which activations a checkpoint boundary keeps
rows.method: Activation / gradient checkpointing (recompute instead of store)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle, given segment boundaries, labels boundary activations as stored and interior ones as recomputed; grader compares the per-activation store/recompute labels for random segmentations.

rows.title: Max concurrent sequences that fit in the block pool
rows.concept: Capacity planning from total blocks and length distribution
rows.method: PagedAttention KV-cache block manager (+ swap/recompute preemption, prefix caching)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes blocks_per_seq = ceil(len/bs) and greedily admits sequences until total_blocks is exhausted, returning the admitted count; grader compares the count for random length vectors + pool sizes.

rows.title: Memory of int4 KV + fp16 residual window vs full fp16 cache
rows.concept: KV quantization memory accounting incl. residual window and scales
rows.method: KV-cache quantization (KIVI-style int2/int4, per-channel K / per-token V)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes quantized bytes = (nbits/8)*(T-R)*d + 2*R*d + per-group (scale,zero-point) bytes, and full = 2*T*d; grader compares total bytes and the compression ratio for random (T,d,nbits,R,group_size).

rows.title: Memory vs recompute for checkpoint-every-k, k in {1,2,4}
rows.method: Activation / gradient checkpointing (recompute instead of store)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes stored-activation bytes and extra forward-layer count for each k; grader checks the submission reproduces both curves (per-k pairs) exactly.

rows.title: Minimum GPU memory to run a streamed model
rows.concept: Lower bound = largest resident window + working buffers
rows.method: Weight offloading for inference (big-model streaming to CPU/disk)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes min_gpu = max over positions of the K-layer window sum plus a fixed activation buffer; grader compares the submitted minimum to the oracle over random layer vectors and K.

rows.title: Naive vs online softmax numerical stability on large logits
rows.concept: Why the max-subtraction (safe softmax) is needed
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes attention in high precision as reference; grader checks the online-softmax output matches while the naive no-max version overflows/deviates on large-magnitude logits.

rows.title: NF4 blockwise codec (levels from N(0,1) quantiles)
rows.method: NF4 4-bit weight storage for frozen base (QLoRA)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle derives the 16 NF4 levels from equal-mass normal quantiles, does blocksize-64 absmax scaling + nearest-level + 4-bit packing; grader checks per-element dequant to tolerance and that packed size == ceil(n/2) + scale bytes.

rows.title: NF4 storage bytes and effective bits/param
rows.method: NF4 4-bit weight storage for frozen base (QLoRA)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes bytes = ceil(n/2) 4-bit codes + (n/blocksize)*scale_bytes and bits/param = 4 + scalebits/blocksize; grader compares both to the oracle for random (n,blocksize,scale dtype).

rows.title: NF4 vs FP4 vs int4-affine reconstruction error
rows.concept: Error ordering of 4-bit grids on real weights
rows.method: NF4 4-bit weight storage for frozen base (QLoRA)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle returns per-grid MSE on normally-distributed weights; grader checks the submission's three MSEs match the oracle and follow MSE(NF4) < MSE(FP4) < MSE(int4-affine).

rows.title: NF4 vs FP4 vs int4: which grid fits normal weights best
rows.concept: Choosing the 4-bit grid for normally-distributed weights
rows.method: NF4 4-bit weight storage for frozen base (QLoRA)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle quantizes N(0,1) weights with each grid, computes MSE, and labels the lowest-error grid (NF4); grader compares the predicted label.

rows.title: Online softmax for one query over streamed K/V blocks
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes full softmax attention for the query; grader runs the submission's streaming online-softmax (running m,l,acc with exp(m_old-m_new) rescale) over K/V blocks and checks the output to 1e-6.

rows.title: Optimal asymmetric scale/zero-point minimizing max-abs error
rows.concept: Deriving the min-max affine mapping for a quant group
rows.method: KV-cache quantization (KIVI-style int2/int4, per-channel K / per-token V)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle derives scale/zp from the group min,max and reports the resulting worst-case abs error (<= scale/2); grader compares the submission's scale, zero-point, and max-abs reconstruction error to the oracle per group.

rows.title: Optimal checkpoint placement (revolve DP)
rows.method: Activation / gradient checkpointing (recompute instead of store)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle is a reference DP computing minimal extra forward-layer count for (L,C); grader checks the submission's recompute total equals the DP optimum across random (L,C).

rows.title: Optimizer memory: Adam fp32 vs 8-bit blockwise vs paged
rows.concept: 8-bit optimizer-state memory incl. per-block absmax overhead
rows.method: Paged / 8-bit optimizers (spill optimizer state on memory spikes)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes fp32 = 8*Phi (m+v), 8-bit = 2*Phi + 2*(Phi/blocksize)*4 absmax bytes, paged adds no steady bytes; grader compares the byte figures for random Phi and block sizes.

rows.title: Peak attention memory: naive O(N^2) vs flash O(N)
rows.concept: Attention memory scaling with sequence length
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes naive = heads*N*N*dtype (score matrix) vs flash = heads*N*d + O(block) and their ratio; grader compares both figures for random (N,heads,d).

rows.title: Peak GPU bytes + total H2D transfer for a K-layer window
rows.concept: Weight-streaming peak memory and PCIe traffic
rows.method: Weight offloading for inference (big-model streaming to CPU/disk)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle slides a K-layer residency window over the layer-size vector: peak = max sum of any K consecutive layers, transfer = sum of all layer sizes loaded per forward; grader compares both numbers to the oracle across random layer arrays and window sizes.

rows.title: Peak KV bytes: offloaded double-buffer vs on-device full cache
rows.concept: KV memory accounting for 2-layer residency vs L-layer residency
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-layer KV bytes = 2*batch*heads*seq*head_dim*dtype_bytes, peak_offloaded = 2*layer_bytes, peak_full = L*layer_bytes; grader compares both byte figures and their ratio to the oracle for random (L,batch,heads,seq,head_dim,dtype).

rows.title: Peak VRAM: full-resident vs model vs sequential offload
rows.method: Diffusion-model offloading (model/sequential/group offload, layerwise casting, slicing/tiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes peak = sum(all components) for full, largest component + working buffer for sequential leaf, and largest component + text buffer for model offload; grader compares the peaks and their ordering.

rows.title: Per-channel-K beats per-token-K on outlier channels
rows.concept: Why K is quantized per-channel in KIVI
rows.method: KV-cache quantization (KIVI-style int2/int4, per-channel K / per-token V)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle group-quantizes K along channel and along token and returns both MSEs; grader checks the submission's two MSEs match the oracle and that MSE(per-channel) < MSE(per-token) on inputs with a few high-variance channels.

rows.title: Per-GPU bytes for params+grads+optimizer given (Phi,N,stage)
rows.method: ZeRO optimizer/gradient/param offload to CPU & NVMe (ZeRO-Offload / ZeRO-Infinity)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle uses 2*Phi (fp16 params) + 2*Phi (fp16 grads) + 12*Phi (Adam fp32 master+m+v) with each component divided by N when its stage sharding applies; grader compares per-GPU bytes to the oracle for random (Phi,N,stage).

rows.title: Per-rank flat partition of Phi across N ranks
rows.concept: Even+remainder partitioning of the parameter count
rows.method: ZeRO optimizer/gradient/param offload to CPU & NVMe (ZeRO-Offload / ZeRO-Infinity)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle assigns floor(Phi/N) params to each rank and distributes the Phi mod N remainder to the first ranks, returning each rank's owned param/grad/opt bytes; grader compares the per-rank byte vector.

rows.title: Per-rank peak memory of full-shard with/without cpu_offload
rows.method: FSDP parameter/optimizer CPU offload + activation offload/checkpoint
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes per-rank = (params+grads+opt)/N plus a transient all-gather buffer of the largest layer; with cpu_offload the sharded states move off-GPU leaving only the transient buffer; grader compares peak bytes for both.

rows.title: Pick the KIVI quant axis for K and for V
rows.concept: Per-channel K vs per-token V axis choice under channel-localized outliers
rows.method: KV-cache quantization (KIVI-style int2/int4, per-channel K / per-token V)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle, for each of K and V, computes group-quant MSE along both axes and labels the lower-MSE axis; on tensors with channel-localized outliers this yields K->channel, V->token. Grader compares the two axis labels.

rows.title: Pick the minimal knob set that fits the memory budget
rows.method: FSDP parameter/optimizer CPU offload + activation offload/checkpoint
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle evaluates peak memory for each subset of the three knobs in increasing-overhead order and returns the first that fits the budget; grader checks the selected knob set equals the oracle for random budgets and model sizes.

rows.title: Prefix-cache block hashing and cross-sequence sharing
rows.concept: Copy-on-write prefix sharing via block-aligned prefix hashes
rows.method: PagedAttention KV-cache block manager (+ swap/recompute preemption, prefix caching)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle hashes each block-aligned prefix (chained hash of token ids up to that block), shares physical blocks across sequences with equal prefix hashes, and counts blocks saved; grader checks the shared-block set and blocks-saved count on random prompt sets.

rows.title: Prove offloaded-cache decode is bit-lossless vs full cache
rows.concept: Losslessness of KV offloading (values unchanged, only location moves)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes each decode-step attention output using the full on-device KV; grader runs the submission's offloaded gather-from-CPU path on the same toy K/V tensors and checks max|out_offload - out_full| < 1e-6 across all steps and layers.

rows.title: QLoRA forward: dequant NF4 base + LoRA delta
rows.concept: NF4 dequant to bf16 plus low-rank adapter output
rows.method: NF4 4-bit weight storage for frozen base (QLoRA)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle dequantizes the NF4 base to bf16, adds the LoRA B@A delta, and computes the linear output; grader checks the submission's output matches within the expected NF4-quant error band of the fp16-base+LoRA reference.

rows.title: Reconstruct create_dynamic_map and quantize Adam v blockwise
rows.method: Paged / 8-bit optimizers (spill optimizer state on memory spikes)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle builds the 256-entry dynamic map and does per-block absmax normalize -> nearest-map-code -> dequant; grader checks the submission's dequantized v matches the oracle to rel-err < 1e-6 on Adam v-states.

rows.title: Reconstruct the 16 NF4 level values
rows.concept: Deriving the asymmetric NF4 grid with a forced exact zero
rows.method: NF4 4-bit weight storage for frozen base (QLoRA)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle builds the NF4 levels as normal quantiles normalized to [-1,1] with the 0.0 entry forced exact; grader checks the submission's 16 levels match the published grid to 1e-4.

rows.title: Recover peak reserved/allocated from a memory snapshot
rows.method: CUDA caching-allocator tuning (fragmentation control + memory profiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle builds a snapshot (segments/blocks with alloc events) and computes peak reserved, peak allocated, and the largest single allocation; grader checks the submission recovers all three from the snapshot structure.

rows.title: Reserved-vs-allocated fragmentation gap after a trace
rows.method: CUDA caching-allocator tuning (fragmentation control + memory profiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle replays the alloc/free trace through a reference caching allocator and reports reserved - allocated bytes at peak; grader compares the gap for random traces.

rows.title: Simulate paged optimizer eviction under a spike (no OOM)
rows.concept: Unified-memory paging of optimizer state at the OOM moment
rows.method: Paged / 8-bit optimizers (spill optimizer state on memory spikes)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle replays an allocation trace with a memory spike, evicting LRU optimizer-state pages to CPU when the GPU budget is exceeded and faulting them back on access; grader compares the page-fault count and the evicted-page set, and asserts no allocation fails.

rows.title: Size rounding + small/large pool selection
rows.concept: Allocation-size rounding and the 1MB pool threshold
rows.method: CUDA caching-allocator tuning (fragmentation control + memory profiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle rounds requests (512B multiples, block rounding) and routes <1MB to the small pool else the large pool, then reports segment sizes; grader compares the routed pool and segment sizes.

rows.title: Sliced attention matching full attention
rows.concept: Query/head-chunked attention to bound score-matrix memory
rows.method: Diffusion-model offloading (model/sequential/group offload, layerwise casting, slicing/tiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes full attention; grader runs the submission's sliced attention (chunks over heads/query, concatenated), checks equality to 1e-6, and compares the reported peak score-matrix bytes to the oracle.

rows.title: Smallest stage+offload target that fits a target model
rows.concept: Choosing the minimal-overhead ZeRO config that fits
rows.method: ZeRO optimizer/gradient/param offload to CPU & NVMe (ZeRO-Offload / ZeRO-Infinity)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle evaluates per-GPU bytes for each (stage, offload) in increasing-overhead order and returns the first that fits the aggregate memory; grader checks the selected config equals the oracle for random (Phi,N,memory).

rows.title: SnapKV observation-window pooled-vote selection
rows.concept: Pooled top-k voting from the end-of-prompt observation window
rows.method: KV-cache eviction / compression (StreamingLLM sinks, H2O, SnapKV)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle aggregates observation-window attention, average-pools with a fixed kernel, and takes the top-k prefill positions; grader checks the selected index set and compression ratio on random attention tensors.

rows.title: Split to minimize disk-resident bytes under max_memory
rows.method: Weight offloading for inference (big-model streaming to CPU/disk)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle finds the assignment that fills GPU then CPU to their caps with whole no-split blocks, minimizing disk bytes; grader checks the submission's disk-byte total equals the oracle optimum for random layer arrays + caps.

rows.title: Splittable vs oversized free blocks under max_split_size
rows.method: CUDA caching-allocator tuning (fragmentation control + memory profiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle labels each free block splittable iff its size <= max_split_size_mb and the remainder would be usable; grader compares the per-block labels.

rows.title: sqrt(L) segment size and its memory/recompute cost
rows.concept: The sqrt-memory optimum for uniform layers
rows.method: Activation / gradient checkpointing (recompute instead of store)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes optimal segment = round(sqrt(L)), stored ~= 2*sqrt(L) activations, extra forward = one full pass; grader compares the segment size, stored count, and recompute count to the oracle.

rows.title: Streamed-layer forward equals full-resident forward
rows.method: Weight offloading for inference (big-model streaming to CPU/disk)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle runs a small MLP fully resident; grader runs the submission's layer-by-layer stream (load layer, compute, free) on the same input and checks the output matches to 1e-6.

rows.title: StreamingLLM sink+window set + rolling position ids
rows.concept: Attention-sink + sliding-window retained set with remapped positions
rows.method: KV-cache eviction / compression (StreamingLLM sinks, H2O, SnapKV)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes {first S sinks} union {last W tokens} and the shifted (rolling) position ids; grader checks the retained index set, remapped positions, and that in-window attention over the kept set matches full attention to tolerance.

rows.title: StreamingLLM vs H2O retention of a mid-context needle
rows.concept: When window-based eviction drops a needed token that H2O keeps
rows.method: KV-cache eviction / compression (StreamingLLM sinks, H2O, SnapKV)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes both retained sets for a stream containing a high-attention needle outside the recent window and reports whether each keeps it plus the needle's retained attention mass; grader compares both.

rows.title: Swap vs recompute preemption accounting
rows.concept: Cost model for the two vLLM preemption modes
rows.method: PagedAttention KV-cache block manager (+ swap/recompute preemption, prefix caching)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle, on a preemption event for a victim sequence, computes swap cost = KV bytes copied to CPU and back, and recompute cost = tokens re-prefilled (= sequence length); grader compares both figures for random victim lengths and block sizes.

rows.title: The online-softmax correction factor, block by block
rows.concept: Deriving exp(m_old - m_new) rescaling for exact partial sums
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle emits the running (m,l,acc) after each block for a reference sequence; grader checks the submission's per-block partial output equals the oracle's, proving equivalence to one-pass softmax.

rows.title: Tiled FlashAttention forward with causal mask
rows.concept: Block-over-Q/K tiled attention with running normalization
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes full causal attention; grader runs the submission's tiled kernel (Q/K blocks, per-block m/l update, causal masking) and checks the full output matrix to 1e-6.

rows.title: torchao 4-bit AdamW state + one step
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle de/quantizes m,v with the 4-bit blockwise scheme and applies one AdamW step; grader checks the dequant error and the one-step updated param match the oracle within tolerance.

rows.title: torchao 8-bit AdamW state (blockwise) + one step
rows.concept: 8-bit blockwise optimizer state with de/quant around the step
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle keeps m,v in 8-bit blockwise codes, dequantizes, runs the AdamW update, requantizes, and reports the updated param over K steps; grader checks the param trajectory matches within the rel-err band of fp32 AdamW.

rows.title: Unsloth offloaded-checkpoint context multiplier
rows.concept: Offloading checkpointed hidden states to CPU for near-zero GPU activation
rows.method: Activation / gradient checkpointing (recompute instead of store)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes GPU activation bytes for standard checkpoint vs offloaded (boundary hidden states moved to CPU) and the resulting max-context multiplier at a fixed GPU budget; grader checks the multiplier within tolerance.

rows.title: VAE slicing (batch split) vs tiling (spatial split) peak memory
rows.concept: Two axes of VAE-decode memory reduction
rows.method: Diffusion-model offloading (model/sequential/group offload, layerwise casting, slicing/tiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes peak activation for slicing (one image at a time) vs tiling (one spatial tile at a time) for a batch of large images and reports which is lower; grader compares both peaks.

rows.title: VAE tiled decode with overlap blending
rows.concept: Overlapping-tile decode to cut VAE peak activation
rows.method: Diffusion-model offloading (model/sequential/group offload, layerwise casting, slicing/tiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle decodes a latent with a toy conv decoder untiled; grader runs the submission's overlapping-tile decode with linear-ramp blending and checks the reconstructed image to tolerance (seam-free).

rows.title: VRAM reduction % from moving optimizer state+step to CPU
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes reduction = offloaded_bytes / total_training_bytes for the given model+dtype (params+grads+opt); grader checks the submitted percentage matches the oracle within tolerance.

rows.title: Wasted slots + physical blocks: paged vs contiguous pre-alloc
rows.method: PagedAttention KV-cache block manager (+ swap/recompute preemption, prefix caching)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle computes paged blocks = sum(ceil(len_i/bs)), wasted = blocks*bs - sum(len_i), and contiguous reserve = n_seq*ceil(max_len/bs)*bs; grader compares the block count and wasted-slot count to the oracle for random length vectors.

rows.title: What lives on GPU vs CPU in forward vs backward under FSDP flags
rows.method: FSDP parameter/optimizer CPU offload + activation offload/checkpoint
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle maps (cpu_offload, activation_checkpoint, activation_offload) flags to which of {shard, gathered full param, activations} are GPU-resident during forward and backward; grader compares the phase-by-phase residency labels.

rows.title: Which attention backend materializes the full score matrix
rows.concept: Classifying attention implementations by memory behavior
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle labels {naive, math-SDPA, mem-efficient, flash} by whether each forms the O(N^2) score matrix; grader compares the predicted labels.

rows.title: Which component is GPU-resident per pipeline stage and mode
rows.concept: model vs sequential vs group offload residency
rows.method: Diffusion-model offloading (model/sequential/group offload, layerwise casting, slicing/tiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle maps each offload mode to the set of components (text encoder / denoiser / VAE) on GPU during the encode/denoise/decode stages; grader compares the residency labels.

rows.title: Which of params/grads/optimizer are sharded at each ZeRO stage
rows.method: ZeRO optimizer/gradient/param offload to CPU & NVMe (ZeRO-Offload / ZeRO-Infinity)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle maps stage 0->none, 1->optimizer, 2->optimizer+grads, 3->optimizer+grads+params to boolean flags; grader compares the three flags per stage.

rows.title: Why expandable_segments avoids a fragmentation OOM
rows.concept: Coalescing virtual segments to eliminate external fragmentation
rows.method: CUDA caching-allocator tuning (fragmentation control + memory profiling)
rows.how_to_grade: Oracle replays a fragmenting trace under fixed segments (OOMs) and under expandable segments (coalesces, fits) and reports the OOM flag and peak reserved for each; grader compares both.

rows.title: act-order column permutation
rows.concept: Quantize columns by descending diag(H) to spend error budget on important columns
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture layer + H. Learner returns the act-order permutation (argsort of diag(H) desc) and the resulting output MSE. Oracle computes the same permutation and runs GPTQ in that order; permutation exact_match and MSE within 1e-6 and <= natural-order MSE; gate. numpy deterministic.

rows.title: Activation calibration scale (moving absmax)
rows.concept: Momentum-updated per-tensor activation scale across calibration batches
rows.how_to_grade: Fixture stream of batches + momentum m. Learner returns the final calibrated per-tensor scale. Oracle runs the same running absmax with momentum m; rel_err < 1e-6; gate. numpy deterministic.

rows.title: Apply a per-channel scale and quantize
rows.concept: W' = W*s, X' = X/s keeps X@W invariant while shrinking salient-weight range before int4
